title: Politicians, private jets and power - the life of a Fifa president
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino appears to be trying to return to business as usual after the failed World Cup private investment plan - but it may not be that easy.
fullText:
Gianni Infantino stepped off a plane in Cali and was greeted on the runway by the president of the Colombian Football Federation.

Ramon Jesurun, a close ally of Infantino's, saw it as a chance to show his support, with the two men smiling in a photo opportunity for the federation's Instagram account.

Infantino had not travelled to Colombia for any run-of-the-mill meeting on Friday. He would attend the inauguration of the country's new president Abelardo de la Espriella.

Infantino was accompanied by Alejandro Dominguez, the president of South America's football governing body Conmebol.

This is the life of a Fifa president.

It involves building ties with some of the most powerful people in the world, shown by Infantino's relationship with US President Donald Trump.

Before the biggest scandal to hit his tenure - the aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise plan - Infantino was an incredibly powerful figure who appeared bulletproof.

Now, after an apology and stated desire to withstand the backlash of his plan to sell a stake in the men's World Cup to private equity firms, Infantino appears to be trying to return to business as usual.

Uefa's threat to boycott Fifa tournaments still stands. That will be tested with the Fifa Under-20 World Cup set to kick off in Poland in 29 days.

Perhaps emboldened by the support he has received from outside Europe in recent days, Infantino is not going to stand down easily.

But what exactly is the role of the Fifa president?

A cavalcade of blacked out Mercedes, flanked by police cars, rolled into the Fifa headquarters in Rabat, Morocco, earlier this week.

Infantino had summoned a select few members of the Fifa management board to discuss his plan to sell off 21% of the commercial and ticketing business to a private equity firm.

This is how the Swiss-Italian travels - in between flights on the Qatar Airways Executive jet which has been made available to him. The plane enabled him to take up to three flights a day, watching two games, throughout the 2026 World Cup.

That type of arrival does look presidential - only more like a president of a country than a sports body.

It enables him to travel the globe, visiting Fifa's official offices like Rabat, where he was based over the past week as the Fifa Forward Enterprise controversy developed.

In his role Infantino is expected to visit the 211 member nations, to see the grassroots projects Fifa has funded.

Part of his remit is to unify football, which cannot be achieved from within the Fifa headquarters in Zurich.

It requires international travel to attend confederation meetings, and the global tournaments Fifa organises. Infantino needs to build relationships with officials and politicians.

In April, before the Fifa Congress in Vancouver, local authorities rejected a request for a level-four motorcade, usually reserved for heads of state or the Pope.

New Zealand police said they had declined a similar request during the 2023 Women's World Cup.

Alongside the cavalcade of cars and the private charter flights comes a large salary, too, three times what he first earned when elected in 2016.

Infantino, who was paid about £1.3m 10 years ago, now takes home about £4m - a base salary of £2.2m plus a confirmed variable bonus payment of £1.8m.

His predecessor Sepp Blatter was paid a £2.6m package for his final year as Fifa president.

Infantino gets a 'per diem' too to cover expenses and living costs, worth £20,500 a year on top of his salary.

As the head of the most popular sport in the world, it should be expected that there is a wage to match.

Infantino would argue that by driving record revenues and funding for member associations, he has proven he is worth the salary.

Infantino's alliance with Trump seemed to have elevated his status even further.

Many in world football felt that this began to come at the expense of his responsibilities in football.

In May 2025, Infantino had been on a diplomatic tour of the Middle East with Trump and turned up two hours late for the Fifa Congress in Paraguay.

Uefa accused Infantino of prioritising "private political interests" and staged a walk-out.

There was also the Fifa Peace Prize, awarded to Trump weeks before the US invaded Venezuela to depose president Nicolas Maduro and launched air attacks on Iran.

Despite criticism, the Fifa ethics committee did not respond to complaints about Infantino's political neutrality over the prize.

At the start of the year, Infantino made a surprise appearance at the inaugural meeting of Trump's Board of Peace, set up to oversee the reconstruction of Gaza.

The International Olympic Committee, of which Infantino is an invited member, said its rules on political neutrality had not been breached.

However, many felt he had positioned himself too close to the US president.

This was heightened when USA striker Folarin Balogun escaped a ban after being sent off at the World Cup.

It was an unprecedented move by Fifa's disciplinary committee, with Trump saying he had personally called Infantino asking for the red card to be reviewed.

Infantino insisted it was a decision taken by an independent body over which no-one could have an influence.

On the final weekend of the World Cup, Trump and Infantino appeared together at Trump Tower in New York. The US president said he had called the Fifa president who "made another great decision".

Then, perhaps the culmination of Infantino's close association with Trump, came Fifa Forward Enterprise.

The private investor was to be a company linked to the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support

Uefa boycott right thing for future of game - Bronze

If Infantino goes, who might replace him as Fifa president?

Independent questions of Infantino's methods and decisions are rare because he does not often speak to the media.

In the past four years he has given just two news conferences, both lasting an hour and held before the start of the World Cup.

Other than that, Infantino generally appears in Fifa-produced interviews issued through their official channels.

Before the 2026 World Cup, Infantino tried to head off at the pass any queries about high ticket prices and supporters' visas.

But, at the news conference before the World Cup, his reply of "just, you know, chill, relax" about Somali referee Omar Artan, who had been denied entry to the USA at Miami Airport, sparked concern.

The Fifa statement issued on Wednesday offered some contrition. But there was a rebuke, too.

It gave Infantino the chance to bite back, saying Fifa would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process".

The allure of the role is great, underscored by the fact there have been just four permanent Fifa presidents since Stanley Rous was elected in 1961.

Outside of Europe, the record revenues achieved by Infantino have funded the football operations of many countries. That has created loyalty, and it is a vote winner.

Yet for Uefa, and a few other national associations, the rap sheet is now too long.

Fifa cannot be run as an autocratic project any longer, claim his critics - many of them within European football.

Expanding the World Cup was in Infantino's election manifesto, and an increase to 64 teams for 2030 seems highly likely if he gets a fourth term.

There was also the expanded summer Club World Cup. The trophy is engraved with a personal tribute - "Inspired by the Fifa president Gianni Infantino".

The unique allocation of the next two men's World Cups helped ensure Saudi Arabia, another close ally of Infantino, would get the 2034 event.

The draw for this summer's World Cup was a long, lavish and outlandish affair. Trump was front and centre, as was Infantino.

Many supporters felt the price of tickets was too high, while some who were prepared to pay for them were denied visas.

Fifa opted to use a secondary market place with uncapped prices and a 30% share on each ticket sold.

Critics said profit had become more important than the supporter experience, with the attorneys general of New York and New Jersey subpoenaing Fifa to answer questions about its ticketing practices.

Even with all these controversies, Infantino was expected to be re-elected, such was his support around the world in many member associations.

Indeed, before the World Cup 111 had already declared for him - enough to guarantee re-election.

Now that picture is uncertain amid the fallout from Fifa's failed private investment plan.

Uefa sees this moment as its chance to force him to step down.

But, as his attendance at the Colombia president's inauguration shows, that may be incredibly difficult to achieve.

title: If You Loved 'Futurama,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next
description: If ‘Futurama’ is your love language, there’s one movie you are almost guaranteed to love.
fullText:
Futurama has been one of the smartest and funniest TV shows for so long, it’s managed to get canceled and brought back several times. It’s easy to see why: Every single episode is jam-packed with jokes, and those jokes range from the incredibly stupid to jokes based on science that about four people in the world understand (and they all work in the Futurama writer’s room, apparently). Its bent vision of the future of the universe is always a delightfully deranged adventure, and if you’re looking to bring a little more of that vibe into your life (and you’ve already binged the hilarious TV shows in that category), you should absolutely watch Idiocracy immediately.

Idiocracy and Futurama share a fundamental premise: A man of average intelligence is frozen, wakes up in the far future, and has adventures. In Futurama, Philip J. Fry (Billy West) fits right in with the ludicrous sci-fi universe he finds himself in; but in Idiocracy, Soldier Joe Bauers (Luke Wilson) emerges from hibernation five centuries later to discover that humanity has regressed so drastically he is now the smartest man on Earth—by a long shot. And if you’re thinking that Futurama played around very specifically with that premise, you’d be right—in season 3, episode 7, “The Day the Earth Stood Stupid,” floating alien brains use a beam of energy to turn humanity stupid—but the beam doesn’t affect Fry, because—stay with me here—he is his own grandfather and thus lacks a crucial “delta wave” in his brain function, leaving him briefly the smartest human on the planet.

Idiocracy is more a tightly focused satire than Futurama, using its premise to mock modern problems and behaviors, but it’s very much on the same wavelength as the show. Just like the show, Idiocracy has loads of hilarious jokes about consumerism and how we’re all manipulated by advertising and marketing tricks, and the film is populated by the kinds of ridiculous characters fans of the show will recognize and love—like Dwayne Elizondo Mountain Dew Herbert Camacho (Terry Crews), the deeply stupid and incredibly violent President of the United States (whose hair is a character unto itself in this movie).

Like Fry often does, Joe finds himself responsible for saving the day despite being, well, pretty average in most ways. Exasperated by the dumbness all around him (this is a future America where the death penalty involves monster truck demolition derbies, the Supreme Court has been renamed the Extreme Court, and an energy drink called Brawndo is used for literally everything from medicine to crop irrigation), Joe plods along, doing his best, and (again, just like Fry) eventually scores a win.

For fans of Futurama, there’s no better choice for movie night. Rent Idiocracy on Prime Video.

Need more to watch? The obvious choice would be the actual Futurama films that were released—Bender’s Big Score (2007), The Beast with a Billion Backs (2008), Bender's Game (2008), and Into the Wild Green Yonder (2009). You can find them on Hulu as part of their Futurama collection, but the movies have been cut into episode-length slices. You can also buy each movie individually on Prime Video.

But if you’ve already watched the Futurama movies (and you probably have), here are a few more movies that aren’t Futurama but offer a similarly wacky sci-fi experience.

As a sci-fi series, Futurama has played around with actual time travel several times, so Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure is the perfect movie for fans of the show. In San Dimas, California, in 1989, Bill Preston (Alex Winter) and Ted Logan (Keanu Reeves) are slacker high school students in danger of failing history—which would have dire consequences for the rather utopian future of humanity. A man named Rufus (George Carlin) is sent back in time to help by giving them access to a time machine—and hilarious shenanigans ensue. Stream Bill and Ted's Excellent Adventure on Tubi or rent it on Prime Video.

Futurama’s writers love a good movie parody—they’ve hit Willy Wonka, Armageddon, Animal House, and One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest among many others. So one of the best parodies of one of our most cherished sci-fi franchises is the perfect follow-up to the show. It’s a Mel Brooks joint, so obviously this send-up of all things Star Wars (original trilogy only) can lean into the juvenile side, but it remains a demented takedown of a foundational science fiction universe. Plus, the long-awaited sequel is due in 2027, so a refresher is in order. Stream Spaceballs on Fubo or rent it on Prime Video.

In a lot of ways, The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy crawled so Futurama could walk. While this film, based on Douglas Adams’ original book, isn’t as pop-culture focused as Futurama, it has the same spirit of dizzy sci-fi craziness, from poetry as a torture device to an Infinite Improbability Drive that warps and bends reality every time it’s used. There are bizarre aliens, smart observations about the nature of our existence, and a rumination on the fundamental importance of towels. Rent The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy on Prime Video.

Futurama is funny, but it’s also very sweet-natured—Philip J. Fry may not be the brightest guy, but he means well, and the Planet Express crew almost always does the right thing. WALL-E has that same spirit while also hilariously lampooning modern life, giving us both an adorable, lonely robot marooned on an environmentally ruined Earth and a vision of humanity’s very fleshy, lazy, and kind of dumb future if we don’t change our ways. Stream WALL-E on Disney+ or rent it on Prime Video.

If you love the rapid-fire gags in Futurama and enjoy the absurdity of wildly impractical technology, you’ll love Megamind. A parody of superhero stories, the film follows two alien babies who are sent ot Earth, Superman-style, when their worlds are destroyed. One becomes arch-villain Megamind (Will Ferrell), the other hero Metro Man (Brad Pitt), who battle each other until Megamind finally gets the drop on his rival, killing Metro Man—and deleting all meaning from his life in the process. With stuff like dehydration guns and realistic holographic disguises, Megamind riffs on sci-fi tropes in ways that Futurama fans will love. Stream Megamind on Peacock or rent it on Prime Video.

title: DuckDuckGo Just Made It Easier to Share Links Without Getting Tracked
description: The browser's "Copy Clean Link" option strips trackers out of URLs.
fullText:
It's tough to stay private on the internet. It's hardly an even playing field: If you use apps and websites as they're designed, your every move is almost guaranteed to be tracked so that companies can compile a profile to target you with ads. That even extends to simple tasks like sharing links with friends: You might think you're simply communicating in private, but as soon as you click "copy" on that link, trackers attach themselves to the URL and come along for the ride.

It doesn't have to be this way. There are many steps you can take to prevent trackers from stalking you across the internet—some more intense than others. And while stripping tracking URLs from links isn't new, it isn't exactly common knowledge, either. That's why whenever a company makes it a bit easier, I'm all for it, so today I'm celebrating DuckDuckGo.

As highlighted by fellow CNET Group site ZDNet, DuckDuckGo's iOS app now includes a feature that automatically eliminates tracking elements from links. That way, you can share links with friends, family members, and coworkers without worrying about trackers following along.

The feature, "Copy Clean Link," doesn't do anything you couldn't do yourself. As ZDNet explains, the feature cuts out everything in the URL in question from the "?" on; essentially, all of the tracking information. Without that data, you turn the URL into a "clean" link, so trackers won't necessarily know you're the user who shared that URL in the first place. You can do this yourself by opening the URL and deleting this text manually, but tapping Copy Clean Link is certainly more convenient.

Interestingly, the feature doesn't pop up when you select a link the usual way, or even when you hit the Share button. Instead, you'll need to open the link in DuckDuckGo, long-press the address bar, and choose "Copy Clean Link." You'll find the same option if you tap the three lines in the bottom right, then scroll down and choose "Copy Clean Link." If you simply select the URL and use iOS' built-in "Copy" option, you'll grab the full URL—trackers and all.

At this time, only iPhone users can use "Copy Clean Link" in DuckDuckGo. That doesn't mean that users of other platforms are out of luck: As previously mentioned, you can manually delete all characters in a URL starting with the "?" to achieve the same effect. That's easier done on desktop than mobile, of course.

If you need an alternative, Brave has a "Copy Clean Link" option as well. It works similarly to DuckDuckGo's—you can long-press the address bar on a webpage you're already visiting or, uniquely, you can long-press any link in the browser to get the option too.

title: Free ChatGPT Users Will Get a Huge Upgrade Next Week
description: ChatGPT Free and Go users will soon have access to unlimited texts.
fullText:
There are 8.3 billion people on this planet, and roughly an eighth of them use ChatGPT. OpenAI confirmed that its infamous AI chatbot now has over one billion weekly active users, a staggering number given that ChatGPT is only three and a half years old. (For reference, that's on par with global Windows users.) Love it or hate it, there's no denying that ChatGPT—and generative AI as a whole—is firmly a part of modern life.

While there are surely many paying ChatGPT customers, the vast majority are using it for free. Though it may be exciting for paid users to try out the company's latest and greatest models, the biggest impact happens whenever OpenAI makes features available free of charge. As it happens, next week, free users are getting perhaps the biggest ChatGPT update in years.

Starting next week, you'll no longer hit a wall when simply texting with ChatGPT. OpenAI says that both free and Go users now have unlimited text chats, which should mean you can send as many text-based messages as you want without running into cooldown periods. Of course, the emphasis here is on "texts." There are absolutely still limits on other ChatGPT features, including messages with files and images, as well as Voice mode and image generation. But for users who primarily use ChatGPT with text-based messages, this update should be more than welcome.

In addition, OpenAI is switching free and Go users to the company's new GPT-5.6 Luna model, which is designed for "cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads." As such, this model likely won't be as capable as OpenAI's more powerful models available to Pro users, but free users aren't totally left in the lurch: OpenAI says there's a new "Think" button that lets you push Luna further for more complex requests. The experience is much changed from the days when users could jump between different models for free, but perhaps the unlimited text chats will make up for it for most users.

OpenAI says that Plus and Pro users are also getting some updates. The company says that its GPT-5.6 Sol model now delivers "more focused" responses, and may issue corrections instead of simply agreeing with the user when they're wrong. It also does away with some of the formatting we've come to expect from AI: Your answer may be more succinct in paragraph form, rather than expansive with bullet points. OpenAI says that Sol makes "fewer mistakes" too, but remember: all AI models hallucinate.

There's also a new slider to push the model from "Instant" to higher effort. The idea is to give users a sliding scale of power, rather than have them switch from distinct models. The more intense you push the model, the longer the responses may take, so OpenAI positions the slider as an option for users to tailor the model to their needs: If you need a quick answer, keep the slider towards the less intense side.

title: Brilliant Benkenstein leads Essex to win over Glamorgan despite Van der Gugten ton
description: A brilliant 140 by Essex's Luc Benkenstein keeps their One Day Cup hopes alive despite Timm van der Gugten's 118 not out for Glamorgan.
fullText:
Essex 312 (47.1 overs): Benkenstein 140, Thain 76; Douthwaite 3-57

Glamorgan 309-7 (50 overs): Van der Gugten 118*, Horton 85; Snater 3-49

A brilliant innings of 140 from 21-year-old Luc Benkenstein saw Essex stay afloat in the One Day Cup with a three-run victory over Glamorgan, despite a first professional hundred from Timm van der Gugten pushing them all the way.

Glamorgan slumped to 78-5 before fighting back to reach 309-7 through Alex Horton (85) and Van der Gugten's battling effort of 118 not out.

Mackenzie Jones, also 21, held his nerve to concede just two runs in a fine final over while Shane Snater took 3-49.

Benkenstein smashed 15 fours and seven sixes, facing just 109 balls and putting on 166 for the first wicket with Noah Thain (76).

But Essex fell away in the second half of their innings with Dan Douthwaite claiming 3-57 as they were bowled out for 312.

Notifications, social media and more with BBC Sport

Both teams made two changes, with Glamorgan recalling strike bowler Van der Gugten and giving tall 24-year-old Australian paceman Connor O'Riordan, formerly with New South Wales academy, another chance to push his case for a longer contract.

The county is short of seam bowling resources for the closing block of the Championship, with Ned Leonard ruled out through injury, and breakthrough teenager Tom Norton also unlikely to appear again this year- highlighting the need to sign an experienced overseas bowler.

Meanwhile Essex had the luxury of resting paceman Jamie Porter, with Zaman Akhter and Charlie Bennett replacing Porter and Mitch Killeen.

Openers Thain and Benkenstein quickly tucked into all the Glamorgan bowling with the exception of Van der Gugten.

Thain was dropped off Romano Franco on 41 while Benkenstein smashed the young spinner out of the ground as the hundred came up in the 17th over.

Essex had 166 on the board by the halfway break, although Thain fell two balls later as he drilled Douthwaite to cover, having hit nine fours and a six.

Captain Tom Westley lofted Franco to long-on but Benkenstein moved confidently to three figures off just 94 balls for his maiden county century in any format.

With Benkenstein going even harder at the bowling in a stand of 67 with Matt Critchley (28), Essex looked in complete control before Glamorgan eventually found some relief.

Critchley was run out by Zain Ul Hassan in a mix-up, Benkenstein eventually chipped Douthwaite to mid-off and O'Riordan claimed his first county wicket when Grant Roelofson edged behind.

The crash of wickets continued with the last eight falling for just 55 runs, a remarkable contrast to the early Essex onslaught.

The bowlers' domination continued in the Glamorgan innings as Eddie Byrom lofted Snater to square leg and Ul Hassan (13) pulled Charlie Bennett to Jones at mid-on.

Jones was given catching practice with Colin Ingram and Jack Hope-Bell falling to mistimed attacking shots as Bennett and Snater made more inroads.

Harry Wallace's first two scoring shots on home debut were sixes, a confident pull into the pavilion and a top edge over fine leg.

Wallace, the 17-year-old son of Glamorgan director of cricket Mark, hit four more boundaries in a promising knock of 39 before Jones had him caught behind to leave the hosts 78 for five.

Hard-hitting Horton, 22, looking to secure the Glamorgan wicket-keeper's role in succession to veteran Chris Cooke, again proved his batting ability with his third substantial knock in seven games.

The century stand with Van der Gugten came off 94 balls to make sure the home crowd had something to cheer in the early evening sunshine, with the Netherlands international making his first white-ball 50.

Horton lofted four sixes and added eight fours to revive faint hopes for his side before Snater returned to induce him to slice a drive to backward point.

Glamorgan only had four wickets in hand with 84 runs needed off the final 10, and Douthwaite (13) was caught at long-off off Jones.

With captain Andy Gorvin providing willing support, Van der Gugten reached three figures in the 48th over off 93 balls and 20 were needed off the final two overs.

But Van der Gugten clubbed the final ball of the penultimate over from Snater for a straight six to leave Glamorgan needing only six off the last over.

Jones held his line and length to deliver three successive dot balls to Gorvin, and Glamorgan could manage only two singles as an unlikely victory eluded them.

title: Palace sign defender Tomiyasu after pre-season trial
description: Crystal Palace complete the signing of Japan defender Takehiro Tomiyasu following a successful pre-season trial.
fullText:
Crystal Palace have completed the signing of Japan defender Takehiro Tomiyasu following a successful trial.

The 27-year-old - who was a free agent after spending the second half of last season with Ajax - was part of Japan's World Cup squad this summer.

The former Arsenal defender, who can play at full-back or centre-back, becomes the second signing for new Palace manager Pierre Sage after Oscar Mingueza.

The Eagles have not announced the length of Tomiyasu's contract.

Palace wanted to strengthen their defensive options with first-choice centre-back Maxence Lacroix having joined Chelsea.

Tomiyasu made 84 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal between 2021 and 2025, having previously played for Bologna and Sint-Truiden.

"Takehiro has experience at the highest level of European and international football," said Palace chairman Steve Parish.

French coach Sage has succeeded Olivier Glasner, who led the Eagles to the first major trophies in their history over the past two seasons - the FA Cup and Conference League - plus the Community Shield.

"This club is in a good moment, winning three titles in two seasons," Tomiyasu added. "Here is where I wanted to be."

Palace also have an interest in a possible loan deal for Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong and BBC Sport reported last month that the Eagles also hold a strong interest in Brest centre-back Raphael le Guen.

Palace set to sign Tomiyasu and consider March deal

This summer is a pivotal one for Crystal Palace with a new manager, a big departure in Lacroix and also another year of European football.

The Eagles are in the Europa League this season following their Conference League win last season and with that comes financial obligations.

Palace have to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio (SCR) when trying to bring in players during this transfer window.

The SCR obligations are stricter than those of the Premier League and Palace have to deal with the rules put in place by Uefa, which cap spending on wages, transfers and agent fees at 70% of club revenue.

In the Premier League, for clubs not competing in Europe, they can spend up to 85% of their revenue.

Uefa fears smaller clubs will almost always face problems because they will have to up their spending to build a squad to play in Europe but - as per rules - cannot spend the same percentage of revenue as their league rivals.

The Eagles have not yet paid a fee for a player this window but are moving towards a deal for 19-year-old Real Salt Lake winger Zavier Gozo.

Palace have also produced a couple of bits of shrewd business in the market, signing Tomiyasu on a free transfer and Mingueza after his contract at Celta Vigo expired.

There is also the possibility the Eagles could sell one or two members of their squad to generate funds and there has been interest in Brennan Johnson, who only joined the club in January.

title: McGregor says comeback starts now after knee surgery
description: Conor McGregor reiterates his desire to return to fighting after undergoing surgery on the knee injury suffered during his UFC comeback.
fullText:
Conor McGregor has reiterated his desire to return to fighting after undergoing surgery on the knee injury sustained during his UFC comeback.

The 38-year-old's return to the octagon against Max Holloway at UFC 329 last month lasted just 69 seconds because of the injury.

The Irishman's knee appeared to give way when he missed with his first attempted roundhouse kick in the opening seconds of the fight.

"Surgery done. Knee repaired," McGregor wrote on Instagram., external

"The doubters can keep talking. I didn't run from the pain - I walked straight into it.

"Now the real work begins. Comeback season starts now. No shortcuts. No excuses. Just the will to rise again."

In the video that accompanied the post, McGregor spoke of other athletes who have made successful returns from serious injuries, including two-time UFC bantamweight champion Dominick Cruz, two-division champion Georges St-Pierre and seven-time Super Bowl-winner Tom Brady.

"These are my motivation here, especially the fighting boys," he said. "My mindset is unstoppable, unbreakable."

Last month's fight, in which Holloway was declared winner by technical knockout, was McGregor's first UFC appearance since he broke his leg in a defeat by Dustin Poirier in 2021.

Critics have questioned whether McGregor still deserves the spotlight after a series of controversies in recent years, including court cases and missed drugs tests.

In November 2024, Nikita Hand, who accused McGregor of raping her, won her claim against him for damages for assault by rape in a civil case.

Last year, McGregor also accepted an 18-month ban for violating the UFC's anti-doping policy after missing three drugs tests within a 12-month period in 2024.

The ban, which was backdated to the third missed test in September 2024, concluded in March.

title: Barca cancel friendly in Morocco after Ceuta border crisis
description: Barcelona cancel pre-season friendly in Morocco because of the ongoing border crisis in Ceuta.
fullText:
Barcelona have cancelled a pre-season friendly in Morocco because of the ongoing border crisis in Ceuta.

The Spanish champions were set to face local side Ittihad Riadi Tangier in north-western Morocco on 15 August as part of their preparations for the new campaign.

"In light of the current uncertainty and circumstances, FC Barcelona considers playing the match would be inappropriate," said the club in a statement.

While the club did not specify the reason for the cancellation, BBC Sport understands the decision is linked to the situation in Ceuta, the Spanish enclave that borders Morocco on the North African coast.

About 78,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory from Morocco by sea last week, resulting in 100 deaths and sparking tensions among EU nations who share open borders.

While a large majority of the migrants have since returned to Morocco, between 3,000 and 5,000 still remain in Ceuta.

Italy had suspended its Schengen arrangement with Spain, backed by Finland and Denmark, while the Czech Republic called for Spain's membership to be temporarily suspended.

Barca also had a friendly with Preston North End cancelled after a pre-season training camp in the UK, where they played Birmingham City.

They are scheduled to face Nottingham Forest on Saturday in the Italian city of Udine and will also host Egypt's Al Ahly on 19 August.

Hansi Flick's side will begin their La Liga title defence against Elche on 23 August.

title: O'Neill out of hospital, but 'no timeline' for Celtic return
description: Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney says there is "no timeline" for Martin O'Neill's return from the "small procedure" the boss underwent in hospital and the 74-year-old will "make the call" about whether he will be in the dugout for Sunday's trip to Kilmarnock.
fullText:
Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney says there is "no timeline" for Martin O'Neill's return from the "small procedure" the boss underwent in hospital and the 74-year-old will "make the call" about whether he will be in the dugout for Sunday's trip to Kilmarnock.

O'Neill, who was given a one-year contract at the start of the season after leading Celtic to a Scottish league and cup Double after two spells as caretaker last term, was discharged from hospital on Thursday.

"I went to see him last night," Maloney revealed.

"It was really positive. He was in good form - loads better than he was Monday, Tuesday. Hopefully that sort of positive feeling he has continues."

O'Neill was in the dugout as Celtic started the new Scottish Premiership season with a 1-0 win over Dundee on Monday.

But Maloney added: "Even for the game at the weekend, it's sort of day-to-day. We saw him last night with regards to the preparation for the game and then he wasn't in today.

"I'll speak to him this afternoon and then he'll make a call for tomorrow. And then I'd imagine he'll make the call for the game at the weekend.

"But, if it's this weekend, great. If it isn't, then we'll prepare for it with that one."

Maloney, who has managed Hibernian and Wigan, admitted it would be "strange" if he has to take charge at Rugby Park.

"We'll definitely miss him if he's not there but you also have to respect what's happened the last few days," he said.

"The impact that he's had over, what was it, since October, it's been nothing short of incredible really - the things that he does with the players and the staff.

"So we will miss him, but we'll be prepared. We've got some brilliant senior players, but we'll see. We'll let him make the call."

Maloney did not expect any new signings to be made, such as the reported bid for Oviedo's Egyptian winger Haissem Hassan, before Sunday's game and admitted those matters were still exclusively between O'Neill and chief executive Michael Nicholson.

The former Scotland midfielder knew there was interest in midfielder Arne Engels and right-back Alistair Johnston, but had no reason to believe they would not be in the squad to face Kilmarnock.

title: Perimeter walls around pitches banned after Vigar death
description: The Football Association has banned solid perimeter walls around pitches after a safety review following the death of former Arsenal youth player Billy Vigar.
fullText:
The Football Association has banned solid perimeter walls around pitches after a safety review was launched following the death of former Arsenal youth player Billy Vigar.

The 21-year-old died after sustaining a "significant brain injury" while playing for Chichester City at Wingate and Finchley FC in September 2025.

It is thought the injury was caused when he collided with a concrete wall.

The review, conducted by independent health and safety experts for the 2026-27 season, said it "no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League system for men [steps 1-6], and the Women's National League [tiers 3-4]".

An FA statement added: "Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons.

"We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes."

Matches at affected grounds can continue as long as clubs assess "the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis" and plan to make changes "within a reasonable timeframe".

The FA and Premier League will provide funding to facilitate the changes.

After Vigar's death, a petition calling for a ban on brick walls around football pitches has received more than 4,000 signatures.

The government and the Professional Footballers' Association wrote to the FA, Premier League, English Football League and National League in June 2023, calling on them to adopt a more proactive approach to player safety in this area.

That came after Bath City's Alex Fletcher suffered a fractured skull after colliding with a concrete advertising hoarding during a match in November 2022.

title: A secret invite and other 'pinch-me' moments before Leicester woke up
description: Leicester are gearing up for League One but 10 years ago they were defending Premier League champions. The dream moments haven't been forgotten.
fullText:
It was a dream then, it is a dream now - especially as Leicester prepare for League One.

Ten years ago the Foxes were preparing to defend their Premier League title and looking forward to Champions League football.

At 5,000-1, they had pulled off the most improbable, the most stunning, the most incredible feat to shock the world.

But now, after back-to-back relegations, those days seem almost as surreal as when they actually happened.

New manager Russell Martin will be expected to take the club back to the Championship at the first attempt, something that sounds nowhere near as impossible as what the Foxes previously managed.

A decade on, the 'pinch-me' moments live on for those who were there, and some have shared them with BBC Sport.

Spoiler: they might not be the ones you knew about.

Leicester had won the title without kicking a ball on 2 May 2016 when nearest challengers Tottenham Hotspur could only manage a 2-2 draw with Chelsea.

The next day, there was only one group of men the media wanted to speak to.

The trouble was they were hard to find.

Crowds gathered at the club's former training ground at Belvoir Drive, a few miles outside the centre of Leicester.

Journalists and fans waited - one cameraman persuaded a neighbour to allow him in to film from their bathroom window as he aimed to get footage of the celebrating Foxes.

The media were finally instructed to head to King Power Stadium where the press room would be opened.

A five-minute drive took 30 minutes through revelling fans and it was a battle to get to there but, inside, the world's media edged in, hoping to hear from those who made this miracle possible.

But only eight reporters would receive a secret invitation to head back to Belvoir Drive.

Quietly, one-by-one, the handpicked members of the British press who regularly covered the club, slipped out of the packed room and made their way back.

This time, they were let in and ushered into the family room, just to the right of reception.

When manager Claudio Ranieri walked in, he received an immediate, impromptu, standing ovation and shook hands with those who had watched the astounding season unfold.

The man the world wanted to speak to gave an engaging audience to a few writers for 45 minutes.

Ranieri had been a left-field appointment at the start of that season, having not managed in England for 12 years since leaving Chelsea in 2004.

And he had considered bringing in some unconventional methods, such as double training sessions, which were nipped in the bud with the help of Craig Shakespeare, who had stayed on as assistant after the sacking of Ranieri's predecessor Nigel Pearson.

There were off-field changes he would bring in, though, including taking the squad out to make their own pizza after the first clean sheet of the season against Crystal Palace in October 2015.

"It sounds funny - we're keeping a clean sheet and gone for pizza but you then end up speaking to someone in the squad you probably wouldn't have spoken to at training because there's 25 of you," says former centre-back Robert Huth.

"You train, but you don't really know the guy. How's he functioning? Does he like me to shout at him? Does he want me to just be quiet?

"You talk and go through the game where maybe you wouldn't mention things, like a problem that you see on a pitch, if it's like, a stiff environment.

"If you're out and about, and you go: 'When the ball's here, I prefer if you do this' - just like tiny little things and you take criticism on differently when you talk in a social environment. You don't want to sit in a meeting room being told what to do."

It allowed winger Riyad Mahrez to flourish and Jamie Vardy to plunder 24 league goals, with Ranieri comparing his counter-attacking forwards to the RAF.

It is well documented that Vardy had invited the squad to his house to watch what would end up being the title-winning match as Spurs blew a 2-0 lead to draw with Chelsea - and that some players needed to wait at the local police station before arriving because of the crowds of fans who had gathered outside.

But not all his team-mates were there.

While everyone else partied, winger Nathan Dyer had a different night, in hospital with wife Laura after the birth of their second child, Shea, two days earlier.

"I had the laptop out watching the game in hospital, the boys were at the party. I wasn't able to make it but I'd never miss the birth of my child," he says.

"It was a strange feeling. It was surreal, like it wasn't real at the time but it was.

"We had to be put in a room as people were putting their heads round and even then you could see the eyes at the door. People were congratulating me and were really proud.

"It was the whole city, even people who were not fans were so happy Leicester had achieved this."

He'd had a dramatic arrival at the club in the first place that season, joining on loan from Swansea on transfer deadline day and being flown to Leicester in the late former owner Khun Vichai's helicopter to beat the deadline.

"My wife was pregnant, we'd just moved into a new house, so everything was in boxes, it was a wild day," he says.

"It was exciting for me but also nerve-wracking because it was so intense, to send the helicopter to get me to get it over the line. It was a proud moment for me - I'd always wanted to be involved in a moment like that, watching on the TV - breaking news!"

Leicester were two points behind Arsenal at the turn of the year but one defeat in the final 16 games - a dramatic late loss at Arsenal in February - had put them on course for the title.

The closer they edged to the impossible, the more the interest in the Foxes exploded.

Vardy had a lookalike - postman Lee Chapman - and Ranieri had a sausage named after him.

Local butchers W Archer & Son created the Ranieri from Packington free-range pork, fennel, garlic and chilli.

It won a star at the Great Taste awards and at one stage the shop was shifting 12kg (26.5lb) a day.

Owner Sean Jeynes even brought a plate of sausages to the stadium before a news conference, which led Ranieri to declare himself 'the sausageman'.

"It was surreal that day. How did that ever happen?" says Jeynes.

"We were making sausages two or three times a day, smelling of garlic, smelling of fennel, but it was just a crazy time. It really was a crazy time - you can't quite comprehend what it was like.

"It had a massive effect on the city, it had a great effect on everybody. Everyone was much happier.

"Nothing can replace the Italian sausage, the recipe, and the pork, fennel, garlic chili and a hint of Champions League.

"People would say, why don't you do a [Brendan] Rodgers sausage [after winning the FA Cup in 2021], but it's just not the same."

The sausage is still occasionally back on their counters, a lasting reminder of a unique time.

That is not the only taste of success that is still being enjoyed today.

"Thanks to Leicester City it meant I could retire at 55 instead of 67," says Foxes Trust co-chair Lynn Wyeth, who stuck £2 on the club at odds of 5,000-1 at the start of the season.

"It was actually really stressful. A first world problem, isn't it? It was stressful enough, watching them get closer and closer thinking, oh my god, can we do it? But knowing that there was £10,000 riding on it as well, was like, 'oh, no, I almost wish I'd cashed out earlier'.

"When I won, I had my account shut for money laundering, I had to prove it was me and that I'd won it.

"We managed to clear it up quite quickly, I think it's just an automatic thing.

"There you go. Thank you, Leicester."

title: Sunrisers knock out three sides with win over Phoenix
description: Sunrisers Leeds put three sides out of contention for the Hundred's knock-out stage with a comprehensive nine-wicket win over Birmingham Phoenix at Edgbaston.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Edgbaston

Birmingham Phoenix 107-9 (100 balls): Lamb 47 (34); Deepti 3-11

Sunrisers Leeds 111-1 (69 balls): Litchfield 71* (33); Fatima 1-25

Sunrisers Leeds won by nine wickets

Sunrisers Leeds put three sides out of contention for the Hundred's knock-out stage with a comprehensive nine-wicket win over Birmingham Phoenix at Edgbaston.

The home side, MI London and London Spirit can no longer progress after Phoebe Litchfield's unbeaten 33-ball 71 helped take Sunrisers past their target of 108 with 31 balls to spare.

Opener Litchfield brought up her fastest ever half-century in the competition, reaching the landmark off 20 deliveries, and hit 13 fours and one six in her innings.

Bryony Smith was the only Sunrisers batter to fall, caught by Alana King off Fatima Sana for 12, with Lauren Winfield-Hill (26) joining Litchfield to put on an unbroken partnership of 87.

Only two Phoenix batters made it into double figures after they were put into bat, with Ellyse Perry and Emma Lamb scoring 31 and 47 respectively, while Deepti Sharma (3-11) and Kate Cross (2-14) impressed for the visitors.

Lamb was the last batter dismissed, run out by Litchfield, as Phoenix lost four wickets for five runs before closing on 107-9.

Sunrisers move above Welsh Fire into fourth and within two points of Manchester Super Giants in the last knock-out place, with all sides now having played six matches.

Bottom-side Phoenix and the London teams, with whom they are level on six points, will only be playing for pride in their last two fixtures.

title: Price fight now likely to be held in 2027 - Shields
description: Pound-for-pound star Claressa Shields says a fight with Wales' Lauren Price is now likely to take place in 2027.
fullText:
Pound-for-pound star Claressa Shields says a fight with Wales' Lauren Price is now likely to take place in 2027.

The 31-year-old American is one of the sport's most decorated fighters - a multi-weight undisputed world champion and reigning undisputed heavyweight champion.

Price, 32, is the unified welterweight champion and, like Shields, is an Olympic gold medallist.

"When I look at Lauren fight, she's very explosive. She's fast. She got a lot of skill. I can't wait to get in there and showcase my skills against her," Shields told BBC Sport.

Shields will move down to middleweight to challenge Australia's WBA and WBC world champion Kaye Scott on 15 August in Atlanta, Georgia.

"I will have this fight and I'd love to fight again at the end of the year at 160lb [middleweight]," she added.

"I thought it was going to Lauren, but I don't know when Lauren is getting back in the ring. But I think me and her will fight in 2027, in the first quarter."

Shields faced off with Price after the Newport fighter's points victory over Stephanie Pineiro in Cardiff in April.

Price's promoter Ben Shalom later said a two-fight deal with Shields was agreed, but the Briton has not fought since and talk had quietened.

Shields, however, is confident it will happen at middleweight and thinks Price - who would have to jump up two divisions from welterweight - will take a warm-up fight to get her "feet wet" at the new division.

Shields has remarkably only lost one fight in boxing - to Savannah Marshall as an amateur - but avenged her defeat against the Briton in the professional ranks at London's O2 Arena in 2022.

But the self-proclaimed 'Greatest Woman of All Time' thinks Price will be a tougher fight than Hartlepool's Marshall.

"She's an Olympic gold medallist and undefeated. For her to have the skillset at 5ft 7in or something and go to the Olympics at 165lb and win an Olympic medal... you have to have a hell of a lot of skill, a hell of a lot of power."

Despite going back down in weight, Shields is a heavy favourite against 41-year-old Scott, who has won five, lost one and drawn one as a pro.

"She has a great amateur background and she's been fast-tracked to some world titles. I'm just going to go out there and show how great I am and see if she's tough enough to withstand that," Shields said.

The Michigan fighter has been largely dominant in all her fights but says an area she is looking to improve on is her knockout record, with just three stoppages in 18 pro wins.

"I don't think it has anything to do with my power. I hurt every girl I fight. I'm dropping girls. Beating their faces up," the unbeaten Shields added.

"But am I just throwing the right shot at the right time to get a knockout? I know I have a lot of power."

title: Why can't the Premier League attract the world's best players?
description: Vinicius Jr chose to stay at Real Madrid, but why does the Premier League rarely attract global superstars at their peak?
fullText:
Had Vinicius Jr joined Arsenal, he would have been a rarity as a genuine global superstar moving to the Premier League at the height of his powers.

The Gunners were prepared to make the Brazil forward their primary target should he decide to leave Real Madrid, and the 26-year-old was open to the possibility.

But he has now signed a new contract at the Bernabeu until 2032.

It is another reminder of a curious contradiction.

Premier League clubs have unrivalled collective spending power and England's top flight is widely regarded as the strongest domestic competition in world football, but attracting established Ballon d'Or contenders has proved difficult.

They have little problem attracting and retaining elite centre-backs and goalkeepers but the scarcity is more obvious further forward, where the most coveted attackers and attacking midfielders still often choose elsewhere.

Since the Premier League began in 1992, only three players have won the men's Ballon d'Or while representing an English top-flight club: Liverpool's Michael Owen in 2001, Manchester United's Cristiano Ronaldo in 2008 and Manchester City's Rodri in 2024.

What England has been exceptionally good at is providing the environment in which elite talents become global stars.

Dennis Bergkamp arrived at Arsenal after a difficult spell at Inter Milan and became one of the Premier League's most influential players. Eric Cantona had already shown flashes of his talent in France and at Leeds before becoming the emblem of Manchester United's first great Premier League side.

Thierry Henry arrived in north London after an underwhelming spell at Juventus before developing into one of his generation's outstanding forwards. Ronaldo joined United as an exciting 18-year-old from Sporting, won the Ballon d'Or five years later, then signed for Real Madrid the following summer.

Erling Haaland is perhaps the clearest recent example. Already one of Europe's most coveted young forwards when Manchester City signed him from Borussia Dortmund in 2022, Haaland had yet to reach the level he has in England.

That is different from signing a player such as Vinicius after he has already won multiple Champions Leagues and established himself among the world's most recognisable footballers.

There have been exceptions, but many of the biggest names arrived after their peak.

The clearest comparison to Vinicius is Andriy Shevchenko, who joined Chelsea from AC Milan in 2006 at the age of 29. He had won the Ballon d'Or only two years earlier and finished fifth in 2005, making him one of the rare established global superstars to move to the Premier League while still close to the height of his career.

Other Ballon d'Or winners such as Ruud Gullit and George Weah also joined Chelsea, but later in their careers, while Ronaldo returned to United at 36, Zlatan Ibrahimovic arrived at 34, and Jurgen Klinsmann signed for Tottenham at 30.

During the 1980s and 1990s, Serie A was both enormously wealthy and the undisputed home of football's biggest stars.

Diego Maradona left Barcelona for Napoli. Brazil's Ronaldo moved from Barcelona to Inter at his explosive peak. Michel Platini, Marco van Basten, Lothar Matthaus and Zinedine Zidane all spent some of the finest years of their careers in Italy.

But the Premier League's financial dominance has produced a different transfer market.

English clubs spend enormous sums, but it can be distributed across deep squads or on players already proven within the competition.

Alexander Isak, Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson, Moises Caicedo, Declan Rice and Jack Grealish have all moved between Premier League clubs for more than £100m.

Others, such as Liverpool's Florian Wirtz, arrive from overseas with enormous reputations but with their best years potentially still ahead.

The model is less about importing one 'Galactico' and more about assembling 18-22 elite players capable of surviving a demanding season.

Real Madrid and Barcelona are difficult for English clubs to compete with when the world's most coveted players become available.

Jude Bellingham is a striking example. Having left Birmingham City for Borussia Dortmund to continue his development, the England midfielder moved to Real Madrid rather than back to his home country.

He remains the only player to represent England's senior men's team during the Premier League era without making an appearance in the competition.

Kylian Mbappe was linked with several clubs elsewhere before fulfilling his ambition of joining Real Madrid, while Neymar chose Barcelona over interest from Premier League teams when leaving Santos in 2013 - attracted in part by the chance to play alongside Lionel Messi.

Cristiano Ronaldo left Manchester United for Real Madrid a year after winning the Ballon d'Or, while Luis Suarez joined Barcelona months after winning the Premier League Golden Boot and PFA Players' Player of the Year with Liverpool.

And Gareth Bale and Eden Hazard swapped London for Madrid after establishing themselves among the Premier League's leading players. Bale joined Real from Tottenham in 2013 after winning the PFA Players' Player of the Year award for a second time, while Hazard made the same move from Chelsea six years later, having previously won the league's top individual honour.

Harry Kane later departed Tottenham for Bayern Munich despite sitting only 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's Premier League record of 260.

There are practical attractions to Spain - climate, lifestyle and, for many South American players, linguistic and cultural familiarity - but the appeal runs deeper.

Real Madrid and Barcelona carry a particular status as destination clubs, reinforced by their Champions League history, global reach and association with individual honours such as the Ballon d'Or.

Both have been interested in Rodri this summer.

Man City reject Barcelona's £38.5m bid for Rodri

Barcelona? Real Madrid? Man City's Rodri has a decision to make

Haaland, meanwhile, represents the counterargument. City signed him from Dortmund at 21 and he has developed into one of the world's most feared number nines.

But even his future illustrates the enduring pull of Real Madrid.

Speaking to DAZN during the 2026 World Cup, Haaland's father Alfie was asked about the prospect of the striker one day moving to the Bernabeu.

"He's happy at City, he's got a long contract… but any player wants to play for Real Madrid," he said.

That does not mean a move is imminent, but the sentiment is revealing. England has repeatedly shown it can provide the stage on which superstars are made. Persuading those already at the summit to choose the Premier League - and convincing those who reach it there to stay - remains the harder task.

title: England opener Gay has shoulder injury scare
description: England opener Emilio Gay suffers a shoulder injury while playing for Durham in their One-Day Cup against Middlesex.
fullText:
England opener Emilio Gay has suffered a shoulder injury while batting for Durham in their One-Day Cup match with Middlesex.

Gay had been feeling his right shoulder but after playing an on-drive off Toby Roland-Jones, he called for the physio.

After a few minutes of treatment he left the field, retiring hurt on eight and his county have said that he will be assessed over the weekend.

Without a contract in The Hundred, the 26-year-old has played in five of Durham's matches in this competition.

Gay has been named in an enlarged 16-man England squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan later this month.

The first match of the three-Test series begins at Headingley on 19 August.

title: 'Critically important' summit called on future of Scottish football
description: The Scottish Football Association is to hold a "critically important" summit around the future of the national game.
fullText:
The Scottish Football Association is to hold a "critically important" summit around the future of the national game.

An email has been sent to all Scottish Professional Football League clubs to attend the forum, which will take place in St Andrews on 4 September.

The email, which has been seen by BBC Scotland, says the SFA will "discuss opportunities" around homegrown talent and hear from clubs who have "optimised their elite talent development model".

The memo also states the objective is to focus on the "current reality" facing Scottish football.

Part of the conversation will be around improving the prospects for homegrown Scottish talent and increasing revenue streams for clubs.

This comes after Scotland's national team failed to make it out of their group at the men's World Cup, their first finals since 1998.

The summit will be hosted by SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell and chief football officer Craig Mulholland.

title: Niewiadoma-Phinney wins on Ventoux to take Tour lead
description: Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney produces a thrilling solo ride to the summit of Mont Ventoux to claim her first Tour de France Femmes stage win and the overall race lead.
fullText:
Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney produced a thrilling solo ride to the summit of Mont Ventoux to claim her first Tour de France Femmes stage win and the overall race lead.

The iconic climb of Mont Ventoux was included in the Tour de France Femmes for the first time for this year's 'queen stage'.

Niewiadoma-Phinney began the 146.8km ride from La Voulte-sur-Rhone third in the general classification, one minute and 17 seconds behind race leader Marlen Reusser, with Demi Vollering second.

And the Polish Canyon-SRAM rider, who won the Tour in 2024, launched an attack with 9km of the Mont Ventoux climb remaining.

As the 31-year-old pulled clear of her rivals on stage seven, it became a battle for the leader's yellow jersey.

She ultimately reached the summit finish one minute and 16 seconds before Dutch rider Vollering, with Reusser 30 seconds further back and defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prevot more than 10 minutes down.

Niewiadoma-Phinney now holds a 15-second lead over Vollering with two stages remaining while Swiss rider Reusser is 39 seconds adrift in third.

"I'm blown away with what just happened," said Niewiadoma-Phinney.

"This victory goes to so many people that were with me along this very long road without proper big wins.

"It was so funny, as we started to climb Mont Ventoux I looked to my right and saw my parents. They made a surprise visit and I could see my dad crying. I was like 'I just need to make them proud'."

Saturday's penultimate stage is the longest of this year's race, with the mostly flat 171.9km ride from Sisteron to Nice set to suit the sprinters.

That will leave the general classification rivals to battle it out for the title on a 99.2km mountain stage beginning and ending in Nice on Sunday.

title: Flintoff leaves England Lions head coach role
description: Former England all-rounder Andrew Flintoff steps down as head coach of England Lions.
fullText:
Former England all-rounder Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of England Lions.

The 48-year-old, who has been in charge of the Lions since September 2024, thanked England managing director Rob Key in his leaving statement for "trusting me with one of the most important roles in English cricket."

Flintoff was named head coach of Australian Big Bash franchise Sydney Thunder in June, taking up his first overseas T20 coaching role.

He was initially set to continue in his Lions role, leaving a planned tour of South Africa early to join-up with Thunder, but now departs the national set-up.

"Unfortunately I've made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions," said Flintoff.

"Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

"I'd like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give everyday.

"I can't wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me."

Flintoff also spent two seasons as Northern Superchargers men's coach in The Hundred, leading the Leeds-based side to fourth and third-placed finishes.

He was not retained for 2026 after the franchise was taken over by the owners of the Sunrisers group.

Prior to his appointment with the Lions, Flintoff helped coach England's white-ball sides on an informal basis, having left his position as a presenter on television driving programme Top Gear.

His last assignment in the Lions role was South Africa A's tour of England in May and June, where his side lost both four-day matches and two of three 50-over games.

"Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players," said England and Wales Cricket Board men's performance director Ed Barney.

"Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group.

"We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game."

Mike Yardy will step in as head coach for the four-day Professional County Club Select XI match that serves as Pakistan's warm-up before their three-Test series against England later this month.

The fixture begins at Beckenham on Wednesday, 12 August, while the Lions will also be the opposition for Sri Lanka's two T20 warm-ups at the start of their limited-overs tour of England in September.
