title: A Russian retail giant’s warehouse burns after Ukraine's latest long-range drone attack
description: Ukrainian long-range drones hit a warehouse of Russia’s biggest online retailer in the Ural Mountains, more than 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) from the two countries’ border, local officials and the ...
fullText:
Ukrainian long-range drones hit a warehouse of Russia's biggest online retailer in the Ural Mountains, more than 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) from the two countries' border, local officials and the company said Friday.

Ukraine has regularly hit targets in the distant Urals this year and has even struck a Russian oil refinery in western Siberia, nearly 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the border. The attacks are examples of how Kyiv has used drone innovation as a key part of its response to the invasion by its much bigger enemy more than four years ago.

Its successes have drawn international interest and drone cooperation agreements with nine countries, with further deals being negotiated with 15 other countries, according to Kyiv officials.

Wildberries said its warehouse in Yekaterinburg, Russia's fourth-largest city, was set ablaze by the attack. Most merchandise wasn't damaged, the company said, unlike at some of the more than a dozen other Wildberries depots struck by Ukraine in recent weeks that have burned down.

The regional governor, Denis Pasler, said three drones hit the warehouse's roof. Artyom Zhoga, the Kremlin's representative in the region, said that 800 people were evacuated from the warehouse and nobody was hurt.

Kyiv is trying to rattle the Russian public and the Kremlin with the attacks.

Russian President Vladimir Putin chaired a meeting Friday of the country's Security Council. He said in televised opening remarks that the meeting would focus on additional measures to "strengthen … protection of infrastructure facilities" but gave no further details.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is pushing for his country to keep up the pace of technological development, especially in air defense systems to help stop Russian ballistic missiles that are exploiting Ukraine's shortage of American-made Patriot interceptor missiles and battering civilian areas.

A joint European anti-ballistic development program is already underway, Zelenskyy said late Thursday, with 10 countries engaged in developing an anti-ballistic shield. Europe is concerned about Moscow's ambitions on the continent beyond Ukraine.

"Ukraine is capable of producing its (anti-ballistic) missile and launcher, while our partners will provide the necessary components and critical elements — radars, sensors, and everything else required," Zelenskyy said on social media. "An anti-ballistic program of our own — one that is truly large-scale — will greatly benefit everyone in Europe."

At the same time, Ukraine is working on manufacturing its own ballistic missiles to use against Russia. "The tests have shown strong potential. We need to turn this into a real weapon," Zelenskyy said.

Ukrainian front-line defenses in eastern regions, meanwhile, remain under strain as Russia's bigger army looks for a breakthrough after months of minimal advances that Western analysts and officials say have had a high cost for Moscow in troop casualties.

Ukraine has been evacuating children from Kramatorsk, one of the four eastern Donetsk region cities that make up the Ukrainian so-called Fortress Belt. The line of four large and heavily defended cities, about 50 kilometers (30 miles) long, has been key to denying Moscow its goal of seizing Ukraine's industrial heartland.

The head of the Donetsk region's regional military administration, Vadym Filashkin, said Friday that more than 800 people, including 91 children, were evacuated over the previous 24 hours.

Ukraine has been deploying midrange strike drones to disrupt Russia's supply lines and slow its advance.

Zelenskyy said that the recently appointed commander-in-chief of the Ukrainian armed forces, Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi, reported to him Friday about the military situation in Donetsk.

He said in a social media post that they reached "an understanding of how to strengthen" Ukraine's defenses there but gave no details.

Russia's air defenses downed 203 Ukrainian drones from late Thursday through early Friday, the Defense Ministry in Moscow said.

Over the past week, the Russian military struck 31 bulk cargo vessels and three tugboats that operated "in the interests of the Ukrainian armed forces," it said.

It added that late Thursday two ships were hit by Geran-4 drones in the Black Sea east and southeast of Odesa and one was struck in the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk.

In other attacks, the ministry said that the military hit a facility assembling long-range drones in Okhtyrka in the Sumy region on Thursday. It also released a video of a train purportedly carrying military equipment struck by a Geran drone and then an Iskander ballistic missile near Vyshneve in the Dnipropetrovsk region.

Meanwhile, Russia attacked Ukraine with 147 long-range strike drones overnight, according to the Ukrainian air force.

In Ukraine's northern Sumy region, a Russian drone struck a busy market Friday morning, wounding 10 people, authorities said.

Russia also launched glide bombs and drones of various types at the regional capital, according to the head of regional administration, Oleh Hryhorov.

The attack targeted residential buildings, transport and infrastructure, wounding two people, he said.

Follow the AP's coverage of the war in Ukraine at https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine

title: Trump distances himself from voter frustration with GOP: ‘They’re not angry at me’
description: President Donald Trump distanced himself from voters’ ire with Republicans ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, telling Punchbowl News in an interview released Friday he thinks voters are angry with t...
fullText:
President Donald Trump distanced himself from voters' ire with Republicans ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, telling Punchbowl News in an interview released Friday he thinks voters are angry with the party more generally, but not him.

"The question is will they vote? 'Cause a lot of them are very angry at Republicans to be honest with you," he said, noting that he's not on the ballot and adding, "They're not angry at me, but they are angry at Republicans."

Republicans are trailing Democrats on the generic congressional ballot by 8 points among registered voters, according to a CNN poll conducted by SSRS out late last month, indicating the electorate is agitating for wholesale changes in Congress.

Democrats also continue to hold a significant advantage in voter enthusiasm and have a 20-point advantage in preferences among those who say they are extremely motivated to vote. And 63% of Americans say the GOP is focusing too little on cost-of-living issues, compared with 52% who say the Democrats aren't spending enough time on it.

The president defended himself from criticisms within his own party that he doesn't care about Congress and losing the majority, pointing to his endorsements and appearances on the trail while arguing that he doesn't have to campaign because he's not running.

"I could do a lot easier. I don't have to be away in Nevada yesterday. I didn't have to be in Los Angeles yesterday making speeches. I didn't have to be supporting all the people. I have a lot, you know, I have a busy schedule," Trump said.

He added, "I said to somebody, 'Wait a minute. You don't understand. I won. I'm not campaigning.'"

Trump committed in the interview to have MAGA Inc. — his super PAC which boasts a $400 million war chest — spend money in the midterms.

"I'm going to help Republicans," Trump said.

There's been some GOP anxiety over the fund, as the PAC accumulates millions of dollars but hasn't started spending to boost members of the party. Trump argued that he controls the PAC, and can direct it to spend money in whatever manner he sees fit. "I could spend it on pretty much anything I want," Trump said.

Members of the president's political operation, including James Blair, who has taken leave from the White House help with Trump's midterm strategy, have said they expected to financially aid Republicans in November. It remains unclear how much they plan to spend in the effort or when they plan to start spending.

As tensions have grown in recent weeks between Trump and Senate Majority Leader John Thune, Trump declined to support the South Dakota senator for another term leading Republicans in the chamber.

"I don't want to get into that," Trump said when asked about Thune in the interview taped on Thursday.

"I do have disagreements," Trump said about his relationship with Thune, saying it was "unfortunate" he does not have the votes to pass the "SAVE America Act" and get rid of the filibuster.

Trump riled up MAGA Republicans to direct their ire at the GOP leader to pass the federal elections overhaul bill despite the Senate having already rejected it. And Thune has repeatedly rejected Trump's calls to have his chamber vote to nuke the filibuster.

The split between Trump and Thune has widened since Trump moved to take out fellow Republican, Sen. John Cornyn, in his primary in May.

In the interview, Trump was much more complimentary of House Speaker Mike Johnson, whom he called a "fantastic person."

title: I tried Burger King's upgraded Whopper, which the chain says is helping drive sales. I can see why.
description: Burger King upgraded its signature Whopper burger with a new bun and packaging. The company said on Thursday that the updates are paying off.
fullText:
Burger King upgraded its signature Whopper burger in February with a new bun and packaging.

The burger is thicker, more flavorful, and doesn't cost more — a win for value-conscious customers.

Burger King executives said this week that the upgraded burger has helped boost sales by 8.5%.

Burger King's updated Whopper burger is helping to boost the brand and reignite the fast-food burger wars.

Inspired by customer complaints that its iconic burger was often squished during transit — it used to be simply wrapped in paper — the fast-food chain updated its signature Whopper in February with new box packaging, a new bun, and new, "creamier" mayonnaise.

The company said on Thursday that the updates are paying off.

The chain reported that US same-store sales jumped 8.5% in the second quarter, a surge that company president Tom Curtis attributed to the updated burger and new family-focused promotions, such as Burger King's Mandalorian meal collab.

Customers also bought about 20% more Whoppers than they did in the previous period, suggesting the makeover is resonating.

Its success comes as other burger chains struggle with sales. On Friday, Wendy's reported a 7% decline in same-store sales for the second quarter. McDonald's, which also released a new burger earlier this year, announced on Tuesday that comparable US sales growth slowed to 0.8% in the second quarter. Both chains pointed to problems with their value strategies: McDonald's cited too many overlapping promotions and discounts, while Wendy's pointed to its decision to pull back on discounting.

I tried Burger King's new "elevated" Whopper following its release, and I thought it was a clear upgrade from the original.

The Whopper has been around for decades. This is the first time it's been served in a cardboard box.

Released in 1957, just four years after the chain opened, the Whopper was 37 cents compared to Burger King's original burger, which cost 18 cents.

Whoppers — and all Burger King burgers, for that matter — are flame-grilled, giving their burgers a distinct smoky flavor. Another difference between Burger King's premium burgers and those of other chains, like McDonald's, is that Burger King's burgers are typically wrapped in paper rather than served in a cardboard box.

This new presentation is the most obvious change from the original Whopper.

The new cardboard box design better protected the burger from getting smushed during transit.

The chain announced on February 26 that it would change its Whopper packaging in response to negative customer feedback.

"So the Whopper being smushed, literally, I've heard it… and we've seen it," Curtis told CNN.

Another change to the burger was the bun itself — it was described in a press release as "a more premium, better-tasting bun."

After I bought the burger, I agreed that the bun looked much thicker, shinier, and better than previous iterations.

The burger has all the same toppings as the original, with upgraded mayonnaise.

While Whoppers don't typically come with cheese, I always order mine with cheese. The other toppings include sliced onions and tomatoes, lettuce, pickles, and a new, "better-tasting" mayo, according to the chain.

The burger definitely felt thicker than the original, even though it was less expensive than the last time I bought a Whopper.

When I ordered a Whopper with cheese on February 14, 2026, it cost $9.17, excluding tax, at my local Burger King in Brooklyn.

When I ordered the same burger on February 27, 2026, it cost $8.58, excluding tax, at the same location.

Burger King's prices can vary by location and franchise. CNN reported that Burger King recommended that franchisees not raise prices for the new elevated Whopper.

The thicker, fluffier bun gave the burger more heft, but the biggest difference was how well it held together.

Unlike the original Whopper — which could turn soggy from its thinner mayonnaise and heavy condiments — this version was less saucy and stayed intact much better.

The new, creamier mayonnaise had more flavor, without making the burger a soggy mess. Combined with the still-flavorful flame-grilled burger patty, crunchy lettuce, and fresh tomato slices, this burger still remained my top pick among the most famous fast-food signature burgers.

I thought the burger was an improvement on the original Whopper without reinventing the wheel.

When updating a fast-food burger as iconic as the Whopper, there's a risk in changing too much — longtime fans may not respond well if it strays too far from what they know and expect.

However, I thought this slightly upgraded version of the Whopper hit all the right notes, and as fast-food customers seek out value more than ever, this burger delivered on that promise, too.

It maintained the same flavor profile while addressing the burger's biggest problem areas: flat, soggy buns and a slightly too high price point.

As a result, I understand why it's helping bring customers through Burger King's doors. It's still the same Whopper you know and love — just with a tune-up.

Editor's note: This story was first published in February 2026 and most recently updated in August 2026.

title: GOP senator deals crushing blow to Trump's AG nominee after Alaska lobbying blitz
description: Todd Blanche's attorney general confirmation lost its last cushion as Lisa Murkowski cited the Epstein files and the $2 billion anti-weaponization fund.
fullText:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche just lost the last little bit of cushion he had left to survive confirmation.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, announced that she would not support Blanche's nomination to be the nation's top prosecutor and law enforcement official, dealing another blow to his rocky confirmation process.

Her defection, despite a heavy lobbying effort by Blanche that saw him make the trek to Alaska, means that Senate Republican leadership can't afford to lose anymore votes to get him across the finish line, given that Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., though now back home, has still not returned to the Senate.

Collins Drops The Hammer On Trump's Pick To Lead Doj, Jeopardizing Path To Confirmation

Murkowski acknowledged Blanche's visit to Alaska and heavy lobbying effort throughout the last few weeks, but it's his connection to President Donald Trump's nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund, and broader concerns of a weaponized Justice Department, that proved the nail in the coffin for her.

"The politicization — even weaponization — of the Department did not start with this administration but has accelerated during it," Murkowski said in a statement. "I take issue with the handling of the release of the Epstein files; the sweeping immunity protections granted to the President, his family, and their businesses; the statements that have been made to anti-abortion groups; and the repeated targeting of individuals ranging from former administration staff to sitting U.S. Senators."

"I am also keenly aware that the Department's nearly $2-billion dollar slush fund—which likely would have rewarded January 6 protesters—is only off the table because this nomination is pending and the Senate has leverage," she continued. "Once we vote, that will end, and there is no telling what the future holds."

Trump's Ag Pick Survives — For Now — As Republicans Question If White House Deal Will Hold

To Murkowski's latter issue, several lawmakers in both sides of the aisle acknowledge that though Blanche and the Department of Justice (DOJ) agreed to permanently rescind the fund in writing to Sens. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, there's nothing stopping Trump from reviving it.

And he's on several occasions made clear he wants to see it come back.

Before making her decision, Trump already took a snipe at her during an interview with Punch Bowl News published Friday morning.

Trump Threatens To Yank His Own Ag Nominee As Gop Revolt Grows

"I'm against Murkowski," Trump said. "I do more for Alaska than any president in history. No president's done for Alaska what I've done. She's not good."

Meanwhile, it's unclear whether the Senate will actually vote on Blanche on Friday, which could be the upper chamber's grand finale of the summer before it exits Washington, D.C., for the remainder of August.

And there's still one more Republican that hasn't weighed in on how they'll vote: Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La.

If he defects, and McConnell is still gone, it will be a 50-50 vote. That means Vice President JD Vance would need to break the tie. But for now, only Murkowski and Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, are publicly opposing Blanche's confirmation.

"The country needs an Attorney General who will check the worst impulses of this administration," Murkowski said. "I hope Mr. Blanche is able to achieve that, if confirmed, but I simply do not have confidence that will be the case."

title: How to Watch Made by Google 2026: The Pixel Event's Start Time and What to Expect
description: The Made by Google 2026 livestream is starting a bit late this year.
fullText:
It's nearly time for another Google keynote. Back in May, the company hosted Google I/O, its annual developers conference, where it announced a series of new software features and AI updates. On the flip side, "Made by Google" is all about the hardware that will run those new software updates. If you're curious about Google's next generation of devices, you'll want to tune into this presentation.

Usually, tech events—especially in the U.S.—are in the morning for West Coasters (and, as such, in the early afternoon for East Coasters). Many companies like Google are based in California, so a 10 a.m. PT start time is pretty common. As I'm on the East Coast, I'm quite used to starting coverage around 1 p.m. for most tech events.

This year is much different. Made by Google officially kicks off at 3 p.m. PT on Wednesday, Aug. 12. That means a 6 p.m. start time for those of us on the East Coast.

If you didn't get an invite to watch Made by Google in person, no worries: The company hosts a livestream for anyone to watch from home. Most companies run a livestream through YouTube, and as Google owns the video platform, it makes sense for its official livestream to live there, too. Even though the event doesn't start until next week, Google already has the livestream video open. You can watch from the feed below, or from the link here.

While most companies officially keep their product announcements under wraps prior to an event, these days leaks and rumors typically spill the beans long before it kicks off. Perhaps that's why Google has gone ahead and spoiled the biggest announcements ahead of time: The company has already posted teasers for both the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro Fold on social media. While even those reveals were hardly a surprise to anyone following the Google rumors, it is funny to have confirmation about two products ahead of time.

In addition to new Pixel smartphones, rumors suggest that we'll also see the new Pixel Watch 5 on Wednesday. Perhaps the company will even announce the Google Pixel Tag, which would mark Google's first attempt at an AirTag-like product. For a full account of the leaks and rumors going into Made by Google 2026, check out our explainer here.

title: Why three is no crowd for Swansea boss Matos
description: Vitor Matos insists Swansea City can operate with three senior strikers in their squad in 2026-27 after the signing of Ross Stewart.
fullText:
Vitor Matos says Ross Stewart has not been signed as a replacement for Zan Vipotnik and believes Swansea City can operate with three senior strikers in their squad in 2026-27.

Swansea have landed a proven Championship performer after signing Scotland international Stewart on a three-year deal.

The former Southampton player joins Vipotnik – last season's second-tier top scorer with 23 league goals – and £6m former Celtic frontman Idah on Swansea's books.

While Swansea are conscious that Vipotnik and Idah could yet be the subject of transfer interest in this summer's window, Matos insists he can keep his three forwards happy.

"There's a lot of games to come, a lot of competitions to participate in, and I think having a squad with depth in all positions is quite important for us," said the Swansea head coach.

"It's something that we felt last season in some moments was a little bit tricky. I remember when I was sitting here in December and everyone asked why we only have Zan Vipotnik as a striker and I needed I think maybe three press conferences to try to justify that.

"Now I'm justifying the opposite. I think it's important to have that depth and then trying to squeeze the best out of the squad."

Vipotnik, 24, has been linked with clubs across Europe in the wake of his spectacular 2025-26 campaign, but Swansea have indicated there have been no bids yet for the Slovenia international.

Republic of Ireland player Idah, 25, will be aiming to make a bigger impression in his second year at Swansea having played second fiddle to Vipotnik – and suffered a serious hamstring injury – last term.

The arrival of 30-year-old Stewart, who was a free agent after failing to agree a new deal at Southampton, means there will be fierce competition for a place in Swansea's attack.

But Matos is adamant the former Sunderland player has not been recruited because one his other forwards is likely to be sold.

"We signed Ross because we believe it was an opportunity for us to catch a player with that right type of profile," he added.

"It's nothing related to [Vipotnik] leaving or not. It's just what was a [good] opportunity.

"He brings leadership in a position where we needed experience of the league. He offers the same spontaneity in terms of the penalty box that Vipi (Vipotnik) has, he offers the same physicality that Adam can offer as well. So I think it's a good combination with what we have at the moment."

Foundations now in place at Swansea - Gorringe

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Stewart has been troubled by injuries at times during his career, with the former Sunderland player managing only 17 appearances across his first two seasons at Southampton before a better run in 2025-26.

But Matos has no concerns over Stewart's fitness record, saying: "I think when you sign Ross you need to understand his history, his journey as a player.

"That's why you have a medical team behind and you have fitness coaches who can really understand. Now it's up to us to take the best out of him. We are really happy that we can count on him."

Though he is injury-free, Stewart will not be considered for Swansea's season-opening EFL Cup tie against Birmingham City on Saturday (15:00 BST) because he has not had a pre-season.

Vipotnik is also short of full fitness after a quad problem, meaning Idah is likely to start up front against the Blues.

title: BBC NI to remain home of Irish Premiership coverage
description: BBC Sport NI agrees a new three-year broadcast deal with the Irish FA and Northern Ireland Football League to ensure the continuation of extensive free-to-air coverage of international and domestic football across BBC iPlayer, online, radio and TV.
fullText:
BBC Sport NI has agreed a new three-year broadcast deal with the Irish FA and Northern Ireland Football League to ensure the continuation of extensive free-to-air coverage of international and domestic football across BBC iPlayer, online, radio and TV.

The new deal means BBC Sport NI will show 30 live Boyle Sports Premiership streams per season - starting with Friday night's north Belfast derby between Cliftonville and Crusaders - as well as 10 senior Women's Northern Ireland international matches and action from domestic cup competitions.

Finals of the Clearer Water Irish Cup and BetMcLean Cup will be shown live on BBC television and BBC iPlayer, as well as streamed coverage of games in the former competition from the fifth round onwards.

Live coverage of the Irish Premiership will also continue on BBC Radio Ulster and BBC Sounds, while highlights from NIFL and Irish Cup games will be available across BBC platforms.

This follows confirmation that BBC Sport NI will broadcast every Northern Ireland senior men's international until June 2028.

"This new agreement strengthens our longstanding commitment to bringing audiences the very best coverage of the game in Northern Ireland, from national teams to domestic league and cup competitions," said Neil Brittain, the executive editor of BBC Sport NI.

"Through BBC iPlayer, digital platforms, television, radio and BBC Sounds, we will continue to make local football available to the widest possible audience."

Steven Mills, NIFL Chief Operations Officer, said: "We are delighted to extend our contract with BBC Sport NI and sincerely thank them for their continued commitment and significant investment in our game.

"Their coverage has played a major role in raising the profile of the Premiership, increasing its reach and supporting the continued growth of the league."

Colin McKendry, Irish Football Association President said: "We are delighted that the Clearer Water Irish Cup, our flagship domestic cup competition, and Northern Ireland senior women's international matches will continue to be showcased on BBC Sport NI.

"Their coverage has played a significant role in raising their profile reaching new audiences and inspiring more people to engage with football across Northern Ireland.

"Alongside them and our partners at NIFL, this agreement will ensure supporters have even more opportunities to watch, follow and enjoy the game, while helping to grow the sport at every level."

title: National League returns - can it live up to last season's drama?
description: The National League kicks off on Saturday with a lot to live up to following the most dramatic end to the 2025-26 campaign.
fullText:
It is 104 days since the National League's regular season concluded with one of the most dramatic finishes to an English league season.

The top two, Rochdale and York City, met with the title and sole automatic promotion spot still on the line.

An afternoon oozing with tension ended with both sides exchanging goals deep, deep, deep into injury time as first Dale and then the Minstermen were left celebrating and holding the trophy.

The National League provided one of the stories for many a year, with a moment to go alongside those created by Michael Thomas and Sergio Aguero in the annals of the most dramatic climaxes to a league campaign.

Now with the 24 teams of the National League ready and raring to go on Saturday to kick off their 2026-27 campaign, how can it possibly top last season's drama?

Rochdale eventually secured the second promotion spot at Wembley in the play-off final after coming from two goals down to equalise in injury time and then beat Boreham Wood on penalties in another drama-filled afternoon.

With the undoubted two best sides having departed, it will leave plenty of others fancying their chances of promotion to the EFL.

In other leagues and other seasons, a total of 95 points would have been enough for Carlisle United to claim promotion.

But against very stiff competition, they came up short in the regular season in finishing third and then in the play-offs with a disappointing home loss to Boreham Wood.

Mark Hughes could not restore them to League Two at the first attempt and so they begin an unprecedented second consecutive term at this level.

The Wales legend departed Brunton Park this summer with Rob Elliot making a journey first made famous by Roman emperor Hadrian in coming across from Gateshead. Elliot is under no illusions about what is expected from Carlisle this season - promotion, preferably of the automatic variety.

Former Newcastle United goalkeeper Elliot has been replaced on Tyneside by ex-Sunderland man Lee Cattermole, who will cut his managerial teeth with the Heed.

As Carlisle try to return to where they believe they belong, Boreham Wood are chasing new territory.

But as Luke Garrard's side showed last term in being seconds away from League Two, they are an excellent footballing side.

Winger Abdul Abdulmalik is being coveted by clubs higher up the pyramid, while in centre-half Chris Bush and forward Matt Rush, they have two more of the stand-out players in the division.

Southend United's past two seasons have both ended at Wembley, with play-off defeat to Oldham Athletic in 2025 and FA Trophy glory over Wealdstone almost three months ago.

They are used to drama in Essex, but club legend Kevin Maher has departed the managerial hot-seat to be replaced by ex-Newcastle and England midfielder Kieron Dyer for his first full-time manager/head coach position.

The fact that the Shrimpers dispensed with Maher only two days after that Wembley success suggests that a sixth-placed finish, albeit 27 points behind champions York, was not good enough for a club averaging a league-best attendance of 8,103, so Dyer will need to hit the ground running.

As Southend begin their sixth season at this level since EFL relegation, it is a fourth for Hartlepool United.

The previous three have been the height of mediocrity in terms of finishes (12th, 11th, ninth), but there is genuine optimism for the new season.

After a long sought-after takeover by American Landon Smith in January, Pools have appointed Lee Clark as manager and have busily brought in proven National League performers as they aim to challenge for the play-off places and higher.

Forest Green Rovers have been play-off losers for the past two seasons and Robbie Savage will again bring his colour to the touchline as he looks to build on a solid first campaign at the club, finishing seventh last season.

Scunthorpe United showed they are going in the right direction again in claiming fifth place after promotion back from National League North. Those two clubs will expect to be in the mix again come April.

Barrow and Harrogate Town were promoted together from the National League in 2020 and, in a remarkable act of symmetry, have each returned after a six-year stay in League Two, during which time neither side ever convinced that they were there for good.

Harrogate go again under manager Simon Weaver, while it has been all change at Barrow after a truly dreadful season in which they went through five bosses and propped up the 92 Premier League and EFL clubs.

Adam Murray was recruited by Barrow after winning promotion with Kidderminster Harriers and tasked with rebuilding and restoring pride at Holker Street. The club has changed colours to mark its 125th anniversary and is keen to bring positivity back after a difficult couple of years.

National League North duo Fylde and Kidderminster are back at this level after one and two seasons away, respectively, but this is completely new territory for Worthing and Hornchurch as they prepare for their first season of fifth-tier football.

They will be new opponents for many and that unknown quantity could take them far. While in Adam Hinshelwood, Worthing have a boss who guided York to second spot and 96 points in April 2025 only to miss out in the National League play-offs.

Worthing and Hornchurch may be newcomers, but at least they have stability. That cannot be said for regulars Woking, who parted company with Jermain Defoe a fortnight ago.

They are still without a permanent boss after a messy saga involving the former England striker, who left after four months and described the experience as "eye-opening". The club later responded.

It may be the fifth tier and away from the spotlight but it does not mean it cannot throw up plenty of its own soap operas and melodramas.

The National League's 3UP campaign remains ongoing and the events of last season demonstrated lots of footballing merit as to why the league deserves a third promotion spot up to League Two, even if genuine questions remain about financial regulations and restrictions.

Instead it remains a hot topic of discussion with only two promotion spots on offer.

The average number of points to win the league (and the only automatic promotion spot) over the past five seasons has been 102.6, demanding high standards, while in the past four seasons, the highest-placed team not to go up has then won the league 12 months later.

The play-offs will again feature teams placed between second and seventh with two eliminators and two semi-finals (all over one leg) with the winner of the play-off final at Wembley securing the second promotion spot.

And whichever two teams will be celebrating promotion next spring, it will have been a campaign to savour following a nine-month slog.

The National League may have lost the Cornish outpost of Truro City this season and the European-esque road-trips down the A38 to the south-west tip of England, but the geographical slog remains.

With clubs as far apart as Carlisle in the far north west, Gateshead in the north east and Eastleigh and Worthing in the far south, every team will encounter plenty of Friday afternoons and the early hours of Wednesday and Thursday mornings sampling the delights of the motorway network.

Just for good measure, the season kicks off this weekend with five clubs embarking on epic round trips of over 400 miles.

Worthing are making the longest journey of the entire season, a whopping 744 miles round trip up to the edge of Scotland as they travel to Brunton Park to face Carlisle.

The opening day will therefore offer The Rebels a sample of exactly what footballing and logistical challenges are needed to succeed in the gruelling National League.

title: Stanway boosts Thistle promotion bid - watch live on BBC
description: Mark Wilson believes the aim of returning Partick Thistle to the Scottish Premiership was a huge factor in Ben Stanway signing a surprise new contract as Livingston visit in Friday's live BBC Scotland match.
fullText:
Mark Wilson believes the aim of returning Partick Thistle to the Scottish Premiership was a huge factor in midfielder Ben Stanway signing a surprise one-year deal to stay at the club.

The 21-year-old had been widely expected to leave Firhill in the summer after a standout campaign of 12 goals last term.

Thistle narrowly missed out on promotion, losing out to St Mirren in the play-off final.

"He wants to be part of something special here at Thistle," said manager Wilson.

"He's been here since he was 11, so 10 years at the club.

"In his tenth year, if he can get promotion, it would really be the icing on the cake for him."

The academy graduate was linked with moves to various Premiership clubs throughout last season, with Wilson describing his exit as practically a "foregone conclusion" back in January.

But the Thistle boss is delighted with the turn of events.

"His performances were so eye-catching, of course there was going to be interest," said Wilson. "If I'm being truthful, I was resigned to probably losing him.

"But we always kept ourselves in with a chance, by keeping in constant dialogue with him – particularly [assistant manager] Alex Rae. As time progressed that window of opportunity opened a wee bit."

The Glasgow side are at home to fellow promotion hopefuls Livingston on Friday - live in front of the BBC Scotland cameras – after an opening weekend 1-0 victory away to Greenock Morton.

Wilson is hopeful Stanway can further enhance his credentials by helping take Thistle back to the top flight for the first time since 2018.

"He's got a song about him from the fans as well; it's not often you get that," added Wilson.

"He just felt an absolute connection with this club and a drive to help Partick Thistle out of this division.

"That's testament to the lad. He's got a real purpose and determination about him that our young players - and even our experienced ones - can learn from."

title: Scottish summer malaise continues but some room for optimism
description: Supporters and former Hibs player Scott Allan react to a mixed night for Scottish clubs in Europe.
fullText:
The Scottish football summer malaise continued with a disappointing night for two Premiership clubs, while two others at least did their best to boost the mood.

Following on from a disappointing World Cup for fans north of the border, it was a mixed start to European qualifying last midweek as Hearts dropped down from the Champions League to the Europa League qualifiers but Hibernian and Motherwell progressed in the Conference League.

However, it was mostly a struggle this week as Hearts sustained another heavy away defeat, this time against Benfica, while Rangers entered the Europa League and stumbled to a 2-1 loss to Jagiellonia Bialystok in Poland.

Hearts look bound for the Conference League play-off round and Rangers could join them if they cannot turn around their tie at Ibrox next Thursday.

On a more positive note, Hibernian built a 2-1 lead over Shkendija to take to North Macedonia while Motherwell picked up a potentially valuable 1-1 draw against HJK Helsinki in Finland.

Old habits haunt Rangers in early McInnes tenure

New Rangers manager Derek McInnes said he had witnessed "a lot of what I thought Rangers were last season" and supporters agreed.

Peter: I'm sorry but I don't see anything to get excited about after two games. The talent on the bench and the lack of talent on the pitch sums up a lot for me. This is going to be a long season.

Joseph: We need to give this man time and resources. The constant merry-go-round is not helping the club. We need a new defence - time and time again the players we have in that position are found wanting. Let the man rebuild this great club and return us to the top of Scottish football where we should be. He needs patience at a difficult time for everyone involved with club - fans, players and coaches.

Paul: It's a case of deja vu again for this Rangers side. Carrying on from their failings last season, not only domestically, but in Europe too. It's going to be a long and winding road ahead if they can't beat a relatively poor and inexperienced side in Jagiellonia, albeit away from home. The only real positive note was the performance of the inspirational Findlay Curtis in the second half, but more work has still to be done at Ibrox in the return leg if they have any aspirations of salvaging this tie and progressing further in the tournament.

John: The loss of soft goals and a worrying lack of midfield creativity once again. Seems to be a recurring theme from last season that we fall behind to teams who then sit in, and our response is to just lump hopeful balls into the box, looking for a lucky break. Surely we should be better than this. We need to be.

Tom: The subs helped but the slow pace made us easy to defend against. Curtis was the main point of attack but we continually passed the ball out to Ross McCrorie so he could transfer it back to the left. Felt we kept Thelo Aasgard and Youssef Chermiti on for too long as both were poor. I expect us to struggle badly against Hibs.

Billy: What a big disappointment. The starting line-up was questionable. We signed a goalscorer in Lawrence Shankland, make him captain and then don't start him in a game we need to score. Nico Raskin should have been on from the start. It will need to be some improvement next week if we are to get through.

As for Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken, he lamented a first-half collapse in their 6-1 first-leg defeat in Lisbon.

However, some fans saw grounds for optimism.

Paul: We probably deserved to be 3-0 down at half-time, but the final scoreline felt harsh and arguably flattered a fabulous Benfica side. I'm proud of how our lads fought back in the second half with gutsy, attractive play and a great goal but sadly conceding two late goals undermined the much improved competitiveness shown after having moved to a back three. I was encouraged by what I saw, especially after half-time, but we simply must stop gifting soft goals to opponents.

James: We expected to get thumped but there were some good performances from our players last night too. Calvin Miller, Beau Reus, Josh McPake and Tom Renaud all had good games. Benfica are a class team and great to watch. Next we have to concentrate on our league form but these games are great for getting the team together and getting up to full fitness for the season ahead.

Maxwell: I have, like many others, been hyper critical of Wouter Vrancken because we expect too much from a new manager/style of play and a bunch of lads sought out by algorithms. Yes, it's painful, and it will continue to be painful, but if our new manager learns quickly, and I think he will, and gets rid of the dead wood, we all know who they are, maybe at the end of the year we will have an exciting team to watch.

Calum: Dundee United on Sunday really is a must-win for confidence now. There are some definite improvements to be made but, all told, could we as a fanbase please bear in mind that we've just played some Champions League regulars?

Lewis: Outclassed but mostly our own doing. Players doing stupid things inside the penalty area with no accountability proves we are missing a leader within the team. If nothing changes soon, we are in trouble.

Steve: We defend like a Sunday league team in stages and it's decimating our confidence. I cannot believe how far this team has fallen from last season and it's time to admit the Wouter Vrancken experiment will not work. We are so vulnerable in defence and tactically I genuinely worry for this team.

Hibs fared best of the Scottish clubs but fans were a little disheartened.

David: A tough watch but got the win in the end. We lack creativity in the midfield without Jamie McGrath and need more direct wingers. I feel the recruitment has thrown David Gray under the bus this summer.

Lee: I feel that a run of results will be good for this squad. Gray needs this because at the moment Hibs fans are being guilty of showing signs of impatience, even when the team are on top. Fans are correct to have high expectations but they need to know when it is time to support and when it's time to bring out the booing. Last night some of the support were guilty of being edgy and this only feeds on to the pitch and impacts players negatively.

Kev: Another scruffy performance from Hibs but a win is a win. Gray has to get more out of this group of players or his time at Easter Road will end very quickly.

Scott: For such an important game the team was flat and lacklustre in the first half. Hibs were in 'don't lose' mode as usual. The second half showed improvement but we were fortunate to come away with a victory. We are a dreadful watch.

Gordon: No intensity, no pace, no urgency, excruciatingly slow in the build-up and constantly passing across the back four. Eye bleeding at times. Gray has to get them to improve all areas mentioned above and get them playing with much more urgency or he's going to find himself under severe pressure.

Kieron: Yes we won but the performance was really poor. There's a huge gap in that midfield, I was seeing players getting frustrated because they were looking up wanting to pass but no-one was showing for it, so instead we had to hit it long, which meant we lost the ball a lot. It's as if they're playing like they've never played with each other before.

As for Motherwell, their unbeaten start to the season continued, with their supporters buoyant.

James: Not a bad performance at all. The pitch looked poor. We looked good in possession but our weakened squad showed towards the end. Still, we're unbeaten, and have a great chance next week but let's take care of Falkirk first. We still really need an out-and-out goalscorer.

Gilbert: Brilliant result, can't wait for the home game, should be a cracking match.

Alan: This is an excellent result and a fantastic building block for the next game. It is only half-time but plenty to play for. It's particularly pleasing to see the manager giving the younger players time on the pitch and the whole approach by the manager (and players) is to be applauded.

James N: Another great result for the team. The manager is so confident and it brings out the best in the players. Onward to next week, let's get a great result.

Gary: Great result but the job is only half done. We need a massive crowd at Fir Park to hopefully inspire the team to a massive tie against Freiburg. Alfred Johansson has made a great start.

David: It's a reflection of the game in Scotland that we hail a European draw in Finland. Let's take it, though, and ensure we do the business in the return leg at Fir Park. Freiburg await and with it great possibilities.

Former Hibernian midfielder Scott Allan on BBC's Scottish Football Podcast:

There's still a lot to play for in the ties outside Hearts, which was was always going to be a big ask. Yes, we can talk about Scottish teams in Europe, but Benfica are one of the most elite teams in Europe. You look at some of the players they bring through year on year.

Rangers, on the other hand, I still feel they'll come through that tie. No point messing about, it was a really poor performance on and off the ball again.

Hibs proved they could show some good European performances last season, I think they'll be able to do that and come through the tie. So not all doom and gloom.

title: Uefa boycott right thing for future of game - Bronze
description: England international Lucy Bronze says a Uefa boycott of Fifa competitions would be the "right thing" for the future of the game.
fullText:
England defender Lucy Bronze says a Uefa boycott of Fifa competitions would be the "right thing" for the future of the game, despite the impact it could have on women's football.

After Fifa president Gianni Infantino announced a plan to sell stakes in competitions to private investors, European football's 55 member associations voted to boycott all Fifa competitions until the proposals were dropped.

The plans have since been aborted - with Infantino apologising for his "errors" - but in a statement on Thursday, Uefa said the boycott could still go ahead.

Women's football would be the first to be impacted if Uefa's stance is upheld, with the Fifa Under-20 Women's World Cup due to start on 5 September.

Six European teams - England, France, Italy, Portugal, Spain and hosts Poland - are scheduled to play in the tournament.

"I think the players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game," said Bronze, who was speaking in New Zealand on Chelsea's pre-season tour.

Mexico break ranks to join Argentina in backing Infantino

Infantino sorry for errors but stays Fifa president

She added: "And if that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen.

"It's for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow.

"It's for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they're in a good place when the game's moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow."

In October, England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland all have qualifiers for next summer's Women's World Cup in Brazil.

Should they not feature in the play-offs because of Uefa's boycott, European teams - including defending champions Spain - would not be able to participate in the tournament, which starts in June.

Also in October, the Under-17 Women's World Cup is scheduled to take place in Morocco.

Speaking to BBC Sport last week, former England defender Anita Asante said: "The first casualties will be women's football tournaments.

"If this isn't resolved by the time of England's qualifiers, then the impact could be huge and it is already a busy schedule."

Baroness Campbell, former Football Association director of women's football, said it was "tragic" that women's football could be first to be affected.

The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino, while Wales, Albania and Croatia are among other individual associations to have turned their back on the 56-year-old.

title: Caldentey embraces 'cool' pressure as Arsenal target Treble
description: Midfielder Mariona Caldentey explains why Arsenal, strengthened by seven new players, are talking up their chances of winning the Treble this season.
fullText:
Mariona Caldentey has won four Champions Leagues, six Spanish titles, six Spanish Cups, two Nations Leagues and a World Cup - but her eyes light up when discussing Arsenal's hopes of silverware in the upcoming 2026-27 season.

With the Gunners chasing a first Women's Super League title since 2019, along with two domestic cups and another Champions League, she is explicit about what she expects.

"We have to do it - now it has to be our time."

The last time Caldentey, 30, was spotted in an Arsenal shirt was in May, standing on an open-top bus as part of the men's and women's victory parade around north London.

Hundreds of thousands of supporters lined the streets to celebrate a first Premier League title in 22 years for the men, with Caldentey and her team-mates also showing off the inaugural Women's Champions Cup they won against Brazilian side Corinthians in February.

It was a prize to cherish last season but, having finished second in the WSL and had their Champions League defence ended by an 87th-minute Lyon winner in their semi-final second leg, the Spain midfielder wants to put things right this season.

"We need to take the next step and are ready for it," she said. "We need to be ambitious, have no fear and believe in ourselves.

"That does not mean we are going to win it - there are other things that we cannot control, but that's the message.

"We are professional athletes at a big club and we have to deal with pressure. We accept it and I think it's a cool part of the job."

Boss Renee Slegers is equally bullish about Arsenal's targets for this season and is expecting her players to deliver.

"We are in a really good place," she told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "We need to be bold and explicit - we want to win the Women's Super League, and, of course, the Treble."

Last season, Arsenal won only four of their first nine games. By contrast, eventual champions Manchester City recovered from losing their opening match at Chelsea to rattle off 13 straight wins and seize control of the title race.

Replicating such a start will leave Arsenal's dreams of a first WSL title in eight seasons in tatters - and it could not be much tougher, with early trips to Stamford Bridge and Etihad Stadium.

They also travel to Brighton who they lost against in the FA Cup quarter-finals in April and who, a month later, held them 1-1 to guarantee City the title.

However, after the novelty of a full pre-season, Slegers is confident of a faster start this time.

"Some players haven't had that since 2017, 2018, and you can see that," she said. "They come back with so much energy, so much excitement.

"I think honestly they've been decompressing, recharging. Sometimes you understand what you're missing when it's not there. I think that's what the players have gone through so you can really feel the excitement to do something."

This summer, Slegers has strengthened her hand with seven new players, including full-back Ona Batlle, Caldentey's compatriot, and England dynamo Georgia Stanway to stiffen midfield.

Caldentey says Arsenal came up short last season through inconsistency and hopes the signings will help overcome that hurdle.

"We have shown amazing moments and amazing games and others where we haven't been good enough," she said. "That happened too many times last year. It was painful.

"We have added a lot of quality and that will help us."

With players such as two-time Ballon d'Or winner and fellow Spaniard Alexia Putellas arriving in the WSL, down the road at London City Lionesses, Caldentey accepts the league is getting tougher.

"It is a really attractive league," she said. "What you see and experience here, you don't get in other places. There are never any easy games.

"You want to play against the best - that's the challenge as a player and the quality here is really high."

And any observer would count Caldentey as among the very best.

In two seasons at Emirates Stadium, she has won WSL Player of the Season, come second in the 2024-25 Ballon d'Or and made the WSL Team of the Year both times.

During that period, her role has evolved from forward to midfielder and yet, despite that, only Alessia Russo has scored and assisted more for Arsenal.

"You have to adapt to what the team needs," she said. "Last year, I played a different role, closer to our defensive line. I was not used to it but these things make you grow.

"I do things better now than a year ago. Of course I enjoy playing higher up where you can be more creative and more risky but whatever my coach or team needs, I'll do it."

Her manager has stated clearly her team needs trophies. Caldentey is steeling herself to deliver.

The making of Spain and Arsenal's humble magician

'Not often you can write Arsenal history' - Gunners win Champions Cup

From Monday, 10 August, listen to an Arsenal special on the Women's Football Weekly podcast. Find interviews with Georgia Stanway, Renee Slegers, Lotte Wubben-Moy and more on the Women's Football Weekly feed.

title: 39 moves across five countries - football's ultimate journeyman
description: As he prepares to manage in the FA Cup for the first time, Zeph Thomas tells BBC Sport about his extraordinary career path spanning 39 moves in 18 years.
fullText:
"If I didn't get the money I thought I deserved, I'd be off," says Zeph Thomas, as he attempts to explain a career path that has spanned an extraordinary 39 moves in 18 years.

The Bradford-born winger, 36, is one of football's ultimate journeymen.

Rossington Main (five spells), Mickleover Sports (four spells), Frickley Athletic (three spells), Garden City Broncbusters (United States), Montegnee (Belgium), Thunder Bay Chill (Canada).

Thomas' list of former clubs goes on and on.

Cowdenbeath, Boston United, Harrogate Town, Scarborough Athletic, Stafford Rangers, Leek Town.

Ilkeston Town, Matlock Town, Goole, Glossop North End, Stocksbridge Park Steels, Brighouse Town (two spells), Emley, Harrogate Railway Athletic, Sheffield, Shaw Lane, Belper Town, Parkgate, Campion, Eccleshill United, Selby Town and Ossett United.

But could Thomas' life on the move be over?

The former St Kitts & Nevis international has embraced his player-manager role at ninth-tier South Yorkshire club Dearne & District since being appointed in 2024.

After winning the Northern Counties East League First Division last season, the village club based in Goldthorpe, near Barnsley, play their first ever FA Cup match on Saturday when they visit Runcorn Town - one of 219 extra preliminary round ties scheduled to take place.

"We've gone from being in the Doncaster Saturday League in 2021 to playing in the FA Cup," adds Thomas.

"It's massive for the area because they have never seen this team play in the competition."

Where & when? This weekend's FA Cup extra preliminary round fixtures

Thomas' career started at Rotherham United when former Manchester United forward Mark Robins was youth team coach.

He was released in 2008 without making a senior appearance, a decision that did not come as a complete surprise to him.

"I was a bit petulant and naive back then," he says.

"I remember scoring in a reserve game and then the next day we had to come in for recovery runs. At the time, I didn't think I should have been doing any of that.

"If my attitude had been better I would probably have been fine to be honest."

With his dreams of making it big in the full-time game shattered, Thomas embarked on a remarkable journey across non-league football in England, while there were spells at clubs in Kansas, Ontario, Scotland and Belgium.

In 2013-14 alone, he was on the books of Sheffield, Mickleover Sports, Scarborough Athletic, Matlock Town and Goole, while he started 2016-17 back at Mickleover Sports and then went to Shaw Lane, Stafford Rangers, Frickley Athletic... before ending back at Mickleover.

The non-league club where he spent his longest spell was Brighouse Town (second stint) between 2020 and 2023.

While at Stocksbridge Park Steels, he played against Jamie Vardy, then at Halifax Town, before Vardy went on to play for England and win the Premier League with Leicester City in 2015-2016.

In 2013, Thomas almost quit playing after suffering a groin injury. He worked in a call centre in Rotherham and thought about joining the army before being given an opportunity to resume his career at Thunder Bay Chill in Ontario.

Has he kept a record of his numerous destinations?

"Not at all. There's definitely been too many to count," adds Thomas.

"It's been a good experience but it could have been better. I moved up or went sideways for more money.

"But playing in different countries was a great experience and I would encourage all young players to go and experience that if they get a chance.

"I worked under different coaches with different ideas and philosophies."

Zeph Thomas: The unknown local player set to feature on the international stage

From international debut to call centre in five months

After a life spent seemingly on the road, Thomas does not have so far to travel to games these days.

He lives a five-minute walk from Dearne & District's ground, with wife Marie and their two children, Jerome, 11, and Lucia, seven.

Thomas combines his part-time job with Dearne & District, who attracted a crowd of 453 for the home league game with Penistone Church on 28 July, with his role as lead coach for Derby County's Under-12s.

He is still registered to play for the non-league club but these days prefers to coach from the dugout and pass on his experience to players.

"Sometimes I feel a bit of a hypocrite because I used to move clubs for extra money," he says.

"Now I say to my players, 'keep on doing what you're doing because the money will come'."

title: Sullivan expected to ignore safety advice and attend West Ham game
description: David Sullivan is expected to attend Saturday's EFL Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth despite being advised to stay away from home matches at the London Stadium.
fullText:
West Ham are expecting David Sullivan to attend Saturday's Carabao Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth despite him being advised to stay away from home matches at London Stadium.

Sullivan, 77, resigned from his position as co-chair of West Ham in June after a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times revealed that seven women have accused Sullivan of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.

He has categorically denied the allegations.

On Monday, a spokesperson for London Stadium told BBC News it had "recommended" to West Ham that Sullivan does not attend matches because of concerns about fan unrest.

London Stadium has asked for advance notice of any planned visits by major shareholder Sullivan - who retains a 38.8% stake in the club - in order to implement additional safety and operational measures.

The match against Portsmouth will be the first the club has played since the allegations against Sullivan were first reported.

The Panorama and Times joint investigation also revealed that Sullivan has been banned from contact with West Ham's women's and youth teams for the past three years because of safeguarding concerns.

London Stadium was unaware of the restrictions until the BBC's report.

Sullivan was banned after a historical allegation about his conduct was raised with the Football Association in 2023. He has previously said the allegation was false.

Sullivan had already been the subject of intense fan abuse for his running of the club, who were relegated to the Championship last season for the first time since 2011.

Although West Ham have stabilised on the pitch, with key figures, including manager Nuno Espirito Santo and skipper Jarrod Bowen committing their future to the club, there remains huge uncertainty off it.

Vanessa Gold, daughter of Sullivan's late business partner and former West Ham co-chair David, backed out of a deal to sell part of her stake in the club to Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky, and instead reached an agreement with Amanda Staveley, the public face of the Saudi Arabia-backed takeover at Newcastle, to sell her entire 25.1% stake.

However, Kretinsky has since sold a small part of his own stake, bringing him under 25%.

That would allow him to buy Gold's shares under West Ham's pre-emption rights rules - which allow existing shareholders first choice to buy shares when they become available.

If he did so he would become West Ham's biggest shareholder, without triggering another clause that would force him to then buy the rest of the club.

It is anticipated Saturday's match against fellow Championship side Portsmouth (15:00 BST) will set an attendance record for an EFL Cup first-round tie, with the Hammers having sold 55,000 season tickets for the new campaign.

title: Image created by 'Spygate' is far from truth - Eckert
description: Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert says he is "grateful" to owner Dragon Solak for backing him in the wake of the Spygate scandal.
fullText:
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert says he is "grateful" to have kept his job in the wake of the Spygate scandal but says the public's impression of events differs from reality.

Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs in May despite beating Middlesbrough in the semi-finals after being found guilty of spying on Boro while they were training.

They were also found to have spied on rivals on two other occasions and Eckert is currently awaiting the result of a Football Association investigation after being charged with misconduct for his role in the affair.

"The owner has the right to take consequences," Eckert told a fans' forum hosted by BBC Radio Solent.

"At that time it would have been right for me to accept they would go in a different direction."

Watch: BBC Radio Solent's Southampton FC Fans' Forum 2026

Eckert will be happy when FA reaches Spygate verdict

The German accused sections of the media of making him look worse than reality, but thanked Southampton's owner Dragan Solak for not being "swayed by public opinion".

Solak said in June he would not sack Eckert and the businessman was pictured in Germany with the squad during a pre-season training camp at the end of last month.

"There has been a lot out in the media and I haven't done a lot of interviews," Eckert said.

"There has been an image created that I think is very far away from the truth.

"If you have a chance to look behind the curtain, the image looks very different. It means a lot that the owner wasn't swayed by public opinion but looked at what actually happened.

"He [Solak] has taken his decision and I am very grateful for that."

title: Atletico Madrid in talks for Tottenham captain Romero
description: Atletico Madrid hold talks over a move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero, who is expected to leave the club this summer.
fullText:
Atletico Madrid have held talks over a move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international, who signed a new four-year deal at Spurs last August, is expected to leave the club this summer.

There has also been interest from Inter Milan in signing the 28-year-old, who played all seven matches in Argentina's run to the World Cup final last month, where they lost to Spain.

But Romero is a long-term target for Atletico manager Diego Simeone, with the Spanish side believed to be pressing ahead with another attempt to sign the centre-back.

Spurs are aware of Atletico's interest and an agreement on personal terms for the player will not be an issue.

Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi recently said he would "respect the will" of players if they wanted to leave.

Romero missed the end of last season with a knee injury as Spurs avoided relegation on the last day.

He was sent off twice last season as Spurs finished 17th.

Meanwhile, fellow centre-back Micky van de Ven is close to agreeing a new five-year deal with Tottenham.

title: Lewis-Skelly's chance to threaten Arsenal's big-name midfielders
description: Myles Lewis-Skelly broke into the Arsenal first team at left-back, but the teenager's preference has always been to play in midfield.
fullText:
It has never been a straightforward journey for Myles Lewis-Skelly into the Arsenal first team.

The 19-year-old's development has been rapid since his breakthrough in the 2024-25 season - he took his chance when injury was rife in the Arsenal squad to become one of the best young full-backs in the Premier League.

That form led to him breaking into the England squad and, in March 2025, Lewis-Skelly became the youngest man to score on England debut when he claimed the opener in a 2-0 win against Albania at Wembley.

A few months later, the academy graduate was rewarded with a new five-year contract.

What was most impressive about his breakthrough is that left-back is not even Lewis-Skelly's natural position.

The teenager came through Arsenal's Hale End academy as a midfielder and has always maintained that is his best position, even if the role of full-back provided him the platform to showcase his talents in the Gunners' first team.

The attributes that show why he was so highly rated during his time in the academy were easy to spot, even while starting in Arsenal's back four.

His ability to invert into midfield, protect the ball in tight spaces and burst away from opposition players are up there with some of the best in the division.

However, despite such a strong finish to his first campaign, last season was much more of a test for the teenager.

Defender Riccardo Calafiori, who Arsenal signed for £42m in 2024, regained his fitness and the Italy international's versatility and maverick nature when going forward plays such a big part in the team's attack.

Meanwhile, Mikel Arteta also brought in defender Piero Hincapie from Bayer Leverkusen on loan with an option to buy, which the club have now turned into a permanent deal.

With both players older and carrying more experience than Lewis-Skelly, minutes were hard to come by for the youngster.

Arteta said himself he had been "tough" on Lewis-Skelly.

But with Martin Zubimendi's performances fading towards the end of last season, Lewis-Skelly was finally given a chance to showcase his ability in midfield against Fulham - with four games of the Premier League campaign remaining.

His performance was so good that Lewis-Skelly then started all but one game in the end of season run-in, as Arsenal won the Premier League title and were beaten by Paris St-Germain in the Champions League final.

Arsenal players 'fuming' after sloppy Real Betis defeat

Arsenal have 'big hopes' for O'Neill - Arteta

Football in this era is as much about the business as it is about the game on the pitch and, with Lewis-Skelly an academy graduate, if the club were to sell him he would present "pure profit" on the balance sheet.

That is something that supporters do not like to hear, especially with a player who is one of their own and has such a bond with the club.

And that debate is something that Lewis-Skelly is aware of himself, writing the caption "pure profit" on a picture of himself with the Premier League trophy when Arsenal celebrated the title at Selhurst Park on the final day of last season.

Arsenal want to be a sustainable club and the transfer market encourages trading.

That is something that is greatly needed for the Gunners who, despite having room in their finances, have to think about selling after spending about £250m on new players last summer.

The club had considered listening to offers for Lewis-Skelly, but his excellent end to the season in his preferred central midfield position has been noted and that may have sparked a rethink over his status this summer.

It is important to note that the Gunners are moving closer to completing the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes for a fee which could be up to £80m - an arrival of that quality could put a barrier in front of Lewis-Skelly's route into the first team.

But Lewis-Skelly's talent, ability and history at Arsenal will always have him as a contender for game time, and this season could present him with a clear run at starting for the Gunners in midfield.

The World Cup's late finish and the number of Arsenal players involved in the tournament mean his competitors for a starting place are going to be behind him in match fitness.

Captain Martin Odegaard, England midfielders Declan Rice and Eberechi Eze as well as Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, who won the tournament with Spain, are all yet to join up fully with the Arsenal squad.

While Lewis-Skelly has started and impressed in pre-season friendlies against Girona and Real Betis, and the player is focused on working hard for his opportunities for in the upcoming campaign.

Against Betis he was at the base of the Arsenal midfield and looked assured with the responsibility he was given as the deepest-lying midfielder.

He showed his strength in bringing the ball upfield when Arsenal needed someone to progress play up the pitch.

He also linked up well with Calafiori, while Lewis-Skelly filled in at left-back when the Italian went on one of his adventurous runs forward.

"We just speak in the last few days about this connection that we have - we don't need to speak," Calafiori said of his partnership with Lewis-Skelly.

"I really like to play with him, a really good player."

The Community Shield against Manchester City is in just nine days' time and Lewis-Skelly looks as though he is going to have the chance to show why he should have been given the nod in the Arsenal midfield sooner.

title: Norrie saves match point in superb Montreal fightback
description: Britain's Cameron Norrie saves a match point as he produces a superb fightback to beat world number seven Alex de Minaur at the Canadian Open.
fullText:
Britain's Cameron Norrie saved a match point as he produced a superb fightback to beat world number seven Alex de Minaur at the Canadian Open.

Norrie was a set and 5-2 down against the Australian third seed before coming through 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1 to reach the fourth round.

De Minaur, leading by a double-break, had a match point on his own serve in the second set but double-faulted.

He twice served for the match but, at 5-4 up, double-faulted again to put the set back on level terms.

World number 37 Norrie edged the tie-break and then ran away with the deciding set to complete victory in two hours and 52 minutes.

"It was a great match to win and to test my level, and I can take so much confidence from this one," the 30-year-old said.

"The level was so high the first two sets.

"From the beginning, [de Minaur] came out firing and I had to match it."

Norrie - who reached the Los Cabos semi-finals last week - will face France's Arthur Fils for a place in the quarter-finals.

De Minaur's exit means that fifth seed Ben Shelton is the only top-10 men's player remaining in Montreal.

World number one Jannik Sinner and third-ranked Novak Djokovic withdrew before the tournament began, while top seed Alexander Zverev lost his first match.

Sixth-ranked Daniil Medvedev, seventh seed Taylor Fritz and world number nine Flavio Cobolli also all lost in the second round.

Tearful Draper struggles during comeback defeat

114 days and counting - how damaging is Alcaraz's wrist injury?
