title: African football backs FIFA’s Infantino
description: As other confederations abandon the FIFA president, Africa gives Infantino a lifeline.
fullText:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is leaning on Africa's 54-member voting bloc to survive the fallout from his failed $20 billion World Cup commercial rights plan, with staunch ally Morocco leading the charge.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF), led by South African billionaire Patrick Motsepe, said on Thursday its executive committee "unanimously reconfirmed its support" for Infantino, thanking him "for his support for African Football."

Four African members of the FIFA Council had previously issued statements backing Infantino after he abandoned the sale proposal last week.

Once reports of the proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup broke last month, three confederations — Asia, Europe, and North America — along with anger from world leaders and dissenting FIFA staff pushed Infantino to back down. Now, a pressure campaign challenging Infantino's leadership is gathering steam, with the continued threat of a European boycott looming.

The statement cements Africa's status as Infantino's most reliable large bloc — and narrows the odds his opponents can assemble a majority against him.

"I'm not surprised that they came out in support of Infantino," Algiers-based football journalist Maher Mezahi told Semafor. He said high ranking CAF figures owe their positions to Infantino.

Morocco's backing reflects a decade-long strategy to use football as diplomatic leverage, Mezahi said, pointing to Rabat's investment in stadiums, its hosting of CAF tournaments, and its status as host of the only FIFA office on the continent — which served as the site of Infantino's Wednesday crisis meeting.

Morocco will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Spain and Portugal, and reports suggest Infantino has offered Morocco the award of long-sought hosting rights for the tournament final over Spain in exchange for continued support ahead of March's presidential vote.

CAF chief Motsepe has called Infantino "loyal to Africa," with some officials citing FIFA funding — guaranteed at $8 million per association over four years — as central to their support.

However, Mezahi added that Africa's usual voting unity has a potential fracture point: Algeria, wary of Infantino's relationship with its rival Morocco, may break ranks in a shift that could pull Tunisia along with it. That regional rivalry, Mezahi said, could give Infantino's opponents an opening to peel off a handful of African votes even as CAF presents a united front publicly.

Morocco's football chief, Fouzi Lekjaa, is hoping his sporting success will translate into political capital. The longtime civil servant — who also serves as budget minister — joined the junior coalition partner Authenticity and Modernity Party in July and is widely expected to enter parliament in September's elections, putting him in a strong position to become the kingdom's next prime minister.

The North Africa country's next cabinet is already being dubbed the "World Cup government." This is on the assumption that Lekjaa's association with the Atlas Lions' recent success — most notably their historic run to the 2022 World Cup semifinals and a quarterfinal this year — will outweigh public frustration over the billions spent on new stadiums.

That raises the stakes of Rabat's FIFA lobbying. Morocco has every incentive to keep its close ally, Infantino, and by extension its relationship with FIFA, onside ahead of the 2030 World Cup as it heads into election season.

Spain's sports minister says her country 'deserves' to host the 2030 World Cup final, not Morocco.

title: Valkyries’ Gabby Williams “Welcomes” Trans Athletes After French Transgender Player Julie Tetart Shows Interest to Play in the WNBA
description: Golden State Valkyries’ Gabby Williams is positioning herself as the opposite of Sophie Cunningham, at least when it comes to her views regarding the inclusion of trans athletes in the WNBA. The Indiana Fever guard has positioned herself firmly against the idea of trans athletes joining the league, making national headlines in the process.
fullText:
Golden State Valkyries' Gabby Williams is positioning herself as the opposite of Sophie Cunningham, at least when it comes to her views regarding the inclusion of trans athletes in the WNBA.

The Indiana Fever guard has positioned herself firmly against the idea of trans athletes joining the league, making national headlines in the process. Williams, on the other hand, seems to welcome the idea:

"I think trans rights now is our new battle; that's where I think that I was saying, like, the battles have changed, you know? Like our intention has been the same, but like the environment has changed; we have seen trans people's rights stripped away from them. There's a lot of discourse around trans athletes and where they can compete in. I would welcome a trans athlete on my team or against my team any time. I don't think it's a problem in the world; it's just another way to kind of attack trans people," said Williams on Thursday during practice.

She also spoke about the possibility of French transgender athlete Julie Tetart, who plays for Monaco in Ligue Féminine 2, joining the WNBA after a breakout season. She praised her for breaking down barriers for other trans athletes.

On the USA Network's WNBA broadcast on Wednesday, Sophie Cunningham spoke about the trans discussion in the league, calling for stakeholders to be respectful of each other's opinions. Moreover, she expressed her discontent that the discussion around the league had lately been about everything but the sport:

"With that being said, I just hate how The W, the basketball of it all, is just getting overshadowed…It just makes me sad that all this sort of drama, on things that truly don't matter, that the basketball is getting overshadowed. My biggest thing is that love and respect, there is room for absolutely everybody, and we don't always have to agree, but that respect and love definitely has to be there."

The WNBA has been a significant part of national discourse over the last few months, not only because of the trans issue, but also due to members of the public calling for the league to better protect Cunningham's teammate, Caitlin Clark, whom they see as the target of harassment and discrimination by her fellow players.

title: Ex-NFL star ruthlessly exposes Caitlin Clark’s flaw that led to Chelsea Gray’s OT game-winner
description: Former NFL star reveals what Caitlin Clark’s ‘issue’ was against the Las Vegas Aces. Following an 86-84 overtime defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces, the Indiana Fever have now fallen to the sixth spot in the WNBA, as they now have a 19-12 record.
fullText:
Former NFL star reveals what Caitlin Clark's 'issue' was against the Las Vegas Aces.

Following an 86-84 overtime defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces, the Indiana Fever have now fallen to the sixth spot in the WNBA, as they now have a 19-12 record.

Speaking of the two-point defeat vs. the Aces, Chelsea Gray sealed the game with a stunning buzzer-beating game-winner. However, the play before that featuring Caitlin Clark has become the biggest talking point of the clash.

The Aces managed to nullify Clark's impact by holding her to 20 points on a 7-of-20 shooting night. Combine that with 8 turnovers, and it's a miracle that the Fever only lost by two points.

Coming to the controversial play before Gray's game-winner, former NFL player Emmanuel Acho broke it down on X, explaining how Clark hunting for a foul and not returning on defense helped the Aces win.

"The issue isn't with this turnover by Caitlin Clark (though she had 8). The issue is she didn't get her butt off the ground and SPRINT to get back in the play!" Acho wrote on X.

He added, "Clark could've blocked Gray's shot from behind or made her put the ball on the deck. She didn't even get back in frame!"

As Acho pointed out, Clark's lack of commitment on the defensive end of the floor gave the Aces a numbers advantage as the second-best team in the WNBA made the Fever pay for Clark's mistake.

title: 6 takeaways from Day 11 of Patriots training camp
description: Drake Maye had a solid day before the defense forced three straight turnovers in Mike Vrabel's 2-minute drill at Patriots training camp. Here's what happened
fullText:
FOXBOROUGH – It looked like the day would end on a high note for quarterback Drake Maye and the Patriots offense.

Instead, the team's defense turned the script on Day 11 of training camp.

Mike Vrabel had his team end Thursday's practice with a 2-minute drill. The coach had his two units line up on the field in a got-to-have-it situation. The offense needed a touchdown to win. The defense needed a stop to secure the victory.

Maye came out firing, hitting three passes in a row. His third completion was a thing of beauty, as A.J. Brown made a phenomenal catch against tight coverage from Christian Gonzalez. That set the offense up at the 25-yard line with 33 seconds on the clock.

However, that's where the good fortune for Maye and the offense ended.

On the next play, Maye tried to squeeze a pass into a tightly covered Kayshon Boutte. Cornerback Marcus Jones jumped in front of the receiver to make a nice interception. Vrabel gave the offense one more opportunity, but that too ended in a turnover as Maye tried to get the ball to a well-covered Hunter Henry.

In that instance, Kevin Byard intercepted the pass in the end zone.

The defense wasn't done, either. Tommy DeVito took the field to start his unit's 2-minute drill. The backup quarterback's first pass was intercepted by safety John Saunders, making it three interceptions in a row for the defense.

"Obviously we're trying to win the game," Boutte said. "So, three interceptions, whether we can't fully blame the quarterback, you know, we can take accountability on the routes, alignments and stuff like that. It's take all 11, not just one man, but as an offense we got to be better. You know, that's a game-winning situation. So if you go based on that scenario, we lost that game."

Patriots defensive players were buzzing after the three-straight turnovers.

"It shows what we have and all the stuff that we're just getting better every day, everybody making plays, new guys making plays every day," edge rusher Bradyn Swinson said. "So that's something that you love to see."

"We got head hunters," added defensive tackle Leonard Taylor. "Everybody wants the ball. Everybody's in the right spot when we need them to, and they're just executing their plays."

Here are the top takeaways from Day 11 of Patriots training camp:

The temperature wasn't the only thing rising on Day 11 of Patriots training camp.

This summer, the battle between A.J. Brown and Christian Gonzalez has been highly competitive. Both Pro Bowl players have had their shares of wins and losses against one another.

On Thursday, the competition ramped up and almost boiled over.

During a 1-on-1 drill, Gonzalez deflected a pass intended for Brown in the end zone. After the ball hit the grass, the Patriots cornerback pointed his finger at the receiver. It appeared as though both players were trash-talking. That's when receiver Kayshon Boutte came onto the field to pull Brown away.

"I was just trying to pull A.J. out to go on to the next," Boutte said. "I heard him say something about 'You a grown man'. So, I just (got in there) before it got too far."

The two players have gone back and forth all camp. The intensity has only increased since pads came on last week. On Monday, Gonzalez could be heard trash-talking about intercepting a pass intended for Brown in 1-on-1 drills. On Thursday, Brown made a phenomenal catch with Gonzalez in coverage during a 2-minute drill.

"It's good on good. He's the number one receiver in this league, going up against the number one corner," Gonzalez said. "I mean, that's how it's going to go. It's football at the end of the day; there's never no disrespect or anything. We're just battling and getting each other better.

Will Campbell's outstanding training camp came to a halt on Thursday.

The Patriots left tackle didn't participate in any competitive drills as he wore a new brace on his left arm. Backup Marcus Bryant played left tackle in Campbell's place. The second-year player said it was nice to be called upon with the starters.

"Just being able to step up and compete," Bryant said. "And being able to step in for my brother means a lot."

Campbell has been great this summer. The second-year tackle is 8-1 in 1-on-1 drills and has earned praise from teammates and coaches for his improvements from last season. However, Campbell was seen wearing a black brace on left his arm during Wednesday's walkthrough.

On Thursday, Campbell was out with his teammates during the start of practice and took part in some of the drills. When 11-on-11s started, Campbell worked off on the side field with Patriots head trainer Frank Piraino.

Campbell didn't take part in 1-on-1 drills, either. Bryant took those reps and performed well, going 2-0 against Dre'Mont Jones and Gabe Jacas.

The injury to Campbell bears watching. The 2025 fourth overall pick looks bound for a big second season, and the Patriots certainly need him.

Thursday's practice ended on a low note for Maye as he threw two interceptions on his final two passes. Up until that point, the quarterback was having a solid day of training camp.

Before the turnovers, Maye was an efficient 10-of-13 on the day before finishing 10-of-15 with two interceptions.

Before the 2-minute drill, the Patriots ran a red zone drill with the offense starting on the 5-yard line. Maye hit DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for touchdowns during that period.

Once again, Brown was Maye's top target. The Pro Bowl receiver finished with three catches.

Thursday was a lighter day for DeVito and Behren Morton. DeVito finished 3-of-6 with the interception. Morton finished 3-of-6 as well.

Romeo Doubs missed his second straight day of camp. The veteran receiver was a full participant before missing Wednesday's walkthrough.

Doubs' absence hasn't necessarily led to more opportunities for Boutte. On Thursday, the receiver lined up with both the starters and backups, but his only catch came on a pass from DeVito.

Boutte was targeted twice by Maye, but the first ball was overthrown and the second one intercepted.

After practice, he said he doesn't lobby for more first-team reps.

"I think everybody would like to have more first-team reps," Boutte said. "You might have 10 plays, you might have five, you might have 20, it's all about opportunity."

With Doubs absent, it's also been interesting to see how the depth chart has unfolded. On Thursday, Efton Chism III received the first first-team rep, lining up with Brown. Meanwhile, Kyle Williams continues to play with the second and third-string offenses.

On Thursday, Williams' only reception came on a pass from Morton with the third team.

The Patriots also missed cornerback Carlon Davis, tight end Jack Westover and receiver Cameron Dorner on Thursday. Harold Landry and Brenden Schooler also remain out.

Second-round pick Gabe Jacas is making up for lost time.

The rookie edge rusher saw more reps on Thursday. He mainly played with the backup defense, but did take a handful of snaps with the starters, replacing Dre'Mont Jones on a handful of reps.

Jacas took two reps in 1-on-1 drills, losing to Marcus Bryant and then beating rookie Demetrious Crownover. In full-team reps, Jacas decisively beat first-round pick Caleb Lomu on one pass-rushing rep.

In 11-on-11 drills, Jacas had a pressure before DeVito's interception.

It's been an up-and-down camp for the Patriots' first-round pick.

On Thursday, Lomu went 1-1 during the team's 1-on-1 period. The day was a good example of what's been happening with the rookie.

On the first rep, Lomu was beaten badly by backup edge rusher Xavier Holmes. However, the first-round pick rebounded and then beat Elijah Ponder on the next rep.

The last time the Patriots did 1-on-1 drills, Lomu went 3-3. The practice before that, he finished 2-2. It's been a mixed bag for the rookie.

title: Journalist: Liverpool Not Interested In Premier League Defender
description: Djed Spence Transfer Talk Leaves Liverpool Still Searching for Defensive BalanceLiverpool’s summer has acquired a familiar shape, one in which need is obvious, solutions appear briefly within reach,...
fullText:
Liverpool's summer has acquired a familiar shape, one in which need is obvious, solutions appear briefly within reach, and then recede just as quickly. The latest example is Alex Crook reporting that the club are not pursuing Djed Spence, despite the logic of the move appearing relatively straightforward from the outside.

Spence, at 25 and an England international, seemed to fit several of Liverpool's more immediate concerns. He offers cover at right back, where uncertainty remains, and can also operate on the left, a versatility that often becomes more valuable the deeper a season goes. In a squad with clear homegrown pressures and visible structural gaps, the appeal was easy to understand. At around £35m, the numbers looked manageable, too.

That is what makes this update feel significant. A sensible transfer is not always the right one, of course, but in Liverpool's current circumstances practicality ought to have some value. Modern squad-building is often described in the language of elite recruitment and market opportunities, yet title challenges are usually sustained by accumulation, by filling weak points before they become fractures.

There is a tactical dimension to this beyond mere depth. Liverpool are entering a new era under Andoni Iraola, and any head coach inheriting a side in transition requires players capable of absorbing varied demands. Full-backs, in particular, are no longer simple touchline runners. They are pressure valves, build-up options and defensive stabilisers. A player able to function on both flanks has obvious value in that context.

Even if Liverpool believe Conor Bradley can reclaim the right-back role, the season demands more than faith. Availability matters as much as talent. Jeremie Frimpong brings qualities of his own, though defensive security has hardly ceased to be a discussion point. On the opposite flank, depth is similarly open to question.

And this is where transfer windows are judged, not by the drama they generate but by the order they impose. Liverpool need reinforcement in defence, and perhaps beyond it. A centre-back, midfield support and attacking depth all have their place in the conversation, but the immediate sense is of a squad still awaiting basic repair work.

Spence may not have been the perfect answer. He may not even have been the preferred one. Yet if Liverpool decline that sort of solution, then what follows has to be persuasive, because the season is close and the margins at the top of English football are ruthlessly narrow.

From a Liverpool perspective, this report lands with a weary sort of familiarity. Djed Spence was never the sort of signing to set pulses racing, but that may have been precisely the point. Supporters can live without spectacle in the market if the squad starts to make more sense. Right now, it still does not fully make sense.

There is always the possibility that the club have a better plan. Recruitment departments do not, in fairness, operate according to public logic alone. They may see flaws in Spence's profile, or believe the money is better deployed elsewhere. If so, fine. But Liverpool have drifted into that dangerous territory where every sensible missed opportunity sharpens attention on what has not yet been fixed.

An unsure fan would probably say this is less about Spence himself and more about confidence in the process. If Liverpool pass on a player who looks useful, adaptable and reasonably priced, then supporters need to see the alternative quite quickly. Otherwise, the fear grows that obvious needs are being left to harden into recurring problems.

There is enough quality in the squad to compete, and Iraola is walking into a group with serious talent. But talent needs structure around it. At the moment, the concern is that Liverpool still look one or two practical decisions short of the balance required to navigate a long season properly.

title: ‘I Have More Fire In Me’ – Nabil Anane Turns Heartbreak Into Motivation At The Inner Circle 25
description: The former World Champion reveals how losing his belt reignited his passion at the highest level.
fullText:
Nabil Anane did not expect losing his ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Title to feel like a relief. But somewhere beneath the initial disappointment, that is exactly what it became.

The towering superstar gets a prime opportunity to work his way back toward that coveted crown when he faces three-division Lumpinee Stadium World Champion Suakim Pongsuphan PK in a high-stakes World Title eliminator at The Inner Circle 25.

The card broadcasts live in Asia primetime from Bangkok's iconic Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, August 7, exclusively for subscribers at live.onefc.com.

Understanding why relief and heartbreak could effortlessly coexist requires looking back at what unfolded at The Inner Circle 7 this past March. That night, Rambolek Chor Ajalaboon dethroned Anane to successfully capture the divisional gold in a highly technical five-round contest.

Rather than viewing the difficult outcome purely as a setback, the 6-foot-4 athlete has come to see it as exactly what his career needed.

"Actually, my mental is good. It lit a fire under me. It made me feel like I'm not stuck. Because when I was the champion, no challengers were calling me out, so it felt a bit stagnant.

"Honestly, I felt stagnant, and my drive went down. I still trained hard – I always train hard – but the fire just wasn't as bright. I think many people can understand that. Now that I'm not the champion anymore, I have a goal again. I have more fire in me."

While he has certainly found a silver lining, the Team Mehdi Zatout representative does not pretend the defeat came without emotional pain.

The result brought an end to an incredible nine-fight unbeaten run in the promotion — a spectacular stretch that included statement victories over ONE World Champions "The Kicking Machine" Superlek and "King of the North" Nico Carrillo, as well as former two-time Lumpinee Stadium Muay Thai World Champion "Left Meteorite" Ratchasiesan Laochokcharoen.

Even so, Anane keeps the athletic setback firmly in perspective, deeply aware that many people around the world are carrying far heavier burdens than a lost championship.

"Of course it was painful. It was very heavy. But it's just about Muay Thai. It's a minor thing compared to [other things]. I think no matter how bad off we are, there are always people who have it worse than us.

"I just lost my belt, but I still have a home to sleep in. My parents are waiting for me at home. The people I love are at home. I have food every night. I can eat whatever I want, and I sleep in an air-conditioned room. Some people don't even have a place to sleep. Their lives are much worse than ours."

Much like life beyond the global stage, adversity has a unique way of revealing true character.

The former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion treats his latest hurdle not as a step backward, but as just another necessary obstacle on his relentless road to greatness.

That mature mindset did not appear overnight. It is the direct product of a martial artist who has successfully weathered setbacks before, learning each time that the version of himself on the other side emerged even stronger.

"This defeat is like a test. That's what I think. If I can get through it, I will be stronger. We shouldn't overthink it. Perhaps it was something that was meant to happen. That's how I look at it. There were many factors, and I've reflected on myself and tried to learn from it.

"It's not my first loss. This one might hurt the most, but I've lost before, and I've always overcome it. Now that I'm older and more mature, why wouldn't I be able to make it better than before? I can definitely do it."

Talk of overcoming setbacks means little without dedicated action behind it, and Nabil Anane has spent the months since his World Title loss proving he means every single word.

Rather than chasing a complete stylistic overhaul, he has taken a much more introspective route. True growth, in his eyes, comes from understanding himself better, not from simply copying what has worked for someone else.

That measured, thoughtful philosophy now runs entirely through his elite preparation for Suakim.

"My training has changed. I understand my body much better. I'm not just blindly doing stuff. Sometimes you have to know your own body. Everyone has their own style and strengths. You can't just copy someone else. It's impossible. You have to master your own game.

"Sure, we can learn things that others are good at, but in the end, you have to adapt them to fit yourself. I'm constantly learning what works best for me and focusing on that. That goes for training and physical conditioning too."

Beyond the promise of a guaranteed World Title rematch against divisional king Rambolek, Anane is highly motivated to win back the hearts of the supporters who have grown a little quieter since his recent defeat.

Public perception can shift rapidly in combat sports, and the young star is well aware that a tough loss carries weight well beyond the official record book. Rather than dwell on that shift, he views Friday night as the perfect opportunity to completely reverse it.

"If I perform well, people will believe in me again. Right now, some people might have lost faith because they saw me lose in a bad way. But I will reclaim that faith and prove it to everyone."

Whether that happens immediately or not, Anane remains incredibly grateful simply to keep competing at his absolute best for the people who never left his corner.

At the end of the day, external validation has never meant too much to the Thai-Algerian standout. There is a much simpler, profound force driving everything he does on the global stage.

"My motivation is the people I love. I just want to make them happy, and I want to be happy alongside those I love and those who love me. That's all there is to it.

"In life, when you find something that makes you happy, you just stick with it. Then you share that happiness with the people you love and move forward together. It's as simple as that."

title: SDFC falls 3-1 to Club América in Leagues Cup opener at Azteca
description: SDFC drops its 2026 Leagues Cup opener, falling 3-1 to Club América at Estadio Banorte on Thursday night behind a Man-of-the-Match performance from Brian Rodríguez.
fullText:
SDFC drops its 2026 Leagues Cup opener, falling 3-1 to Club América at Estadio Banorte on Thursday night behind a Man-of-the-Match performance from Brian Rodríguez.

Final en Ciudad de México. pic.twitter.com/o60w1vAfyZ

A matchup against one of North America's most prestigious clubs, Club América, awaited San Diego FC as they traveled down to Mexico City to the historic Estadio Banorte, famously known as Estadio Azteca.

Thursday night's game marked SDFC's third match in Mexico, with the Chrome & Azul searching for their first victory south of the border.

The first half at Estadio Banorte all but sealed the game result, with Club América scoring three unanswered goals in the opening half.

Midfielder Brian Rodríguez was all over the first half, giving América the early lead in the 11-minute finishing off a carving dribble with a left-footed low-driven shot across goal and into the right-side netting.

¡Cómo la armó el Rayito! ⚡️

El uruguayo adelanta a las Águilas en casa en su debut en #LeaguesCup2026 🏆

Mira @ClubAmerica vs. @sandiegofc en @AppleTV 📺 https://t.co/MVPcF6a5l2 pic.twitter.com/NFimtOL1ef

Brian Rodríguez once again on another piercing dribble, then set up América's second score of the night in the 33-minute, with his pass into the goal area only needing the finishing touch from midfielder Érick Sánchez for the 2-0 lead.

¡Brian lo prepara y 'Chiquito' lo firma! Las Águilas ya lo ganan 2-0 en casa 🏟️🦅

Mira @ClubAmerica vs. @sandiegofc en @AppleTV 📺 https://t.co/MVPcF6a5l2 pic.twitter.com/eSn7EVyclY

América's third goal of the night came off the right-footed strike of forward Isaías Violante. With Brian Rodríguez providing his second assist of the night, Violante blasted his shot into the far right post and into the net for the 3-0 scoreline heading into the locker room break.

¡Violanteee! ¡Ya son 3️⃣ para las Águilas!

Mira @ClubAmerica vs. @sandiegofc en @AppleTV 📺 https://t.co/MVPcF6a5l2 pic.twitter.com/zTXTXZGA9w

One goal, two assists y baile para celebrar el triunfo en #LeaguesCup2026 😎

Brian Rodríguez is the Man of the Match pres. by GEICO 🔝 pic.twitter.com/pU3WXWUUi9

SDFC left the first half with the 58%-42% possession advantage, but it was América dominating the chance creation numbers, scoring three times through 12 total shots.

The Chrome & Azul pulled a goal back in the 63-minute, with defender Luca Bombino meeting a loose ball inside the penalty box and rifling his shot into the roof of the goal to make it a 3-1 scoreline.

LUCA BOMBINO PULLS ONE BACK 👏 pic.twitter.com/cGwPKObfbR

Although netting SDFC's first goal in Leagues Cup 2026, SDFC were held at that single score with the full-time whistle at Estadio Banorte finishing the match at 3-1, as San Diego FC fell to Club América to open their Leagues Cup campaign.

Thursday night's loss leaves SDFC still waiting for their first victory in Mexico, with their record on Mexican soil now reading 0-3, having lost to Pumas UNAM, Toluca and now Club América.

SDFC's remaining Phase One Leagues Cup matches shift to Snapdragon Stadium, hosting Baja Cup rivals Club Tijuana on Sunday night, Aug. 9, all set for a 7 p.m. kickoff.

The Chrome & Azul conclude Phase One play next Wednesday night, Aug. 12, against Club Puebla.

title: Jake Rogers nearly slips up after epic Red Sox debut following Tigers trade
description: Jake Rogers is still catching his bearings after a whirlwind week, which ended with a trade to the Red Sox, saw him get traded twice.
fullText:
Jake Rogers nearly slips up after epic Red Sox debut following Tigers trade appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Backup catcher Jake Rogers, acquired in the Adley Rutschman trade, had to step up and play a role for the Boston Red Sox on Thursday in their bonkers 12-11 win over the Chicago White Sox after 13 innings.

Connor Wong had to be replaced with a pinch-runner, thrusting Rogers into action in the 10th inning. Rogers ended up drawing a walk in the 10th to load the bases (he failed to score), and he then drove in the tying run in the 12th (via a sacrifice fly) to set up Caleb Durbin's heroics in the 13th.

After the game, Rogers expressed his feelings towards joining a scorching hot Red Sox team. In doing so, he slipped up and almost mentioned his former employer instead of his current one before catching himself.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"To see these guys perform the way they are, I mean, it's a fun group to be a part of and a great time to be in Detr — or, sorry, Boston. Caught myself there," Rogers said, via Tim Healey of the Boston Globe.

Rogers still might be in the process of gathering his bearings after an eventful trade deadline saw him move twice in the span of a week. Rogers went from the Detroit Tigers to the Baltimore Orioles and then to the Boston Red Sox finally, as he was included as a throw-in in the Rutschman trade.

He had spent the entirety of his career up to 2026 with the Tigers, and then he played just three games for the Orioles before he was dealt to the Red Sox. Rogers is expected to be the third-string catcher in Beantown once Rutschman returns, as one would think that Wong would be the one who will be taking on the backup role.

Rogers has a history of being a strong defensive catcher and he has shown that he can come up clutch for the Red Sox, so perhaps there's a role for him on the big-league roster even when Rutschman comes back from the injured list.

title: What Man United need in the transfer window: Top targets and players leaving before deadline day
description: Michael Carrick still needs some clarity on his squad before the season starts, both in terms of incomings and outgoings.
fullText:
What Man United need in the transfer window: Top targets and players leaving before deadline day originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Manchester United fans had hoped this summer transfer window would prove a roaring success, giving Michael Carrick a reinforced squad capable of building on his promising first few months in charge.

With less than three weeks left before deadline day, many supporters are disappointed.

United moved swiftly to address their problems in midfield, but what some had anticipated would be a complete overhaul of the middle of the team has instead turned into more circumspect, with uncertainty around any further additions.

There are also some concerns in attack and defence, plus the big question over what to do with Marcus Rashford.

However, it would be wrong to suggest United have made a hash of the window so far. Their spending, although limited, has been prudent, and there could yet be some fresh deals to come before the window closes on September 1.

MORE:Man United's preseason results and full schedule

United's two big arrivals to date are Andrey Santos from Chelsea, and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa.

Casemiro left on a free transfer after his contract expired, but departures on loan or permanently have otherwise been limited. Rasmus Hojlund completed a permanent move to Napoli in June after a clause in his loan deal was triggered by virtue of their qualification for the Champions League.

United's most desperate need when the window opened was to improve a midfield that had been further weakened by Casemiro's exit at the end of his contract and a serious knee injury to Manuel Ugarte.

There was a desire to strengthen in attack, most notably on the left wing, although this was of secondary importance to the spine of the team. Similarly, a new centre-back would have been a bonus, rather than a real area of focus.

There remains some interest in a new left-back to compete with Luke Shaw, and to replace him in the longer term, but this too was subject to the movement of the market. Senne Lammens has the goalkeeper jersey locked down, and Karl Darlow's arrival as an extra back-up means they can sell others.

A new centre-forward to compete with Benjamin Sesko, who has a nagging leg injury, would leave United in a much stronger position at the start of the season, but again, any such deal looks like one that depends on how the market develops over the next couple of weeks.

In terms of departures, a few fringe players will be moved on either on loan or permanent transfers, while some youngsters could be sent out to get some game time in short-term deals.

Much to the frustration of supporters, United do not appear to be actively pursuing specific names at this stage of the window. Rather, the policy appears to be to wait for opportunistic deals.

It is known that bringing in a third midfielder would be welcome, but there is no obvious sign of such a deal happening. Carlos Baleba is still occasionally linked but would appear to be less of a clear-cut target now. Things can obviously change late in the window, but right now, United appear content to go into the new season with Santos, Tielemans, Kobbie Mainoo and Mason Mount as their options in central midfield behind playmaker Bruno Fernandes.

United are said to admire Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall, but the big outgoings from St. James' Park this summer — they have already sold Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, with Bruno Guimaraes set to join Arsenal — mean the Magpies do not need the money. The Red Devils would have to offer a sizeable fee to tempt them to sell Hall now.

A few players are available for transfer, either on loan or permanent deals.

Two goalkeepers look set to depart. Altay Bayindir is poised to join Celta Vigo on loan with a buy option, while Radek Vitek, who impressed on loan at Bristol City last season, is signing for Middlesbrough. Fabrizio Romano reported that Vitek will leave for an initial £7 million ($9.4 million), with the fee potentially doubling through add-ons, while United retain both a buy-back and a 35 per cent sell-on clause.

Joshua Zirkzee could also be on his way out. Talks are ongoing with Juventus, who are keen to bring the striker back to Serie A. United would prefer a straight sale or a loan with an obligation to buy, having paid £36.5m ($49.2m) for the Netherlands international two years ago.

United may listen to offers for youngsters Harry Amass, Toby Collyer and Ethan Wheatley, who are unlikely to get first-team football this season. Wheatley is said to be a target for Everton.

It had seemed likely that Rashford would join Barcelona permanently after helping them win La Liga while on loan there last season. Instead, the Catalans chose not to take up the option to buy him for £26m ($35m) and signed Anthony Gordon from Newcastle for well over double that price.

Rashford has rejoined United for preseason training and could be given a new opportunity to impress under Michael Carrick, with former head coach Ruben Amorim, who effectively removed the forward from first-team consideration, now gone. However, there is a sense that United would prefer to cash in on the player if a buyer can be found.

After a successful loan spell with Barcelona, should Manchester United keep Marcus Rashford at the club this summer? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/7ltfTdPUJF

Rashford certainly has admirers, but his reported weekly wage of £325,000 ($428,000) is too much for the vast majority of interested clubs to pay. The chances are he will need to lower his demands in order to secure a move to another team in England or a competitive side in one of Europe's top leagues, as his only options to match his current salary would likely come from Saudi Arabia or Turkey.

Right now, Rashford and United are at an interesting impasse. Both would be happy for the player to stay and see what he can offer in the first half of the season before considering options again in the January transfer window, yet it feels like a parting of the ways would still be the best way forward, both for Rashford's career and United's financial picture.

title: Bruins Could Get Some More Beef on D With This Vet
description: The Boston Bruins could get some more beef on the blue line with this veteran D-man, given the opponents in the East. The post Bruins Could Get Some More Beef on D With This Vet appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Boston Bruins have had another relatively quiet offseason. In a way, remaining quiet is better than making questionable decisions. But as the rest of the Atlantic Division gears up for a big season, Don Sweeney can't afford to sit on his hands.

Fortunately, there's an interesting UFA option out there that could help add some more beef to the Bruins' lineup. That option is Logan Stanley.

The 6'7" 230-pound blueliner could very well give the Bruins a meaner edge heading into this season. That's something crucial when facing some of the more belligerent opponents like the Tampa Bay Lightning and Florida Panthers.

Adding Stanley should help solidify the bottom four, particularly with the departure of Andrew Peeke this summer. Peeke was mostly a defensive defenseman, something that all teams need to have in their bottom four.

Stanley brings that. He delivers decent if unspectacular play. His physicality is an asset, ensuring that the opposition remains honest.

The only question mark would be the terms of a deal for Stanley. The veteran blueliner is still 28 and likely looking for a multi-year deal. And that's just the thing. The Bruins might not be willing to commit beyond a one or two-year deal.

But there might be a way that the Bruins could bring Stanley in without breaking the bank.

The Bruins could take a shot on Stanley by signing him to a one-year, show-me deal. So, something along the lines of a $4 million cap hit, which might seem a bit onerous for a bottom-pairing defenseman, could make sense.

The deal could be part of a broader promise by the organization. If Stanley fits, the two sides could work out a contract extension. If he doesn't somehow fit in, he could be another NHL trade deadline piece to move.

Sure, the Bruins wouldn't get much for him at the deadline. But the club could allow Stanley to get another shot much like the Winnipeg Jets did this past season by sending him to the Buffalo Sabres.

Bruins Should Take Flyer on Hurricanes' Beleaguered Center

The prospect of rolling out Nikita Zadorov and Logan Stanley one after the other should be tantalizing to Bruins fans. The bruising, if not necessarily flashy play could help offset some of the apparent lack of offensive punch Boston shows.

The Bruins aren't built to win games by outscoring opponents. The game plan should once again focus on buying David Pastrnak enough time to bust games wide open.

And that's precisely what Stanley helps accomplish.

It's unclear if the Bruins would be willing to meet Stanley's contract demands. But if there's a way to work something out, the Bruins would be remiss if they didn't at least kick the tires on the hulking blueliner.

The Bruins need every edge they can get. And if it comes in a massive package, all the better. The Atlantic Division playoff race should be airtight. That's why having strong reinforcements could make a massive difference in 2026-27.

title: Barcelona looking to close the deal to Real Madrid target as soon as possible – Romano
description: Barcelona appear to be on the verge of completing the biggest coup of the summer as they are closing in on signing Rodri.The Manchester City midfielder has reportedly agreed to a move to Catalonia, as...
fullText:
Barcelona appear to be on the verge of completing the biggest coup of the summer as they are closing in on signing Rodri.

The Manchester City midfielder has reportedly agreed to a move to Catalonia, as he looks to finally return to Spain after a fantastic spell at the Etihad.

This is a massive coup for the Catalans considering the fact that Rodri was very close to joining Real Madrid.

The Rodri deal is just around the corner. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images)

A recent report from Fabzirio Romano has offered crucial updates on the Rodri saga, adding that Barcelona are keen on closing the deal as fast as possible.

According to the transfer expert, Barcelona want to move quickly for one key reason: to avoid any last-minute surprises.

The club have been working behind the scenes on the deal for some time, and are now eager to push it over the line without complications.

To that end, Barcelona have already sent their contract proposal to Rodri and his agent, while also making contact with Manchester City to inform them that talks with the player are underway.

Romano also highlights just how much work has gone into the pursuit, with the entire hierarchy playing a part.

Rodri is set to snub Real Madrid in favour of a Barcelona switch. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images)

Rodri has spoken to both Joan Laporta and Deco, with the sporting director said to have done an incredible job in getting the doors open for the deal.

The midfielder has also held conversations with Hansi Flick, meaning the player, coach and directors are all fully engaged in trying to make the move happen.

Crucially, Rodri has given Barcelona the green light to negotiate, opening the door to the Catalans for the very first time.

The next step now rests with Rodri himself. Barcelona are waiting for the player to formally communicate his decision to Manchester City, at which point they can advance and finalise the club-to-club aspect of the deal.

Interestingly, City's patience last week may have played into Barcelona's hands. When Real Madrid arrived ready to pay €50 million, the Premier League champions opted against closing the deal, sensing other clubs could join the race.

That gamble has now seen Barcelona enter the picture, with Los Blancos suddenly viewing Rodri as far away.

For Barcelona, landing Rodri would be a stunning statement, and something that seemed almost unthinkable just a few weeks ago.

title: World Cup-winning midfielder has personally informed Real Madrid of decision to join Barcelona
description: In just over 24 hours, Real Madrid have completely slipped out of control of the Rodri operation that they had marked as a summer priority.They were in pole position to land the midfielder and were in...
fullText:
In just over 24 hours, Real Madrid have completely slipped out of control of the Rodri operation that they had marked as a summer priority.

They were in pole position to land the midfielder and were in talks directly with Manchester City. The two parties were seemingly negotiating an agreement but Barcelona used the opportunity to swoop in.

All of a sudden, the Catalans have now leapfrogged Real Madrid in the race and reports have it that the player's transfer to Barcelona is now very advanced. The player has reportedly chosen Catalonia over Madrid.

As relayed in a recent update, Rodri's agent directly told El Larguero via Diario AS the reality of the situation, and where Real Madrid and Barcelona stood all along in the dynamic.

Real Madrid made a massive effort for Rodri. (Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

The agent conveyed that the Manchester City star was 'genuinely grateful' for the respect and interest Real Madrid showed in him over the past two weeks of negotiations.

He also said that everyone at the club, from the president to the staff and even the CEO, did everything possible to sign Rodri and that Real Madrid left no stone unturned. In fact, he confirmed that Los Blancos even submitted an 'unrejectable' offer.

Out of respect for Real Madrid, the player and his agent personally called the club administration last night to thank them for everything and inform them of the player's decision to sign for another club. They wish to avoid any unnecessary drama.

While Real Madrid's project offered a more prominent role to Rodri, it is completely understandable why he chose Barcelona over Los Blancos once the interest arrived.

The Barcelona-dominant Spain NT dressing room played a part in Rodri's decision. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

For starters, his style of football would be more suited to the Catalans' possession-dominant style, and the influence of Pep Guardiola will make the transition easier.

Further, the Barcelona dressing room is dominated by Spanish internationals, all of whom are close to Rodri and played a part in convincing him to join the Catalans.

Jose Mourinho is said to be furious at the development as he prioritised a new defensive midfielder this summer and saw Rodri as the perfect signing. It remains to be seen if Los Blancos push for any new midfielder after Rodri's snub.

title: Real Madrid fans get angry after Rodri chooses Barcelona
description: They are NOT happy
fullText:
Real Madrid fans have taken to social media to express their displeasure with reports that Manchester City midfielder Rodri has decided not to join their club, and instead try to join their worst enemy, Barcelona.

Nothing is definitive, but the anger is real. It comes at a time when Madrid announced the signing of Yan Diomandé from RB Lepizig. Posts announcing the transfer, usually reserved for hype for the incoming player, were instead filled with replies that expressed frustration and sometimes anger towards the club's top brass over the Rodri transfer saga.

There were rumors that Florentino Pérez wasn't too keen on the idea of signing Rodri because doing so was a campaign promise of one of his rivals for the club presidency.

But after Rodri's stellar World Cup, it just made too much sense: he would address an area of need on the pitch, and would shore up Madrid's lack of representation in the Spain team that became world champions.

Madrid media has been signaling confidence for a while, and even said the player would reject Barcelona. But the latest reports paint a different picture: They say Barcelona manager Hansi Flick convinced Rodri to join his system and become a key cog.

It's again worth mentioning that this is all happening in transfer pages and rumors, and even if you believe those, this is not set in stone. Still, the dissatisfaction is palpable in replies to recent social media posts from Madrid.

Losing out on Rodri wouldn't just mean losing out on a brilliant player. It would mean losing out on Spain's emblematic figure from their World Cup triumph at a time when Real aren't closely identified with the national team — not by a long shot.

And to lose out an emblem of Spain, born in Madrid, to Barcelona? That may prove too much for some.

title: Even Red Sox’s Chad Tracy can’t believe historic comeback to beat White Sox
description: Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy explains Thursday's gutsy win vs. White Sox with a sentence that perfectly sums up the team's torrid run
fullText:
Even Red Sox's Chad Tracy can't believe historic comeback to beat White Sox appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Boston Red Sox were quite sloppy for much of Thursday night's series finale versus the Chicago White Sox, making the type of mistakes that fans saw for the first three months of the campaign. They committed two errors that resulted in three runs, potential tying run Jarren Duran made the final out of the eighth inning after attempting to steal third base and former Sox prospect Chase Meidroth blasted two two-run homers. This should have been a loss that temporarily transported Fenway Park to this past spring.

But if it was not clear already, Boston once again proved that this is a completely different team. Chad Tracy's ballclub overcame its blunders and the Chicago White Sox's steady offensive attack, relying on clutch two-out hits, run-saving defense and a whole lot of moxie to stun Chicago with a 12-11 extra-innings victory. This weakling-turned-juggernaut came back five times during this four-and-a-half-hour game, before Caleb Durbin notched the walk-off single in the 13th.

This no longer feels like a magical story. Awe-inspiring grit is simply a part of the Red Sox's identity. Tracy used seven words that encapsulate how this group has carried itself during what is now a 31-5 stretch since June 25.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"They just did not want to lose," the interim manager said after Boston's eighth consecutive win, per USA TODAY's Bob Nightengale. "It was incredible."

Durbin continues to be at the forefront of this historic turnaround, typifying the heads-up, tenacious style of baseball that he first honed with the Milwaukee Brewers. He totaled a team-high three hits to go with his heroic RBI. This was truly a collective effort, though.

Anthony Seigler and Andruw Monasterio, both of whom came over with Durbin in a February trade involving Kyle Harrison, also left a huge imprint on this marathon matchup. The former ended a brutal dry spell with three RBIs, which included a game-tying sacrifice fly in the 10h inning, and the latter smashed two RBI doubles.

Ceddanne Rafaela, Masataka Yoshida and Connor Wong all enjoyed multi-hit outings as well, Duran mitigated damage by throwing out Braden Montgomery at home in the 12th and Brayan Bello gutted through two innings on short rest. The Red Sox punched back from all sides, and finally, their opponents fell to the ground.

Boston is now just a half-game behind the New York Yankees for second place in the American League Wild Card standings and just five clear of the Tampa Bay Rays for the top record in the AL. Boston has shown everyone that a franchise can reinvent itself despite overwhelming bad optics, a last-place record and injuries to two of its most highly touted players.

Ideally, the Red Sox (63-51) will not have to be nearly as resilient in their upcoming home series versus the free-falling Athletics (45-70), one of the many teams that was ahead of Boston entering July.

title: 'Virat Kohli has been my sponsor': 2026 CWG boxing gold medalist Sakshi Dhanda credits India star for support
description: Sakshi Chaudhary Dhanda quickly silenced critics after she defeated Ruby White for 51 kg gold at the CWG, and the name she thanked was none other than the Run Machine Virat Kohli.
fullText:
'Virat Kohli has been my sponsor': 2026 CWG boxing gold medalist Sakshi Dhanda credits India star for support originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

India's Sakshi Chaudhary Dhanda won the gold medal in the 51 kg category at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The boxer credited Virat Kohli alongside Vijender Singh as her sponsor and role model throughout the journey.

The Virat Kohli Foundation helped Sakshi for the last three years during her crucial years.

Indian boxers were absolutely dominant at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. With seven golds and three silvers, this was the most medals in the sport won at the event by any single nation. In fact, in the women's division. India won five out of the six gold medals available.

Sakshi Chaudhary Dhanda was one of those five with the Bhiwani, Haryana, native, winning the gold in the 51 kg category after defeating England's Ruby White. She completely outclassed her opponent and marked a remarkable comeback for a fighter whose career had once been derailed by a serious shoulder injury.

The boxer from Bhiwani in Haryana had to drop a weight category and beat a string of established names, including world champion Nikhat Zareen, just to make the India squad. That backdrop made her podium finish at the 2026 Commonwealth Games all the more satisfying, and she was quick to acknowledge the support that helped her get there.

Despite her emphatic win, Sakshi remained humble and was quick to praise former Indian boxer and Olympic bronze medalist Vijender Singh as her inspiration and idol. She also was quick to acknowledge Kohli's role in her journey.

She told IANS, "Virat Kohli has also supported me a lot throughout my journey. He has been my sponsor, and I would like to thank him as well. " While some might be confused about their connection, those who have followed Kohli over the years know that the Run Machine has run the Virat Kohli Foundation since 2013 to help Indian sportspersons in their journey for greatness.

Bhiwani, Haryana: Commonwealth Games 51 kg gold medallist boxer Sakshi Dhanda says, "I started boxing after watching Vijender Singh. Virat Kohli has also supported me a lot throughout my journey. He has been my sponsor, and I would like to thank him as well" pic.twitter.com/N4jwW29zAB

Both Sakshi Chaudhary and her father Manoj have credited Kohli for helping support her career for a stretch of three years when the boxer struggled financially. She also credited the ICT star for his grit, work ethic, and discipline.

Sakshi Chaudhary isn't the only name Kohli has supported in his mission to elevate the Indian sporting scene. The RCB has been part of multiple charities throughout his career, going back to his early playing days. It won't be wrong to say that he is majorly responsible for India winning the landslide seven golds at the CWG.

Sakshi's career was nearly derailed after her shoulder injury, and Indian fans have already seen how quickly an athlete can go from world-class to obsolete. So Kohli's backing in bringing the boxer back to the forefront and her own ability to survive the ruthless bracket till the finals are nothing short of incredible.

If her gold medal inspires more high-profile figures to invest in athletes across sports, then Kohli's quiet patronage will have delivered a return that stretches far beyond a single Commonwealth Games medal in Glasgow.

title: Former Ferrari driver makes honest admission over Hamilton's 2026 revival
description: Former F1 driver and Ferrari racer Gerhard Berger has expressed his delight at seeing Lewis Hamilton and the Maranello outfit return to winning ways this season after a first year together that fell short of expectations. After a disappointing first season with Ferrari that yielded no wins, podiums or pole positions, Hamilton has enjoyed a dramatic turnaround under Formula 1's new regulations.
fullText:
Former F1 driver and Ferrari racer Gerhard Berger has expressed his delight at seeing Lewis Hamilton and the Maranello outfit return to winning ways this season after a first year together that fell short of expectations.

After a disappointing first season with Ferrari that yielded no wins, podiums or pole positions, Hamilton has enjoyed a dramatic turnaround under Formula 1's new regulations. Eleven races into the campaign, the seven-time world champion sits second in the Drivers' Championship on 169 points, having claimed one victory and five podium finishes. His resurgence has also seen him establish the upper hand over his Ferrari teammate.

Speaking to F1.com, Berger admitted he has been pleased to see Ferrari return to winning ways this season, adding that he is equally happy for Hamilton after the difficulties the Briton faced during his first year with the Scuderia. The former Ferrari driver believes Hamilton had to overcome both technical challenges and the presence of a highly competitive teammate, but feels the seven-time world champion is now beginning to turn things around.

"In general, we are all so happy if we see a winning Ferrari. Ferrari is Ferrari. I was very happy also for Lewis, because for Lewis, it's been very difficult. He came to Ferrari and wanted to repeat his success from the past.

"Suddenly, he found himself in a difficult situation from a technical side, but also from a team mate side – a very fast team mate. For Lewis, last year was very hard, but now it looks like he's coming out of the corner a bit."

Berger is not alone in praising Hamilton's resurgence. Damon Hill also believes the Ferrari driver returning to the front was never in doubt, arguing that someone with Hamilton's mentality was always going to bounce back.

The 1996 world champion described the Briton as an ultra-competitive racer who refuses to settle for anything less than success, adding that Hamilton has worked relentlessly behind the scenes to shape Ferrari around his own driving style and make the most of the influence his achievements have earned him within the team.

"Cream always rises to the top, doesn't it? I mean, he's someone who is... you cut him in half and it just says 'competitor' right the way through. He's going to win at anything he does. I don't think it sits easily with him to back off. He's been working hard over the winter, clearly, and he's worked on how he wants the Ferrari to be for him.

"They signed him, they paid a lot of money to have him, so he's saying, 'Okay, I'm not going to just sit here and do what you do. I'm going to tell you what I do, and you're going to make it suit me'. The power he has, the reputation he has, he's putting to work, to protect himself. He's right to do that."

title: Liverpool can sign their very own Rayan Cherki
description: Last season, Liverpool had a choice between Rayan Cherki and Florian Wirtz. Both players were willing to join the Reds with Arne Slot even meeting up with Cherki to discuss a potential move.In the end...
fullText:
Last season, Liverpool had a choice between Rayan Cherki and Florian Wirtz.

Both players were willing to join the Reds with Arne Slot even meeting up with Cherki to discuss a potential move.

In the end, Wirtz was the player who was welcomed to Anfield despite Cherki being worth around £70 million less.

Most people thought that both players would do well in the Premier League so, with this in mind, when Liverpool passed up the chance to sign the Frenchman, it was hardly surprising to see that Manchester City swooped in and got a deal over the line.

Both players were expected to carry over their performance levels from their previous teams but, in the end, only Cherki really delivered.

This led Liverpool's fans to question why Richard Hughes and Slot chose to spend well over £100 million on Wirtz when Cherki would've cost much less and would've arguably been a better signing.

However, now that things have changed at Anfield and the transfer window is back open, it seems like Liverpool could now sign their very own version of Cherki this summer.

Liverpool's attack is one of their main areas that needs upgrading this summer.

Several members of their first-team squad have left and, even though a couple have been brought in, it still doesn't feel like Liverpool have enough quality to start challenging for silverware again.

However, with the recent rumours that have emerged about Liverpool's potential transfer business, it feels like Liverpool could be about to sign some much-needed players.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Bradley Barcola now feel closer to a Liverpool switch then ever.

The Paris Saint-Germain duo are both up for grabs with Luis Enrique actually wanting to get rid of the former of the two.

And now, as per a fresh update from Caught Offside, Mbaye has made a decision on his future, especially with how PSG currently see him.

"An interesting detail to be aware of here is that Mbaye has had his issues with PSG, and they're understood to be open to a sale this summer," they wrote.

"As others have reported, it is my understanding that senior figures at the Parc des Princes have concerns about the teenager due to his fitness, weight problems, and diet.

"Sources also state he has often had trouble with being late to training, and this has led to him struggling to break into Luis Enrique's team on a more regular basis.

"Those close to the player deny this, but there is clearly bad blood there and this has encouraged Liverpool to make a move, with talks expected to start soon."

As mentioned, Liverpool's main priority for upgrades this summer is their attack.

They have hardly any depth among their ranks and, since Mbaye would only cost around €40 million, he's an absolute steal.

The 18-year-old would also not need to be registered by Liverpool until he's 21 years old and, by then, he'd be classed as homegrown.

However, despite all of the positive aspects of the deal, the fact that he's being seen the same way as Cherki should fill Liverpool fans with hope.

Before joining City, Cherki was supposed to be overweight and lazy, or that was what was coming out of Lyon anyway.

But, when he turned up to Manchester, he was in peak physical condition as he contributed to 28 goals across all competitions.

If Mbaye can get even half of those returns for Liverpool, it'd be a massive weight off of their shoulders.

And, even though he may not be ready to start straight away, after getting used to Iraola's system and developing even further, he could easily be Liverpool's Mohamed Salah successor.

title: Atletico Madrid coach plans to include Barcelona top target in league opener against Malaga
description: While Julian Alvarez might have hoped for something different, it appears the player has no choice but to return to training at Atletico Madrid on August 10.The Argentine has made no secret of his des...
fullText:
While Julian Alvarez might have hoped for something different, it appears the player has no choice but to return to training at Atletico Madrid on August 10.

The Argentine has made no secret of his desire to leave the club and complete a move to Barcelona, but Atletico have stood firm throughout, refusing to even entertain a sale.

And now, it seems Diego Simeone is already planning for the season ahead with Alvarez firmly in his thoughts.

Alvarez's hopes of a summer move is fading. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images)

According to Diario AS, Simeone is counting on Alvarez being available for Atletico's league opener against Malaga on August 19 at the Metropolitano.

The Atletico coach knows how vital it is to start the campaign strongly and wants the 'Spider' in peak condition for the clash. With that in mind, Simeone is already scheduling the striker's training sessions to ensure he is ready.

Alvarez is due to return to training on Monday, linking up with the other players who did not travel to Atletico's fixture in Seoul.

That leaves him just over a week to build up his fitness before the Malaga game, and Simeone wants him to make the most of every session.

Barcelona have their hands tied in the Alvarez pursuit. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

The report reiterates that Atletico's stance has not shifted one bit since the saga began.

The club have repeatedly insisted Alvarez will not be sold to Barcelona, nor to Real Madrid, who quickly withdrew from any interest.

Atletico even filed a complaint against Barcelona over the matter, and CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin has been unequivocal in stating that no offer will be accepted.

From Atletico's perspective, backing down now would represent a betrayal of everything they have built. The club also believe Alvarez has been poorly advised and led astray by his agents.

Alvarez, for his part, is expected to hold a meeting with Simeone regarding his future sometime next week.

Atletico are well aware there are few players of the Argentine's quality, and they have no intention of letting him go.

title: MotoGP now has the same American owners as Formula 1 – can it become as popular?
description: BRITISH GRAND PRIX : The world’s premier motorbike class heads to Silverstone this weekend for the British Grand Prix but, a month on from a world-record attendance for F1, Kieran Jackson tells why MotoGP has some way to go before it can compete with its four-wheeled brother
fullText:
When Formula 1's stateside overlords Liberty Media acquired a majority stake in MotoGP last year, at the cost of a mere £3.6billion, the blueprint for growth in the world's premier motorbike class was not a closely guarded secret. Modern-day F1 is the competition every sport worldwide is, to a large extent, looking to replicate. As the saying goes: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

And yet, beyond your two-wheeled petrolhead hardcores, cut-through is tricky. Aside from Spain's defending champion Marc Marquez, how many of the 2026 grid have you heard of? Do names like current championship leader Jorge Martin ring a bell? In the UK, the case for notoriety is not aided by the lack of a single British driver on the grid, 50 years since the last British champion in Barry Sheene. Undoubtedly, luring star names is at the forefront of the growth drive.

Enter Guenther Steiner: the former Haas team boss, famous for his expletive-laden rants and the unlikely star of the Drive to Survive phenomenon which launched F1 into the public mainstream.

Two-and-a-half years on from leaving the world of F1 (at least as a team principal; he is still a regular on punditry duties for Australian and German TV networks), Steiner has shifted his motorsport compass somewhat. Now, he is the CEO and owner of the Red Bull KTM Tech 3 outfit in MotoGP. And ahead of this weekend's British Grand Prix at Silverstone – fresh off a two-year contract extension announced on Thursday – the popular Italian-American is relishing a new challenge and a new paddock.

"I think MotoGP is like F1 was like 20 years ago," Steiner says, not discarding the mid-2000s era of Michael Schumacher dominating on track and Bernie Ecclestone off-track but, rather, an inference towards the growth of the sport in the two decades since that is incontestable.

"It's a sport which is growing, everyone wants to grow. If I can help to do that, I'm more than happy to do that. The potential of MotoGP is immense. As a sport, you can keep the costs much lower because the bike is smaller. I know how complex an F1 car is compared to a bike.

"And the sport itself? It really is something when they go side by side. It's amazing. MotoGP does not need help in the racing. The racing is good – leave it alone."

Was the latter remark the smallest of digs at Formula 1? Maybe yes, maybe no. Nonetheless, any seasoned observer of the 500cc bike series will know that the highlights package for most races contains no shortage of hard-hitting action, courageous overtakes and – as seen in Barcelona in May with Marquez's younger brother, Alex – dramatic crashes.

This weekend's Silverstone event occupies an intriguing spot on the sporting calendar. Shifted from a late-May date last year, the race takes place on a weekend with a minimal amount of top-level sport throughout the country. On-site, Silverstone executives are expecting their biggest crowd (around the 50,000 mark) since Valentino Rossi's final year in 2021.

Yet while die-hard fans will scoff at comparisons, the scope for enlargement is obvious. A month ago, Silverstone attracted a world-record 550,000 fans to four days of action over the F1 weekend. The lack of a free-to-air deal this weekend, with coverage solely on TNT Sports, feels like a missed opportunity too.

"It's very difficult [to compare it to F1]," Steiner insists. "Is it better or worse? It's just different.

"MotoGP doesn't have to look exactly like what F1 is; they can write their own story. You do not have to copy and paste the racing or the commercial opportunities. F1 was big under Bernie [Ecclestone] but under Liberty, they gave it another spike. They can do the same now with MotoGP.

"Not everyone can be F1, which is around the second biggest worldwide sport now behind football. But… it can be very big."

The room for expansion is obvious: not just the UK, but the USA (where there is currently just one race, at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin) and bike-mad India are two massive growth markets. Sixteen of the 22 full-time riders are from either Spain or Italy. Regardless, for the second year running, MotoGP will have a record-breaking calendar at 22 races, criss-crossing five different continents.

For the future? Carving the riders into front-of-the-camera personalities, with increased marketing and media opportunities, is a must. Deep-rooted rivalries between riders and team bosses would help too, in an ecosystem which is generally affable and warm. A fly-on-the-wall series to depict all this, à la Drive to Survive, feels like a no-brainer down the line.

Yet 100 years to the day since the first-ever British Grand Prix was held at Brooklands, the sport which goes by the mantra "half the wheels, twice the balls" has a real opportunity to expand and accelerate. The raw ingredients are there: daredevils risking it all for sporting theatre and glory. And once the eyeballs watch, they may not be able to resist looking away.

title: Yan Diomande explains decision to join Real Madrid in farewell letter: ‘Childhood dream come true’
description: Real Madrid had an eventful Thursday as they announced not only Vinicius Jr.’s contract renewal but also finalised and made the arrival of Yan Diomande official.The RB Leipzig winger’s signing was...
fullText:
Real Madrid had an eventful Thursday as they announced not only Vinicius Jr.'s contract renewal but also finalised and made the arrival of Yan Diomande official.

The RB Leipzig winger's signing was announced after a long transfer saga, putting an end to all speculation and ensuring that Real Madrid receive the attacking boost that can take them to the next level.

In the process, Diomande became the most expensive signing in Real Madrid history as the club reportedly shelled out €140 million including variables for the transfer.

Taking to his Instagram after the official confirmation of his transfer to Real Madrid, Diomande penned a farewell letter to fans of the Bundesliga side where he explained why he prioritised a move to Real Madrid.

"I am incredibly grateful to RB Leipzig. The club and its management believed in me a year ago, even though I had only played a few professional matches at that point," he began, praising Leipzig for their faith in him.

Diomande has signed a deal until 2033. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images)

"They placed their trust in me and allowed me to prove myself at the highest level," he added.

The new Real Madrid player then acknowledged the role Leipzig played in pushing him to the highest level for both club and country, saying,

"I was able to establish myself in one of Europe's top leagues, earn my place in the Côte d'Ivoire national team and represent my country on the biggest stage of all, the FIFA World Cup."

"None of this would have been possible without RB Leipzig, and for that I will always be grateful."

Diomande then explained why he was moving to Real Madrid and how it has always been a dream of his.

"Moving to Real Madrid is a childhood dream come true for me. I am all the more grateful to the management at RB Leipzig for making this move possible despite my current contract."

Diomande has dreamt of Real Madrid for long. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

Thanking the fans for their love, support and belief, the star winger said,

"To the fans, thank you for your incredible support from the very beginning. Your passion, your belief in me and your encouragement meant more than words can express."

"I'll always be grateful for the love you've shown me," he added.

Towards the end of his letter, Diomande highlighted how he was excited for the chapter that lies ahead and what he hoped from the objective.

"Today, a new chapter begins. Leaving is never easy, but I'm excited for what's ahead and I'll always look back on my time in Leipzig with immense pride."

"This club will always hold a special place in my heart, and I'll continue to follow its journey closely. Who knows? Maybe we'll meet one day again in the Champions League. Thank you for everything," he concluded.

title: Shubman Gill injury update: Will the India captain play first Test vs Sri Lanka
description: After his right finger was injured, the Indian skipper was pulled from fielding duties in the practice match against Sri Lanka and here's the chances on if Shubman Gill will play the first Test.
fullText:
India captain Shubman Gill has become the latest fitness concern for a depleted India squad, suffering an injury scare during training ahead of the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka.

The blow adds to a growing list of setbacks that have disrupted India's preparations for the tour.

Gill was struck on his right thumb by a delivery from one of the pacers while batting in the nets on Thursday, the second day of India's training in Sri Lanka. The 26-year-old was visibly in pain and received immediate treatment from the team physio, who applied a band-aid before Gill resumed his batting session.

His discomfort did not end there. Later in the day, Gill appeared to hurt his right hand again during slip-catching practice, forcing him to stop fielding drills and apply an ice pack. The double blow briefly raised alarm within an India camp already stretched thin by injuries.

Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source

The early indications on Shubman Gill's fitness offer India considerable relief.

Preliminary assessments reportedly showed no structural damage or fracture to his right hand, and the India captain was able to complete his training session without major discomfort after returning to face the spinners in the nets.

The Indian team management will be hopeful the knock is nothing serious, given Gill has been India's standout batter in the longest format since taking over the captaincy during the England series.

The exact severity is yet to be officially confirmed by the BCCI, but Gill's continued participation in practice points to a minor issue rather than a lasting one.

Barring any setback in the coming days, Gill is expected to be available when India begins the series against Sri Lanka in Galle on August 15, with the second Test to follow at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo from August 23.

Even if Gill's scare proves minor, the episode underlines just how badly injuries have disrupted India's build-up to this series. Jasprit Bumrah has been ruled out with a knee problem, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana are sidelined, Washington Sundar misses the opening Test with a hamstring issue, and Sai Sudharsan remains doubtful as he recovers from a toe injury.

India is currently playing a three-day warm-up game against Sri Lanka Cricket XI.
