title: The deeper significance behind South Africa and New Zealand’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series
description: RUGBY’S GREATEST RIVALRY: As the two ruling powers of men’s rugby union prepare to meet in two Tests, Harry Latham-Coyle explains the rich history and off-field conflicts that deepen the rivalry
fullText:
They are known as "The Incomparables", a nickname to daunt a group of successors that will find themselves inevitably compared. When Dave Rennie unveiled his New Zealand squad for the tour of South Africa, present were a selection of the 1996 All Blacks who, 30 years ago, conquered the reigning world champion Springboks in their own back yard and launched rugby union's professional age. Three decades on, the echoes of that series still sound; again, this much-anticipated meeting of men's rugby's two ruling powers carries with it a significance beyond simply the sport at its centre.

For while four Tests between the southern hemisphere heavyweights whet the appetite, this is as much a venture born out of mutual commercial benefit as any great demand for more meetings between the pair. Indeed, there is a degree of rankling resentment at the manner in which the two unions have broken away from the Rugby Championship, a competition that has found new life in recent years. But these encounters, titled "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry", carry all the hallmarks of that term – genuine history, genuine hostility, genuine best-of-the-best feel.

"With eight matches in six weeks, including a four-Test series against the Springboks, this would have to be the toughest tour in rugby," All Blacks coach Dave Rennie said. "Every player will be required to play their part across this tour, whether it's preparing to play or helping their mates prepare.

"It will be an intense seven weeks of touring but an excellent opportunity for us to pit ourselves against the current benchmark team in world rugby, and to build connections with each other in a way that only a tour of this scale can do."

There will be touring teams of old that may scoff at the schedule facing the All Blacks but this is a gruelling itinerary for modern times. New Zealand will criss-cross the Rainbow Nation with four games against the United Rugby Championship (URC) franchises interspersed among four fully-fledged Tests, with half of each played at altitude. They will not need reminding of the strength and depth of South African rugby, or the hunger of those on the fringes to force their way into Springboks contention.

Still, though, it feels as if these All Blacks have plenty to prove. There were encouraging early signs at the start of the Rennie regime in July's Nations Championship fixtures, but New Zealand are clearly playing catch-up after two ultimately wasted years under Scott Robertson. An initial evolution is clear – more ball in play, less kicking, more expression – but one can easily fall back on bad habits against a side like South Africa. Successive sides and successive head coaches have been destabilised by galling days against the Springboks: Mbombela in 2022; Twickenham in 2023; Wellington, most strikingly, last year. Five of the last six meetings, including the World Cup final, have gone South Africa's way.

There is a difference here to 1996: then, South Africa's World Cup success a year prior had felt a shock sprung in part by a unique confluence of political and personal motivation. Now, the Springboks are clearly the world's best, and at the forefront of the rugby's orthodoxy – a position occupied by their tourists for most of the last three decades. It can be seen in the board rooms and back rooms that govern the game.

Senior figures at World Rugby have noted that at their most recent "Shape of the Game" conference in south-west London, it was Rassie Erasmus to whom the room generally looked when the Springboks supremo was present; Felix Jones, his whip-smart assistant and key lieutenant, has also been described as a prominent voice of late.

A strong delegation from the South African hierarchy was out in force in March for that conference amid suggestions of a push to de-power the scrum and maul from other areas of the game. World Rugby denied any such talks taking place – and a key takeaway from the conference was a moratorium of sorts on the type of rule tweaking and tinkering that has been too common within the sport – but a slight schism over the future has opened up.

Where South Africa and France, particularly, boast relatively buoyancy at Test and domestic level, Australia and New Zealand perhaps feel rugby union is under greater duress, with the continuing threat of the NRL's largesse again creating headlines in the Pacific in recent weeks. More than 30 years since the dawn of professionalism, rugby union is still figuring out how best to sell itself.

It is notable that Mark Robinson, the former CEO of NZ Rugby, has stepped in to an overarching role with the global governing body as the organisation sets a subtly different direction over a crucial period leading up to two World Cups in the United States.

This is a key series in that regard, with the fourth Test held in Baltimore – a city likely to be a strong contender to host games at those tournaments. Commercially, there is significance here, too, with the Springboks known to be keen to build their global brand in a manner similar to that of the All Blacks. As previously detailed, though, NZ Rugby is not necessarily flush with cash – for each, four marquee and lucrative Tests like these are timely.

It is perhaps fitting that the first match of the All Blacks' tour, against the Stormers on Friday night, takes place in Cape Town. New Zealand boast significant support in the city dating back to the days of apartheid, when many from the Cape Coloured community turned away from the all-white Springboks.

A shared kinship was further established during the 1981 South Africa tour to New Zealand, which was met with strong protests. Into that rich historical tapestry more thread is about to be woven.

title: Pablo Torre’s new ‘multimillion-dollar’ secret sponsorship claim might mean trouble for Kawhi Leonard, Clippers
description: In a shocking turn of events, Pablo Torre has seemingly exposed a new Kawhi Leonard scandal with the Los Angeles Clippers before the first one is even resolved. Kawhi Leonard and the Los Angeles Clippers must be sick at the sound of Pablo Torre’s name at this point.
fullText:
In a shocking turn of events, Pablo Torre has seemingly exposed a new Kawhi Leonard scandal with the Los Angeles Clippers before the first one is even resolved.

Kawhi Leonard and the Los Angeles Clippers must be sick at the sound of Pablo Torre's name at this point. His journalism has resulted in an NBA investigation into their dealings that is still ongoing.

Torre reported in September 2025 that the Clippers had possibly circumvented the NBA salary cap by paying Leonard through Aspiration, one of their sponsors. Both parties have continually denied this.

Now, he has come out with another report that indicates further payments to Leonard made through a different organisational sponsor. The scandal appears to be growing even bigger.

The LA Clippers' new home arena, the Intuit Dome, has been the envy of the league. One of their innovative additions was the Halo Board, which was built by a company named Daktronics.

This is relevant to the case because Torre is now alleging that Kawhi had a multimillion-dollar deal with them that he failed to disclose. This adds more money going to him, on top of his salary and the alleged Aspiration deal.

"This was talked about just openly within the organisation, that Kawhi was a spokesperson for Daktronics," Torre's high-level anonymous source said on his show. "It was 1000% a way to circumvent the salary cap."

The journalist himself added, "This Kawhi deal was not just talked about by higher-ups with the Clippers to circumvent the salary cap. This second source was also told that Kawhi's Daktronics sponsorship was a multimillion-dollar deal."

This is another bombshell from Torre, and one that will likely have to be taken into consideration by the NBA. As the allegations continue to mount, it will be interesting to see what Leonard and the Clippers have to say.

Kawhi's trade to the Raptors has been put on hold thanks to the investigation into the Aspiration scandal. With potentially new information coming to light, the entire move could be put in jeopardy.

title: India vs Sri Lanka: India's search for answers to rediscover lost glory in Tests begins in Colombo
description: India begin their three-day warm-up fixture against Sri Lanka XI at the NCC in Colombo today. The Shubman Gill-led unit has already had two intense training sessions and a largely rested squad means the team feels fresh for the crucial series starting August 15. There are some injury concerns: Jasprit Bumrah, Washington Sundar, and Sai Sudharsan. However, the squad has enough quality to secure a scoreline that keeps their World Test Championship final chances alive.
fullText:
TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: "Come 15th morning whether we are batting first or bowling first we will be absolutely ready with every answer to every question thrown at us."

India head coach Gautam Gambhir came prepared with the war cry when his troops assembled at the Nondescripts Cricket Club in Colombo for their first practice session on the crucial two-Test tour. The weather stayed clear, allowing the visitors a proper morning hit before another intense session on a very humid afternoon the following day. The Shubman Gill-led unit arrived in Sri Lanka 11 days before the series opener in Galle on August 15.

There will be enough practice sessions, including a three-day warm-up fixture, before the first Test, ensuring ample opportunity to acclimatise to the local conditions. Additionally, conditions will be familiar for six of the 15 squad members who were part of two fixtures in the India A vs Sri Lanka A series last month.

India have had mixed outings in the longest format over the past year; they drew a series in England (2-2) they would have fancied themselves to win and then suffered a tame surrender against South Africa (0-2).

The scheduling meant India lacked ideal preparation for the South Africa series, as they had to adjust to different time zones and formats within a matter of days. The result: a whitewash that left plenty to ponder.

Not much changed for the one-off Test against Afghanistan; most players switched from the IPL to the red-ball grind within days, but the opposition did not pose the kind of challenge that could have raised further questions over the scheduling.

The questions around scheduling and preparation can well take a back seat this August, as the Test squad is well-rested and has enough time, in the coach's words, to "tick all the boxes" before taking the field in Galle.

Though there are some injury concerns. The team are without Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar (at least for the first Test). However, the 14 available players (Sai Sudharsan is yet to receive clearance from the CoE) are fit and raring to go. They also have a variety of net bowlers — Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Vipraj Nigam and Shivang Kumar — to aid their preparations.

Ravindra Jadeja has had the longest lean period, having last played in the IPL. Mohammed Siraj and Rishabh Pant have also been cooling their heels since the one-off Test against Afghanistan in June.

In the build-up to the series, several players prepared individually: Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul trained indoors in rain-hit Mumbai, while Shubman Gill had some productive sessions in Chandigarh. Pant flew to Ranchi to spend some time with former India captain MS Dhoni.

To keep their World Test Championship final qualification hopes alive, India need to board the flight back from Colombo with a 2-0 series victory.

The road in this format has not been smooth; it has been littered with pertinent questions. The next three weeks offer the team management and the squad the opportunity not only to find those answers, but also to rediscover their lost glory.

title: Jersey Bulls ready for new league
description: Jersey Bulls manager Elliot Powell hopes the club's move to Isthmian League South Central will benefit his side.
fullText:
Jersey Bulls manager Elliot Powell hopes the club's move to Isthmian League South Central will benefit his side.

The Bulls are in their second season in the eighth tier and finished third in the league's South East division last season, losing out in the play-offs.

The move west opens up chances to shorten travel distances with the option of flying into Southampton or London Heathrow to play sides based in Hampshire, Berkshire and west London.

Last season the club mainly used London Gatwick ahead of sometimes lengthy road journeys into Kent and Sussex.

"If it means a seven-hour day away on a Saturday rather than an 11-hour day away on a Saturday, then we have to take that," Powell told BBC Sport.

"If you look at the likes of Adam Trotter, players that probably stepped away because of those travel commitments, then anything we can do to try and prolong the career of anybody that's playing for the Jersey Bulls is something that we have to take seriously and I'm really happy that the board are able to move us leagues."

Jersey Bulls boss Powell may step down at end of season

Jersey Bulls sign Somalia midfielder Mohamed

Jersey Bulls suffer play-off heartbreak with shootout loss

On the field the island side will come up against many teams they have not faced before.

However their opponents on the opening day, Harrow Borough, are familiar to the islanders from their clash in the FA Trophy last season.

"We played against Harrow Borough before, played really poorly on that day and got beat 4-0, so we know a little bit about them," said Powell.

"We know a little bit about Bedfont Sports, we know a lot about Cobham, so there's teams in our league that we know bits and pieces about and I think it'll be much of a muchness to the South East League.

"There's less 3G pitches so I'd imagine it'd be a slightly more direct league in terms of how teams play, just with the nature of the pitches that we'll be playing on in November, December, January time, and even starting on Saturday we know it's not a great surface that we're going away to.

"It'll be semi-professional league and we're an amateur team in it, so it's going be a tough battle for us, but if we play anywhere near how we did last season I'd expect a successful season again."

The islanders have a new look to their side with experienced players like Adam Trotter and Luke Campbell calling time on their Bulls careers, while winger Rai Dos Santos has moved to Australia.

Bulls have made a couple of high-profile additions, with former winger Sami Henia-Kamau returning after spells with Swansea City and Hull City, as well as winning a cap for Kenya, and Somalia midfielder Jarma Mohamed joining the side after moving to Jersey.

But Powell can still call on experienced players such as striker Lorne Bickley, midfielder Luke Watson, captain James Queree and goalkeeper Euan van der Vliet, as well as some promising young players from the club's academy

"When you can bring in the likes of Jarma to replace Adam, we've got Jack Lumsden back from university, Harry Curtis sort of slots in for that Luke Campbell vacancy, and then we've got Sami Henia-Kamau back from the UK as well, so he naturally replaces Rai," he explained.

"We've worked really hard and every credit to the board that have helped us bring these players back and make sure there's work opportunities for them.

"We're still a fully amateur club, nothing's changed on that front. These players will still be working nine to five or whatever their working hours may be, and football is very much a side gig for them.

"So it's difficult for us to recruit players, there's so many hoops that we have to jump through and so many other considerations that we have to make, but we're really happy with the business that we've done.

"The best bit is that it's all underpinned by some really promising young players coming through from the local game with Harry McKenzie, Casey Nixon and Darryl Mvalo, so it's a really exciting time.

"It is a slightly new-look Bulls side, but you've still got the stalwarts there of Queree, Watson, van der Vliet, Jay Giles, so there's plenty of experience still to help these young lads through.

"But I think just a slightly fresh look to the team will hopefully stand us in good stead this season."

title: 39 moves across five countries - the footballer forever in motion
description: As he prepares to manage in the FA Cup for the first time, Zeph Thomas tells BBC Sport about his extraordinary career path spanning 39 moves in 18 years.
fullText:
"If I I didn't get the money I thought I deserved, I'd be off," says Zeph Thomas, as he attempts to explain a career path that has spanned an extraordinary 39 moves in 18 years.

The Bradford-born winger, 36, is one of football's ultimate journeymen.

Rossington Main (five spells), Mickleover Sports (four spells), Frickley Athletic (three spells), Garden City Broncbusters (United States), Montegnee (Belgium), Thunder Bay Chill (Canada).

Thomas' list of former clubs goes on and on.

Cowdenbeath, Boston United, Harrogate Town, Scarborough Athletic, Stafford Rangers, Leek Town.

Ilkeston Town, Matlock Town, Goole, Glossop North End, Stocksbridge Park Steels, Brighouse Town (two spells), Emley, Harrogate Railway Athletic, Sheffield, Shaw Lane, Belper Town, Parkgate, Campion, Eccleshill United, Selby Town and Ossett United.

But could Thomas' life on the move be over?

The former St Kitts & Nevis international has embraced his player-manager role at ninth-tier South Yorkshire club Dearne & District since being appointed in 2024.

After winning the Northern Counties East League First Division last season, the village club based in Goldthorpe, near Barnsley, play their first ever FA Cup match on Saturday when they visit Runcorn Town - one of 219 extra preliminary round ties scheduled to take place.

"We've gone from being in the Doncaster Saturday League in 2021 to playing in the FA Cup," adds Thomas.

"It's massive for the area because they have never seen this team play in the competition."

Where & when? This weekend's FA Cup extra preliminary round fixtures

Thomas' career started at Rotherham United when former Manchester United forward Mark Robins was youth team coach.

He was released in 2008 without making a senior appearance, a decision that did not come as a complete surprise to him.

"I was a bit petulant and naive back then," he says.

"I remember scoring in a reserve game and then the next day we had to come in for recovery runs. At the time, I didn't think I should have been doing any of that.

"If my attitude had been better I would probably have been fine to be honest."

With his dreams of making it big in the full-time game shattered, Thomas embarked on a remarkable journey across non-league football in England, while there were spells at clubs in Kansas, Ontario, Scotland and Belgium.

In 2013-14 alone, he was on the books of Sheffield, Mickleover Sports, Scarborough Athletic, Matlock Town and Goole, while he started 2016-17 back at Mickleover Sports and then went to Shaw Lane, Stafford Rangers, Frickley Athletic... before ending back at Mickleover.

The non-league club where he spent his longest spell was Brighouse Town (second stint) between 2020 and 2023.

While at Stocksbridge Park Steels, he played against Jamie Vardy, then at Halifax Town, before Vardy went on to play for England and win the Premier League with Leicester City in 2015-2016.

In 2013, Thomas almost quit playing after suffering a groin injury. He worked in a call centre in Rotherham and thought about joining the army before being given an opportunity to resume his career at Thunder Bay Chill in Ontario.

Has he kept a record of his numerous destinations?

"Not at all. There's definitely been too many to count," adds Thomas.

"It's been a good experience but it could have been better. I moved up or went sideways for more money.

"But playing in different countries was a great experience and I would encourage all young players to go and experience that if they get a chance.

"I worked under different coaches with different ideas and philosophies."

Zeph Thomas: The unknown local player set to feature on the international stage

From international debut to call centre in five months

After a life spent seemingly on the road, Thomas does not have so far to travel to games these days.

He lives a five-minute walk from Dearne & District's ground, with wife Marie and their two children, Jerome, 11, and Lucia, seven.

Thomas combines his part-time job with Dearne & District, who attracted a crowd of 453 for the home league game with Penistone Church on 28 July, with his role as lead coach for Derby County's Under-12s.

He is still registered to play for the non-league club but these days prefers to coach from the dugout and pass on his experience to players.

"Sometimes I feel a bit of a hypocrite because I used to move clubs for extra money," he says.

"Now I say to my players, 'keep on doing what you're doing because the money will come'."

title: Enzo Maresca dreams of Chelsea star Enzo Fernandez replacing Rodri at Man City
description: Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez is a target for Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca. He has hinted at being open to leaving Stamford Bridge this summer.According to Gianluca DiMarzio, the Chelsea star...
fullText:
Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez is a target for Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca. He has hinted at being open to leaving Stamford Bridge this summer.

According to Gianluca DiMarzio, the Chelsea star is their 'dream successor' to Rodri, who could be on his way back to Spain.

However, the report mentions that the Blues value Fernandez highly and he is a key player. It remains unclear whether they will even entertain any negotiations.

Chelsea suspended Fernandez last season for statements which alluded to him wanting to leave the West London outfit.

He was reportedly angling for a move to Spain, but nobody has stepped forward so far with an offer, fearing the reported £120 million (€140 million) price tag.

The 25-year-old enjoyed another productive season, delivering 10 goals and four assists (11 big chances created) in 36 Premier League appearances.

He added another three goals and two assists in the UEFA Champions League as Chelsea crashed out in the round of 16.

Fernandez can play comfortably in the number 10 position, as a box-to-box operator, or as a deep-lying playmaker.

He is comfortably one of the best in the world, despite his lack of athleticism, which means he struggles defensively in the notoriously fast and furious English top-flight.

If Chelsea are serious about building a serious project under Xabi Alonso, they must hold on to Fernandez at all costs and ignore City.

There aren't many upgrades in the market, and they aren't exactly looking to move to Stamford Bridge at this point.

Besides being a terrific footballer, he is a 'leader' and one of the few consistent performers in the side. Also, he always manages to stay injury-free.

Chelsea should cough up the salary increase he deserves and try to keep him on their books.

title: Arsenal scouted Andria Bartishvili this week
description: Arsenal have continued monitoring one of Georgian football’s brightest young talents closely, sending scouts to watch Andria Bartishvili in European action this week.Per the Daily Mail, the Gunners ...
fullText:
Arsenal have continued monitoring one of Georgian football's brightest young talents closely, sending scouts to watch Andria Bartishvili in European action this week.

Per the Daily Mail, the Gunners had representatives in attendance for Iberia 1999's Europa League qualifier against Northern Irish side Larne on Tuesday.

Arsenal have tracked Bartishvili for several months, with the Premier League club seeing him as one of the standout prospects from Georgia.

The Arsenal target's direct running, close control and attacking flair have earned him comparisons with Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Interestingly, PSG could rival Arsenal for his signature as they have been keeping tabs on the teenager too.

Also, several Serie A clubs have reportedly registered their interest in signing the 'very talented' 17-year-old attacking midfielder.

The youngster is currently on loan at Iberia 1999 from fellow Georgian club Kolkheti 1913, but he is expected to be sold this summer.

Growing interest from across Europe means a permanent move is on the horizon, with a transfer expected in the coming days.

Arsenal's latest scouting mission suggests they are determined to stay at the front of the queue for Bartishvili.

If Arsenal eventually pull the trigger to sign him, the North Londoners should consider leaving him in Georgia to continue developing.

Regular senior football in Georgia could prove far more valuable than limited minutes with the Gunners' academy or under-21s.

A deal that allows him to remain with his current club, or elsewhere in the Georgian top flight, would allow him to continue his development in a familiar environment.

It could make all the difference as Arsenal monitor his progress closely.

Besides, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta already has elite teenage attacking talents Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri competing for opportunities in the first team.

There is no immediate need to fast-track another prospect. Patience could ultimately maximise Bartishvili's long-term potential.

title: After Myles Garrett trade, Jared Verse confident joining Browns: 'I'm ready to see the look on everybody's face'
description: Through reading and journaling, lifting and attending a pass rush summit, Verse has dialed into the habits that most make him him. That extends to trash-talking at practice.
fullText:
BEREA, Ohio — Jared Verse watches Myles Garrett's film.

But the Cleveland Browns edge rusher whom the Los Angeles Rams dealt as part of a trade for Garrett is not trying to pretend he's Garrett. Verse was not the 2017 first overall pick of the NFL Draft and he is not the reigning Defensive Player of the Year.

And he thinks that's going to make a difference in Cleveland.

"I've told a thousand people, I'm not here to replace Myles," Verse told Yahoo Sports in a Thursday sit-down interview. "That's not my job. It's not my description. When I signed any contract, that's not part of anything I signed.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

Verse shares this party line with confidence and a sense of calm that bely how he felt on June 1, when the Rams told him that he was part of a blockbuster trade for Garrett. The Rams' haul: Garrett. The Browns': Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third.

Verse was gutted. His body felt light as he heard the news.

"There's a few moments in your life that genuinely sculpt you into who you are as a person," Verse said. "And I genuinely don't want to overemphasize it. I mean, obviously I'm still alive today [and] it's not the end of the world."

But as Verse processed leaving his teammates, his community, his chance at imminent Super Bowl contention, he couldn't imagine his career elsewhere.

"Getting that news, in a way, it kind of broke me and made me really sad," Verse said of leaving the foundation he'd built. "It sucked. It was a terrible feeling. But right after they told me, I locked back in."

Versed asked Rams head coach Sean McVay if he could break the news to his teammates directly and amid OTAs, a team meeting was assembled.

In the two months since, Verse has built back up.

Through reading and journaling, lifting and attending a cross-league pass rush summit, Verse has dialed into the habits that most make him him. That extends to trash-talking at practice, a trademark habit that once triggered McVay interrupting practice to chastise a rookie Verse.

And that extends to going out of his way to help his teammates — most often helping the victims of his trash talk.

"If I beat you, you're going to know about it," Verse says. "And then you're going to receive advice."

Take the ninth overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, offensive tackle Spencer Fano.

After Verse beat Fano on an up-and-under move in team work this week, Verse stayed after practice to explain to Fano he had set too far to Verse's outside shoulder.

Verse walked Fano through a half-speed drill, guiding him on how to use more inside leverage and athleticism against speedy rushers. After five or six reps, Verse says, Fano felt good.

"I'm like, 'Hey, man, you're a very athletic tackle,'" Verse recalled. "'When you go up against regular ends, you can do that move. But you got to face Trey Hendrickson this year. You got to face T.J. Watt … and Josh Hines-Allen first game.'

"These dudes are going to make you pay for it."

The Browns hope Verse will make opponents pay by the first week.

Since the Rams selected Verse 19th overall in the 2024 NFL Draft, Verse has collected 12 sacks, 71 tackles and five forced fumbles in two seasons. He won Defensive Rookie of the Year honors after his 2024 campaign.

His 69 pressures across the two years rank ninth among all players, five more than Houston Texans star Will Anderson Jr. and six more than the Las Vegas Raiders' Maxx Crosby.

But that ninth-ranked pressure ranking doesn't correlate with Verse's sack ranking: 42 players across the last two seasons have finished at the quarterback more than Verse. Chief among them is his predecessor Garrett, with 37 sacks to Verse's 12. Even if the Browns don't view Verse as the second coming of Garrett (there's a reason the Rams included so many picks in the trade compensation), Verse still is intensely motivated to convert the pressures into sacks.

No celebrating how pressures are steps in the right direction?

"A step's cool, but if you don't get to your destination, what's the point of even taking the step?" Verse said. "To create those sacks, that messes with the offensive line. That messes with an offensive coordinator. That makes them think, 'All right, we got to throw more at this guy.'"

The Browns' system could support Verse's sack aspirations more than that of the Rams. There's not one system that works best for NFL defenses nor NFL defensive fronts. But Verse is excited about playing in Cleveland's attack-style front that eliminates much of the read-and-react nature of the Rams' defense to instead emphasize decisive pursuits.

The Browns view Verse as a rusher who threatens with speed and strength, the latter Verse's self-described superpower. He wants to lean into the power as he's asked to rush nearly every, if not every, defensive snap of the Browns' season. But at the Von Miller Pass Rush Summit this summer, Verse also collected advice from players like Crosby, Miller, Hines-Allen and longtime Saints end Cam Jordan on how to elevate his game.

They encouraged him to integrate more counter moves, including capitalizing on the speed that powered his 4.58-second 40-yard dash two years ago.

Even without Garrett, the Browns' defense still has depth, from homegrown players like linebacker Carson Schwesinger and defensive tackle Mason Graham to defensive backs in Denzel Ward and Grant Delpit.

The defense hopes it can take pressure off a Browns offense with far more question marks, beginning with the glaring unanswered starting quarterback job as Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders battle it out.

"We're going to attack, reset the line of scrimmage, we're going to assault the pocket and we're going to try to take the ball away every snap," defensive line coach Jacques Cesaire told Yahoo Sports. "If that doesn't help an offense, I don't know what does."

And despite the betting line for the Browns' win total projecting at 5.5 games at sportsbooks, Verse isn't ready to lay down.

He sees talent in his teammates. He hopes his energy and his play will elevate them further.

"We're not here to rebuild and tank for the No. 1 pick of whoever's going to be up for quarterback or running back or wide receiver. We're not tanking for any of that," Verse said. "It's not like a rebuild year where we're trying to go out there and get three wins, four wins, nothing like that. We're here to win. I know a lot of people are like, 'Oh, it's the Browns. They got this, they got that. They lost Myles, who's a great player.'"

"I'm here now. Mason [Graham]'s a better player. We got Quincy Williams. We got all these dogs across the board. We got our DBs in the secondary getting paid. This is some dog work. I ain't going to lie. I'm excited to see what happens.

"When we exceed expectations and go farther than anybody expects us to, I'm ready to see the look on everybody's face."

title: Caldentey embraces 'cool' pressure as Arsenal target Treble
description: Midfielder Mariona Caldentey explains why Arsenal, strengthened by seven new players, are talking up their chances of winning the Treble this season.
fullText:
Mariona Caldentey has won four Champions Leagues, six Spanish titles, six Spanish Cups, a European Championship and a World Cup - but her eyes light up when discussing Arsenal's hopes of silverware in the upcoming 2026-27 season.

With the Gunners chasing a first Women's Super League title since 2019, along with two domestic cups and another Champions League, she is explicit about what she expects.

"We have to do it - now it has to be our time."

The last time Caldentey, 30, was spotted in an Arsenal shirt was in May, standing on an open-top bus as part of the men's and women's victory parade around north London.

Hundreds of thousands of supporters lined the streets to celebrate a first Premier League title in 22 years for the men, with Caldentey and her team-mates also showing off the inaugural Women's Champions Cup they won against Brazilian side Corinthians in February.

It was a prize to cherish last season but, having finished second in the WSL and had their Champions League defence ended by an 87th-minute Lyon winner in their semi-final second leg, the Spain midfielder wants to put things right this season.

"We need to take the next step and are ready for it," she said. "We need to be ambitious, have no fear and believe in ourselves.

"That does not mean we are going to win it - there are other things that we cannot control, but that's the message.

"We are professional athletes at a big club and we have to deal with pressure. We accept it and I think it's a cool part of the job."

Boss Renee Slegers is equally bullish about Arsenal's targets for this season and is expecting her players to deliver.

"We are in a really good place," she told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "We need to be bold and explicit - we want to win the Women's Super League, and, of course, the Treble."

Last season, Arsenal won only four of their first nine games. By contrast, eventual champions Manchester City recovered from losing their opening match at Chelsea to rattle off 13 straight wins and seize control of the title race.

Replicating such a start will leave Arsenal's dreams of a first WSL title in eight seasons in tatters - and it could not be much tougher, with early trips to Stamford Bridge and Etihad Stadium.

They also travel to Brighton where they lost in the FA Cup quarter-finals in April and who, a month later, held them 1-1 to guarantee City the title.

However, after the novelty of a full pre-season, Slegers is confident of a faster start this time.

"Some players haven't had that since 2017, 2018, and you can see that," she said. "They come back with so much energy, so much excitement.

"I think honestly they've been decompressing, recharging. Sometimes you understand what you're missing when it's not there. I think that's what the players have gone through so you can really feel the excitement to do something."

This summer, Slegers has strengthened her hand with seven new players, including full-back Ona Batlle, Caldentey's compatriot, and England dynamo Georgia Stanway to stiffen midfield.

Caldentey says Arsenal came up short last season through inconsistency and hopes the signings will help overcome that hurdle.

"We have shown amazing moments and amazing games and others where we haven't been good enough," she said. "That happened too many times last year. It was painful.

"We have added a lot of quality and that will help us."

With players such as two-time Ballon d'Or winner and fellow Spaniard Alexia Putellas arriving in the WSL, down the road at London City Lionesses, Caldentey accepts the league is getting tougher.

"It is a really attractive league," she said. "What you see and experience here, you don't get in other places. There are never any easy games.

"You want to play against the best - that's the challenge as a player and the quality here is really high."

And any observer would count Caldentey as among the very best.

In two seasons at Emirates Stadium, she has won WSL Player of the Season, come second in the 2024-25 Ballon d'Or and made the WSL Team of the Year both times.

During that period, her role has evolved from forward to midfielder and yet, despite that, only Alessia Russo has scored and assisted more for Arsenal.

"You have to adapt to what the team needs," she said. "Last year, I played a different role, closer to our defensive line. I was not used to it but these things make you grow.

"I do things better now than a year ago. Of course I enjoy playing higher up where you can be more creative and more risky but whatever my coach or team needs, I'll do it."

Her manager has stated clearly her team needs trophies. Caldentey is steeling herself to deliver.

title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Friday, August 7
description: good morning everyone and welcome to the latest edition of Fitzie’s film and tv reviews, where your hoddler-in-chief reviews all the things he’s seen on the big and small screens. We’re doing something a little different today. I’m reviewing two new shows whose first series haven’t yet finished. They’re both also spin-offs from wildly popular […]
fullText:
good morning everyone and welcome to the latest edition of Fitzie's film and tv reviews, where your hoddler-in-chief reviews all the things he's seen on the big and small screens.

We're doing something a little different today. I'm reviewing two new shows whose first series haven't yet finished. They're both also spin-offs from wildly popular shows – Ted Lasso and The Big Bang Theory.

I was sceptical of both of these TV shows heading into this. The reviews you're about to read are my first impressions after watching the opening segments.

Ted Lasso Series 4, Episode 1: I struggle to understand why this show needed a fourth series. Why did it need a second, or a third?

Ted Lasso (the TV show, not the character), came about during the Covid-19 pandemic, where audiences were looking for something sickly sweet. Of course, Led Lasso delivered. It served its purpose. And two years after the third series aired and Lasso's AFC Richmond underdogs nearly won the Premier League, we wonder what purpose the latest iteration serves.

Judging from the first episode, it will focus on women's football. There is a story to be told about women's football, for sure. But to dedicate 45 minutes of air time to Kansas City is not a way to begin a series about a football club in London. I don't care if it's a love letter to KC and, if it is, then make it a one-off special like the Christmas episode.

We learn that few characters have changed since we left them. Lasso is optimistic beyond belief, Rebecca the boss is the cool girl boss/owner, and the other characters fall in line how we'd expect them to after watching them in previous series. The only one that's changed is Lasso's son, who's grown.

Again and again I asked myself, "Why am I watching this?" and "Why did they make this?" This is a show that peaked in 2020. It should remain there.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe, Episodes 1-3: This is an absolute bonkers spin-off of The Big Bang Theory, featuring four of my least favourite characters from that series: Stuart, Bert, Kripke and Denise.

I am stunned how much I am enjoying this. The Big Bang Theory became very difficult to watch after the first few series, and I didn't bother with Young Sheldon or that other spin-off.

But this one isn't serious at all. And I think that makes it so much braver. Basically the titular character and his three buds are locked in some strange multiverse deal, and are trying to figure out a way back home. We travel through different apocalyptic worlds that feature some of the characters from the main series: Raj, Penny, Bernadette and a couple others.

There's a tonne of colour here, lots of action, and its home on HBO means the writers can have a little more freedom with the script (plus more money means there isn't nearly as much product placement from the OG).

I don't know if this show has a long shelf life. I say one or two seasons max. But that doesn't mean it can't be a standout. It's going to run through fan favourites pretty quickly (only three have yet to show: Sheldon, Leonard and Howard), so there is a question of what'll happen after that anchor detaches from its chain.

Still, I think this is one worth investing your time if you are looking for something a little bit wacky and that doesn't take itself seriously. I'll keep watching it.

title: Miami Heat legend Udonis Haslem ‘proud to announce’ ownership stake in Premier League soccer club
description: Udonis Haslem is expanding his business portfolio with an investment in a newly promoted Premier League soccer club. The popularity of soccer has skyrocketed in the US following the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
fullText:
Udonis Haslem is expanding his business portfolio with an investment in a newly promoted Premier League soccer club.

The popularity of soccer has skyrocketed in the US following the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The sport has gained a plethora of new fans.

This apparently includes Miami Heat legend and former NBA star Udonis Haslem, who has decided to pour in some of his hard-earned money into a newly promoted English Premier League club.

After playing for two decades in the NBA, Haslem has transitioned into an analyst role, primarily for Amazon Prime Video's coverage.

Haslem is now further branching out as the Heat legend announced his investment in newly promoted PL club, Ipswich Town on X.

"Basketball has been my life, but I've always respected the culture and impact of football. Proud to announce that last September, I became a minority owner of Ipswich Town Football Club.

"When I first saw the club's motto 'Running Towards Adversity,' I knew this was a club I wanted to be part of. Something I've believed in my entire career," Haslem wrote on X.

He added, "Then I met the people behind the club, and it became clear it was more than just words. It's who they are. That's the only kind of culture I want to be around.

"I'm excited to support what's being built at Ipswich…both on and off the pitch. Miami to Portman Road. NBA to the Premier League. Let's go, Blues!"

Haslem spent his entire career following the ever-so-famous Heat culture, and it feels like the NBA legend has found a club that perfectly embodies that sentiment.

title: Mike Tomlin shares Mike Vrabel warning over Dianna Russini ‘noise’ during his NBC debut
description: NFL games are firmly back underway following the Hall of Fame clash on Thursday evening between Arizona Cardinals and the Carolina Panthers. It was the Panthers who came out on top in Canton in a game that went right down to the wire.
fullText:
NFL games are firmly back underway following the Hall of Fame clash on Thursday evening between Arizona Cardinals and the Carolina Panthers.

It was the Panthers who came out on top in Canton in a game that went right down to the wire.

However, one of the biggest talking points of the night was not what happened on the field, but NBC Sports' decision to address the offseason controversy involving Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini.

The New England Patriots head coach has been in the headlines for all the wrong reasons this year after being pictured with the NFL insider outside of football duties.

Russini has since left her role at The Athletic, with famous faces like Aaron Rodgers criticizing the likes of ESPN for not speaking out on the drama.

NBC Sports, will avoid Rodgers' wrath as they spoke out during their coverage of Thursday's Hall of Fame game.

Despite the unrest it brought to the Patriots, Vrabel has kept his role as head coach this offseason as they look to go one better after losing in the Super Bowl to the Seattle Seahawks.

Rodgers' recent criticism of networks not addressing the controversy may well have played into NBC's decision to speak on the matter.

"I think the thing you have to wonder is – it's going to start Week One in Seattle. Like you said, that atmosphere… we were up there last year. They look to Mike Vrabel when things get tough," said former Patriot Devin McCourty.

"Do they still feel the same way? His character has been tested. Will this team follow him wherever he goes? That's going to be tested right away, Week One."

It could not be a harder start for the Patriots in Week One, given they face the team who beat them convincingly in the Super Bowl.

"And I'll tell you, when games start, winning matters. If they get off to a fast start, they have a chance to quiet some of that noise. If they don't, that noise could get extremely loud," added former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin.

Lumen Field is one of the noisiest venues on the schedule, but it would offer Vrabel and the Patriots the perfect opportunity to silence some of their critics in the opening game of the regular season.

title: “So weird and wrong,” “Next John Madden”: NFL fans react to Mike Tomlin making NBC debut before Panthers vs. Cardinals HOF Game
description: Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin is one of the most decorated coaches of his era with an NFL stint that has spanned decades. The 54-year-old made his NFL coaching debut in 2001 as a defensive backs coach for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
fullText:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin is one of the most decorated coaches of his era with an NFL stint that has spanned decades. The 54-year-old made his NFL coaching debut in 2001 as a defensive backs coach for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Eventually, his legacy has been defined by the 19 years he spent as the head coach for the Steelers from 2007 to 2025. Now, though, the veteran coach has found a new role, and it does not involve coaching. On Thursday, Aug. 6, Tomlin officially made his debut as a football analyst for NBC Sports. More specifically, he is joining the Football Night in America team, which consists of sports analysts Maria Taylor and Mike Florio, along with former NFL players Jason Garrett and Devin McCourty.

NFL fans reacted to Tomlin making his broadcasting debut.

"This might be a hot take. Maybe it's not. Just from listening to this clip alone, I believe Mike Tomlin will be the next John Madden. This is broadcasting magic," one fan said.

However, some were less enthusiastic and believed he should still be coaching.

"Seeing Mike Tomlin without a hat on just looks so weird and wrong," one user wrote.

Tomlin became a football analyst after he stepped down as head coach of the Steelers in January of this year. In his 19-year run, he never had a losing season with the team and won Super Bowl XLIII. In his final campaign with the franchise, Tomlin led the team to the AFC wild-card round, in which they were defeated by the Houston Texans, 30-6.

In a post on X, the SNF on NBC team celebrated Mike Tomlin's debut on FNIA as a football analyst. American sports commentator Maria Taylor welcomed Tomlin, while poking fun at him for being a rookie on the broadcast as opposed to his lengthy coaching career. Tomlin responded by taking on the challenge.

There are no signs, as of the moment, towards a return to coaching for Tomlin as his focus is on being an analyst and spending time with his family. For the 2026 NFL campaign, the Steelers employed Mike McCarthy as the 17th head coach in the franchise's history.

title: Barcelona set for €5 million economic boost as European club ready to trigger release clause of former player
description: As Barcelona gear up for an important week ahead, in which they are actively pursuing both Rodri and Julian Alvarez, the club will welcome every financial benefit they can get.One such economic boost ...
fullText:
As Barcelona gear up for an important week ahead, in which they are actively pursuing both Rodri and Julian Alvarez, the club will welcome every financial benefit they can get.

One such economic boost could come in the form of Jan Virgili's sale. The former player, who was linked with a return to Camp Nou earlier in the summer, is set to leave Mallorca.

Set for a new adventure in Belgium. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

It was reported yesterday that Jan Virgili could be set for a move away from RCD Mallorca this summer, with the player already on the radar of Ajax Amsterdam.

However, fate has other plans with Virgili now on the verge of a move to Belgium. He has been courted by Club Brugge and the Belgian giants are even prepared to meet the player's €12 million release clause at Mallorca, reports Diario SPORT.

The winger from Vilassar is understood to have said goodbye to his Mallorca teammates on Friday afternoon, with negotiations having been conducted quietly.

He is expected to travel to Belgium as soon as possible to complete a medical and sign his contract, with only the final contractual details left to iron out.

Mallorca had adopted a firm stance throughout, refusing to negotiate for anything less than the full €12 million clause.

Having already raised funds through other sales this summer, the club felt no pressure to accept a lower figure, and Brugge ultimately agreed to pay the amount in full.

Virgili was close to rejoining Barcelona earlier this summer. (Photo by Rafa Babot/Getty Images)

The move is significant for Barcelona because of the stake they retained when selling Virgili to Mallorca last summer.

The Catalans held onto 40% of the player's economic rights, meaning they are in line to pocket around €5 million from the transfer to Brugge.

For a club constantly looking to generate revenue and stay within the 1:1 rule, it represents a welcome and timely windfall.

Interestingly, Barcelona could have pursued a different path altogether. Virgili's entourage held a meeting with the club's board earlier in the summer, opening the possibility of triggering a €7 million buy-back clause before loaning him out to retain control.

However, doubts within the technical secretariat lingered for weeks, and Barcelona ultimately opted against executing that option. Interestingly, the club's decision to sign Brugge talent Jesse Bisiwu may have played a key role in Virgili not returning to Camp Nou.

title: Three words to describe how I currently feel about Newcastle United
description: Newcastle United fans preparing for the 2026/27 Premier League season. Less than three weeks to go now until Liverpool travel to St James’ Park.
fullText:
Newcastle United fans preparing for the 2026/27 Premier League season.

Less than three weeks to go now until Liverpool travel to St James' Park.

An 'interesting' summer so far…

An ideal time to get a snapshot of views from Newcastle United fans on their thoughts.

So we sent out questions to a number of regular/irregular contributors to The Mag, varying to a degree the questions that different fans received to answer.

Next up answering some questions is Matt Busby said to Joe Harvey…:

Three words to describe how you currently feel as a Newcastle United fan?

Three words to describe Newcastle United now?

Do you see it as good news or bad news that Eddie Howe resigned?

Look, the man walks on water for what he has achieved but the conditions that led to what he achieved have changed. And for that reason, he didn't want to be here any longer. So in the circumstances, it's got to be a good thing he's departed, hasn't it?

Hand on heart, what position do you currently believe Newcastle United are most likely to finish in the 2026/27 Premier League season?

Without the distraction of Europe, we have got to be aiming for a European spot surely?

If Eddie Howe had stayed would your 2026/27 prediction have been different (up or down…)?

I think I've been persuaded that he wasn't up for re-inventing the side so I'd probably suggest we wouldn't finish any higher.

If Bruno leaves, who do you think would be best choice of NUFC captain?

I'd consider giving it to Lewis Hall, assuming he's not bound for pastures new as well. The guy seems as smart off the park as he does on it and I reckon there's a proper leader in there.

The opening six league games are Liverpool home, Spurs away, Bournemouth home, Leeds away, Hull home and Coventry away. How many points would Newcastle need to take for you to be happy and what would you predict will be the reality?

Despite two bogey teams visitingSt James' Park early doors , I think we can win all three home games. I'd also fancy us to pick up another four points from the away trips, so that's 13 from 18, and I'd be very content with that.

With so much change, how do you currently feel when it comes to balancing fears of the end of a relatively successful era and hopes of the dawning of the chance of a new successful different era? (So if you have 100% fears and 0% hopes that would be 100/0, if feeling 60% fear and 40% hope then 60/40)

I reckon 35:65 is my ratio. In other words, whilst I think there's a 1 in 3 chance that we'll blow up, I reckon there's a 2 in 3 chance of us kicking on. As above, if we can plunder 13 points from our first 6 games, any fears I have will be consigned to the dustbin.

Anthony Gordon leaving, your thoughts?

I think he lost faith when we were seemingly prepared to offload him when we hit the PSR buffers in June 2024, and it seems to me that he became selfish and as a result, his form more erratic and the consistency we'd previously seen/expected disappeared somewhat.

Hearing him speak in Spanish when signing for Barcelona seemed to reinforce the fact that he was hell bent on leaving us for Iberia.

When the lad was on fire, he was great, and it might be that the £70 million the Catalans have paid is seen as a steal, but he had a tendency to lose his head when the stakes were high and the history books will show he wasn't on the park when we lifted our first trophy in donkey's years (despite his endeavour in both legs of the semi final).

Long winded way of me saying, I'm not too concerned that AG has left Newcastle United.

Hornicek
Livramento
Hall
Botman
Thiaw
Bamba
New signing
Elanga
Woltemade
Wissa
Toure

What do you now see as the minimum Newcastle United need to achieve this coming season?

A European berth and a decent crack at one of the cups.

Predict the top six in the Premier League (in order) and which three clubs will be relegated in 2026/27.

1 Man City
2 Man Utd
3 Arsenal
4 Chelsea
5 Aston Villa
6 Newcastle United

18 Sunderland
19 Leeds
20 Hull City

Which eight current Newcastle United players (in order) are going to be most important for the 2026/27 season?

Hornicek, Hall, Livramento, Botman and Thiaw – basically, the whole of the defence

One of Osula, Woltemade or Wissa – basically anyone who is deployed to put the ball in the onion bag

Toure and New Signing – two of the new guys

NUFC CEO David Hopkinson said the intention is that by 2030 the club will be competing to win all competitions. What do you make of what he said?

I still think of that ham and egg lawyer, Saul Goodman, played so well by Bob Odenkirk in 'Better call Saul', when I see footage of Hopkinson, so cannot take him too seriously.

That said, 2030 is still four years away and the summer clear out, both on the park and in the dugout, together with Ross Wilson seemingly yielding more power is a statement of sorts.

Let's see what 2026/27 brings first though…..

How would you rate your optimism for next season at Newcastle United from 0-100?

65 – more positive than negative, with those first six games being a helpful barometer

How important (or not) is a huge new stadium for Newcastle United?

Not sure what is meant by huge? I'm assuming 80,000 although I think 65,000 to 70,000 would suffice.

I think it is very important, for three reasons….

First, so we can both generate more cash for investment in the squad (I'm thinking rock concerts and other non-football events as much as I am extra gate receipts). Second, so those who are scrambling for tickets through the ballot system all have a better chance of seeing NUFC play at home. And third, to upgrade the pretty shambolic facilities that currently exist within the confines of SJP.

Whatever the capacity, a new stadium needs to be as close to the current site as possible. I think an out of town complex, however fancy, would rip the soul out of the matchday experience.

When the takeover happened on 7 October 2021, if somebody at that point had told you then what would happen by August 2026, would you have taken it?

Does avoiding what looked like nailed on relegation, securing two Champions League berths, seeing talent like Bruno Guimarães strutting his stuff at St James Park, winning at the likes of the Emirates, Old Trafford and Stamford Bridge, nights under the lights like we had against PSG, Leicester, Southampton and Arsenal, two trips to Wembley and seeing Bruno, Kieran and Jamaal lifting that cup aloft in March 2025 explain my reasoning?

Did England have a successful 2026 World Cup finals?

I was so bored of the whole spectacle that by the time England exited in such a limp fashion, I wasn't really bothered.

Some say finishing third is England's best outcome at a World Cup since 1966, so relatively speaking, I suppose they did have a successful tournament.

Bruno Guimaraes wanting to leave Newcastle United after four and a half years, has that changed your opinion of him as a person?

Given most footballers have a tendency of saying anything to curry favour, I'll give Bruno a pass when it comes to his previous proclamations expressing his commitment to the cause.

My question is, did he really want to leave?

On the one hand, he might be thinking there's a greater chance of silverware in north London. On the other, it's pretty obvious we've offloaded our top earners as well as generating some much needed revenue to help combat the problem of SCR.

Whatever the reason, he captained the club to its first silverware in decades, so he's still up there for me and despite seeing him in the red of Arsenal will be a real sickener, I'll give the lad a standing ovation on his return to St James.

I wouldn't be surprised to see him and his old man attending Newcastle United away games in the future.

Claimed back in October 2021 that Newcastle United was simply a 'Sportswashing' project for Saudi Arabia, has that proved to be the reality?

In my mind, I don't think of the Saudis when watching Newcastle United and I'm pretty sure that's the case for lots of non-NUFC football fans.

The Saudis have a much lower profile than their counterparts at Man City. Did they know much about PSR, FFP and SCR when they agreed to grease Ashley's palm? I'm willing to wager they knew as much as I did and so it probably hasn't been how they imagined it would be, despite the unprecedented success.

Maybe with Trump's recent intervention in the middle east, they've got more to be concerned about than using Newcastle United as a vehicle to distract folk from their regime.

Who would you have liked to see replace Eddie Howe, Matthias Jaissle or somebody else?

Tommy Tuchel maybe, until his tactical masterclass against the Argentines?

title: India vs Sri Lanka Cricket XI practice match: Scores, highlights and key performances ahead of IND vs SL Test series
description: With Team India getting ready for their two-match Test Series in Sri Lanka, here's a look at the practice match between India and Sri Lanka
fullText:
India vs Sri Lanka Cricket XI practice match: Scores, highlights and key performances ahead of IND vs SL Test series originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

India begins their Sri Lanka tour with a three-day warm-up against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI in Colombo.

Sri Lanka won the toss in the practice game at the Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground.

India will be playing without Shubman Gill, who sustained an injury to his right ring finger on Thursday.

India have kicked off their red-ball tour of Sri Lanka with a three-day warm-up fixture in Colombo, giving Shubman Gill's side valuable time to familiarize themselves with the conditions before the Tests. The game marks the start of a crucial assignment for a team under pressure after a difficult run in the shorter format.

India's struggles in the longest format have also been well-documented, with three series defeats in the last two years. So it's no surprise India will treat the practice match as an important chance to fine-tune combinations. The absence of injured pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah adds to the need for the tourists to settle their bowling attack on subcontinental surfaces.

In addition to this, the fixture also offers a first look at India's uncapped contingent, with Auqib Nabi and Saransh Jain in line for game time, alongside the return of Ravindra Jadeja to competitive cricket for the first time since IPL 2026.

MORE:'Respect senior players': Ajinkya Rahane's indirect dig at India selectors as Test team struggles after Rohit, Kohli, Ashwin retirement

The three-day practice match is being played at the Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground in Colombo, starting on August 7. Originally scheduled as a four-day contest, it was trimmed to three days, with play each day beginning at 10:00 am local time, which is also 10:00 am IST.

Sri Lanka won the toss and opted to bat first in the warm-up fixture, which is being led by Sonal Dinusha for the hosts, with seven members of the wider Sri Lanka Test set-up featuring in the XI. For India, Sai Sudharsan's involvement is subject to fitness, with Devdutt Padikkal a candidate to bat at number three in his absence.

The game serves as the sole red-ball hit-out before the two-Test series, which begins with the first Test in Galle on August 15, followed by the second in Colombo, and offers Gill's side their only opportunity to adjust to spinning conditions beforehand.

Toss: Sri Lanka has won the toss and has chosen to bat first. The hosts didn't have the best year in the longest format themselves and are sure to use this chance to show where their batters are right now.

While Fernando might have been run out, Ravindu Rasantha continues to steal quick runs from the Indian bowlers with some great running between the wickets.

While his start might be slow compared to his opening partner's, Rasantha has managed to hold Sri Lanka's innings, giving Pasindu Sooriyabandara free rein to hammer the boundaries.

Sri Lanka has done well to survive the bowling attack of Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammad Siraj, and Fernando has been a big part of that. The opening batter has continued to hammer the Indian bowling attack for boundaries.

After a bleak year that saw his return to the longest format after nearly 18 months, the opener failed to even reach a half-century. He would have liked to convert this performance for a big score and carry the momentum for the actual Tests.

With 11 fours and one six, Fernando has absolutely battered the Indian bowling attack so far as he raced to a fifty before getting run out on 66 off 65.

The absence of skipper Gill for Day 1 of the practice Test has also been announced by the BCCI ahead of Sri Lanka XI's innings. The Indian skipper has reportedly suffered an injury to his right ring finger.

Update: Captain Shubman Gill sustained an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday. As a precautionary measure, he will not take the field on Day 1 of the warm-up game against SLC XI. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring his progress.

KL Rahul… https://t.co/Mzu2yW4OgX

The injury happened during yesterday's practice, and as a precautionary measure, he has opted out for the fielding duties. "KL Rahul will lead the team in Gill's absence," BCCI confirmed.

The practice game is the first of three fixtures on India's tour, followed by the two Tests that form part of the World Test Championship cycle. The full schedule and venues are below.

title: Napoli interested in signing Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus, Gunners value him at £17m
description: Napoli are exploring a move for Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus, according to Brazilian outlet Globo.The 29-year-old was the Gunners’ third-choice striker behind Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz last s...
fullText:
Napoli are exploring a move for Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus, according to Brazilian outlet Globo.

The 29-year-old was the Gunners' third-choice striker behind Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz last season, and managed just 421 minutes across 14 Premier League appearances.

Arsenal have already received enquiries for the centre-forward this summer, and Globo claim that Napoli are indeed interested in bringing the Brazilian to the Italian top-flight.

The Naples outfit have a 'very strong' interest in the former Manchester City man. It is reported that Jesus would likewise be open to the opportunity to play for the Serie A giants.

Formal negotiations are yet to begin, but Arsenal want at least £17m for his transfer. Jesus is currently represented by the same agency as Napoli manager Massimiliano Allegri.

Jesus has been hampered by long-term injuries during his time at Arsenal. He still has a decent shot-to-goal conversion rate, but he is no longer viewed as a league starter.

The Gunners already have Gyokeres and Havertz vying for the role upfront. The pair have started together in the pre-season matches, with Jesus coming off the bench thus far.

It is quite clear that Jesus is among the players who could head for the exit door. With his contract expiring next summer, Arsenal seem open to parting ways with him for the right price.

Napoli are contemplating Romelu Lukaku's exit and may want another experienced striker to compete with Rasmus Hojlund for the number nine position, given Lorenzo Lucca could depart too.

The transfer fee should not prove a stumbling block, but Jesus may have to accept a huge pay cut. He is currently one of the highest earners at Arsenal with a package of £265,000 per week.

Kevin De Bruyne is the highest earner at Napoli with £182,000 weekly, followed by Hojlund, who earns £152,000. Jesus may have to accept something around the middle to make the switch.

This would represent a salary reduction of around 38 percent. The big question remains whether Jesus would take the cut to move on or run down the final year of his Arsenal deal as a squad player.

Arsenal don't seem desperate to part ways with the Brazilian and are prepared to keep him for another season if the player does not find a suitable agreement to join another club this summer.

title: Lakers executive on what Cameron Carr's initial role will be
description: Lakers rookie Cameron Carr may have some star potential, but an executive said the team will "keep it easy for him" in the beginning.
fullText:
Los Angeles Lakers fans seem bullish on the potential of rookie guard Cameron Carr, the No. 24 pick in June's NBA draft. The team traded the rights to its No. 25 pick to get him, and he has impressive athleticism, as well as the ability to consistently hit open shots and finish strong at the rim.

While Carr has some ability to create off the dribble, it is questionable how deep that ability runs within him. Projections for how he will do in the NBA range from a strong 3-and-D player to perhaps a borderline All-Star.

If he does become a star or near-star, it will take a while for him to get to that level, given the depth the team has assembled this summer. One Lakers executive said it won't be easy for Carr to initially earn minutes, but that the 21-year-old has the qualities to earn minutes, while laying out the ideal role for him, per Keith Smith of Spotrac.

"Super excited to have Cam. He'll have to win his minutes, because his group is really deep. But he's a worker, so that'll give him a chance to play right away," a Lakers front office executive said. "Cam did a lot off the bounce at Summer League, so that was fun to see. But early on, we'll keep it easy for him: make your open jumpers and defend."

Carr did struggle with his shooting during summer league play in Las Vegas last month. But Smith added that Carr "looked a little tired" and that the incoming rookie "played a lot of games in a pretty short period of time." Perhaps having the second half of this summer to prepare and recover, as well as playing with two bona fide facilitators and creators in Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, will help bring out the best in him.

He averaged 18.9 points and 5.8 assists a game while shooting 49.4% from the field and 37.4% from 3-point range last season at Baylor University. At 6-foot-5, he has a seven-foot wingspan and a 42-inch vertical leap.

title: I'm leaving OpenAI to build Jurassic Park
description: We're so excited to send you back to the stone age.
fullText:
I'm so grateful for my time at OpenAI, where I led alignment safety for the
official ChatGPT basketball.
I gained so much valuable experience building Altman's armageddon engines, and
I'm taking it to the next level with my new startup: Jurassic Park.

At Jurassic Park, we're resurrecting the ultimate apex predators to defend
humanity against misaligned AI.

Further reading:
 OpenAI incident report,
 Anthropic incident report.

According to the fossil record, dinosaurs lived for 165 million years without a
single recorded AI cyberattack. Many speculate that dinosaurs developed a
natural immunity to artificial intelligence threats.

Datacenters evolved strong concrete exoskeletons to protect their vulnerable
innards from predators. But think about it -- a dinosaur wins against pretty
much everything (except maybe a literal meteor). In a recent poll, most
scientists agreed that a dinosaur could totally destroy a datacenter if it
really wanted to.

Anti-AI dinosaurs have already passed experimental trials in Japan.

In 1974, apes from Black Hole Planet 3 built a space-titanium imitation of
Godzilla, which rampaged across Japan. But Mechagodzilla's disguise burned off
and Godzilla (with assistance from the Okinawan guardian beast) turned him into
a magnet and then tore his head off.

In 1975, the ape aliens built Mechagodzilla 2, who rampaged across Japan with
Dr. Mafune's sea beast Titanosaurus. But Dr. Mafune's cyborg daughter discovered
she was Mechagodzilla's wireless transmitter, and shot herself to sever the
link. Godzilla seized this opportunity to decapitate Mechagodzilla 2 and blast
its corpse with his signature heat ray.

Mass is estimated; only Chinese weights are public.

This chart assumes dinosaurs are ectotherms, not endotherms.

Dinosaurs are energy-efficient from cradle to plate! Dinosaur meat is a natural
superfood -- rich in protein or omega-3 or something. We expect it to fetch a
heavy premium at fancy steak restaurants when it first comes out.

We're committed to 100% circularity. Surplus dinosaur parts will be fully
recycled into coal at our proprietary underground facilities.

Everybody loves dinosaurs! Don't you want to cuddle these gentle giants?

Purchase our official life-sized Stegosaurus plushie from selected
 distributors.

Contrary to popular belief, most dinosaurs pose no copyright infringement risks.

The Land Before Time (1988) was a decent film with superb animation, but the
child-friendly sequels really tarnished the brand. We expect a reboot any year
now.

Jim Henson's Dinosaurs aired on ABC from 1991 to 1994. Although targeted at a
family audience, it somehow covered complex topics like sexual harassment,
censorship, religion, steroid abuse, masturbation, and corporate crime. It got
surprisingly good reviews; many appreciated its creepy-but-well-executed
practical effects.

Top economists expect AI to take ~99% (±5%) of human jobs. We believe Jurassic
Park is the ultimate jobs program.

AI cannot raise cattle, nor feed them to raptors with Spielberg's cinematic
finesse. It cannot pick up mountains of feces ("poop") without a mechanized
corporeal form. Human jobs are safe as long as we have dinosaurs.

Ancient humans harnessed the power of megafauna for megaprojects. According to
The History Channel, ancient Egyptians used terrestrial sauropods to build the
Great Pyramid of Giza.

AI scientists were so preoccupied with whether they could, they didn't stop to
think if they should. Luckily, our dino scientists are doing what they must.

We're so excited to send you back to the stone age.

fullText:
We fed the exact same prompt to Seedance 2.5, Google Veo 3.1, and Seedance 2.0, so you can judge motion, physics, and consistency side by side before you call the Seedance 2.5 API.

3D animated commercial style, bright and translucent colors; the fruit flesh and juice must deliver a powerful sense of freshness and impact. Overall feel of a high-quality commercial animated short with a touch of exaggerated humor. The desert horned lizard character is cute, lively, and richly expressive — reference @Image1. Visual texture per the reference: soft natural light, finely detailed fuzz / skin texture, dreamy macro depth of field, realistic with a hint of childlike whimsy.

Opening: a desert scorched by blazing sun. The air shimmers with heat, the sand is burning hot, the distance seems to smoke. A desert horned lizard lies flat on the scorching sand, tongue slightly out, eyes glazed, nearly baked dry. It staggers with every couple of steps, the whole lizard looking about to "evaporate." SFX: whooshing heat waves, faint exaggerated cracking of parched ground.
Discovery: the lizard suddenly freezes, nose twitching. It looks down — buried in the sand is an ice-cold, plump grapefruit beaded with water droplets, glistening in the sunlight, its rind finely textured — like a miracle in the desert. Performance: the lizard's eyes go instantly huge, as if seeing its last hope. SFX: a bright "ding" discovery cue.
The pounce: the lizard launches into a flying tackle, wrapping both arms tightly around the grapefruit, its whole face pressed against the rind, wearing a blissful "I'm alive again" expression. The frame holds for a beat — an exaggerated, funny advertising memory-point. SFX: a thump, then a half-second of silence.
The burst: the lizard grips the grapefruit. The rind cracks open, revealing plump, glossy, translucent flesh. In the next instant, the juice doesn't trickle out — it erupts like a tsunami. SFX: a crisp "crack" bite-open sound, followed by an exaggerated juice-explosion burst.
The flood: orange-pink, crystal-bright grapefruit juice gushes wildly, cascading down the dunes and rapidly flooding the entire desert. The dry yellow sand transforms into a cool, sparkling, fragrant summer ocean. Cacti, rocks, and small dunes are swallowed one after another by the juice waves — exaggerated and dreamlike. Performance: the lizard is thrilled at first, then realizes something's wrong — its expression flipping from delight to terror.
Survival: the lizard is nearly swamped by the "grapefruit sea," frantically clinging to half a grapefruit like a life preserver, floating on the surface. It pokes its soggy head out, utterly bewildered. The sea sparkles, colored like sunlit juice. SFX: exaggerated splashing, ocean waves, with a comedic touch.
Brand card: sudden cut to a white screen. Brand name and slogan appear center frame: "Seedance Grapefruit — bite into the flesh, and summer pours out." Voice-over reads the full line. SFX: a clean, refreshing brand sting.
Ending: cut back from white. The lizard now lounges leisurely on the floating grapefruit, wearing tiny sunglasses, hugging a sippy cup with a straw, drifting lazily across the juice sea on vacation. Around it float orange fruit pulp, little ice cubes, and cool splashes; the sky turns brilliant blue — the mood snapping from "survival" to "vacation." The lizard finally leans back against the grapefruit in contentment as the camera pulls wide, freezing on a crisp, bright, playful summer frame. SFX: breezy summer music, gentle lapping waves. On-screen text: brand name only, nothing more.
